# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-B: the sahajavimarśa, the prakāśa/vimarśa, kārikās 3–5 — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 700–1400 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fourth vimarśa continued.
Covers: the māyāpade memory; the ābhāsa/anābhāsa order; the yogi's perception and the param-
pramātṛ; the svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya (the general and the particular) and the deśa-kāla avaccheda;
kārikā 3 (naca yuktaṃ smṛterbhede smaryamāṇasya bhāsanam — the memory's non-difference from the
experience); the ekaviṣayatva and the ekapramātṛ; kārikā 4 (naiva hyanubhavo bhāti smṛtau — the
experience does not shine separately in the memory); kārikā 5 (yoginām api bhāsante — the yogins'
cognitions also shine, not known by another); the svasaṃvida (self-cognition) as the jñāna's
characteristic; the grāhyagrāhaka. Max-effort T1.*

---

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-B)

1. **The māyāpade memory.** In the māyā-position the memory-practical-activity is the limitor-form
   contraction (aupādhikarūpasaṃkoca) of the manifestation. The 'tena' (by that) gives the reason
   for the memory's establishment: the naśe/sadbhāve (the destruction has no fault, the being has no
   support) — hence the "not-if" (na cet) fall is fit as a prasaṅga-reversal.
2. **The ābhāsa/anābhāsa order and time.** The krama (order) is the ābhāsānābhāsātmā time; the body's
   per-instant difference bestows the utter time-difference; the body-knower-conceiting ones (whose
   cognitions depend on the external sense-organs) have no fitness to see past/future. But with the
   prasaṃkhyāna (reflection) teaching, the body-conceit is thinned, and the ātyantika-kālabheda
   falls away — the memory of the prior-experienced objects then is.
3. **The yogi's perception and the param-pramātṛ.** The Mālinīvijayavārtika 4.4 (yogam ekatvam
   icchanti) is cited: the yogin's objects are in his own time-less self as "I" or "I-this"; the
   question of the some-only manifestation and prior-time-distinction is answered via the
   svātantrya. The māyā-knower's memory in the puryaṣṭaka/prāṇa/śūnya is only the aupādhika-
   difference.
4. **The smṛti's svarūpa.** The memory is the cognition-particular on the avacchinna-object of the
   past experience — but if the prior manifestation does not open (anunmeṣe) and there is no prior-
   manifestation-rehearsal, it is just a new experience (abhinava eva anubhavaḥ), not memory. The
   'pūrvānubhava' is the distinguishing feature.
5. **The svatantravikalpa and the "father-king" example.** The distracted (vyākṣepa-born) vikalpa,
   even if it flashes the false "father is king," is not memory (no pūrvānubhavollekha). The memory
   requires the ekībhāva with the prior-knowers' cognition-manifestation; otherwise the
   tadānīntana/other-knowers' attachment fails — the smṛtitva is negated in the two examples.
6. **The ghaṭābhāsamātra and the arthitva.** The desire (arthitva) determines the extent of the
   memory: the water-carrying desirer remembers the golden pot only by the wide-bottom-belly-form;
   the scholar remembers only the brāhmaṇa-word's correctness. The svalakṣaṇa-form-ness of the
   general (sāmānya) is spread by the deśa-kāla alone.
7. **The sāmānya/svalakṣaṇa.** The general (sāmānya) is not the Buddhist's svalakṣaṇa-contracted-
   self; the bhāva is vikasitasvabhāva (expanded-own-nature), and the saṃkoca (contraction) is by
   the deśa-kāla manifestation-generals mixed (the ṣaḍrasa-drink analogy). The mutual-avaccheda
   (anyonyāvaccheda) — "sat dravyaṃ, sat guṇa" — with the paryāya (alternation) and the yugapad
   (simultaneity). The niyatiśakti (rule-power) of the Bhagavat governs the ābhāsa-mixing.
8. **The sāmānyatā and the Vākyapadīya.** The 'sāmānya' word is unetymologized (avyutpanna,
   sādhāraṇārtha), not the bhāva-suffix-ending. The Vākyapadīya 3.14/3.9/2.11 are cited (the jāti
   of jātis, the anupravṛttidharma). The svalakṣaṇa = the contracted general (the vyāpakatva/
   nityatva removed by the deśa-kāla); "here-this-is" (atredaṃ sad) — the "sad"-locus.
9. **The pratyakṣīkāra and the Patañjali smṛti.** The present-viśeṣaṇa enters the memory, so the
   remembered appears as if directly perceived (pratyakṣīkāra); Patañjali's "svapno bhāvitaḥ
   smartavyā smṛtiḥ" is cited. The Yogasūtra 1.43 (śabdasaṃketasmṛtipariśuddhau... nirvitarkā) is
   cited; the sahajavimarśa (natural-reflection) is the "sa iti" vimarśa.
10. **Kārikā 3 (naca yuktaṃ smṛterbhede).** The remembered's manifestation is not the now-one but
    the prior-one; in the memory the self-part manifestation is time-unlimited, the object-part
    is the prior-one with the necessary rehearsal. The māyā-pramātṛ's separate-like manifestation
    (māyāśaktyā pṛthagbhūtam iva) is only in the experience-cognition, not in the memory. The
    ekaviṣayatva establishes the ekapramātṛ (the adhikaraṇasiddhānta).
11. **The ekatva and the ekātmā.** The oneness (aikyam), the tracing-form (anusandhānarūpaṃ), the
    freedom (svātantryaṃ) — the self's distinguishing feature. "Eka ātmā" is said with the bhāva-
    suffix (taddharmaprādhānya) like "caitanyam ātmā." The Ārya verse (dharmāntarapratikṣepā-
    pratikṣepau) and the Śivasūtra are cited. "Saḥ" for the hidden-form, "eṣa" for the clear-form —
    the pratyabhijñā (recognition) is indicated.
12. **Kārikā 4 (naiva hyanubhavo bhāti smṛtau).** The experience does not shine separately in the
    memory like the prior object; the "prāg aham anvabhūvam" is the ātmārohaṇa-manifestation. The
    agent-lagging-ness of the experience (kartṛlagnatā) even in the object-lagging-ness
    (karmalagnatāyāṃ); the māyā-pramātṛ's dharmas (sukhitvādayo) are the known-ones, their vedyatā
    is figurative (upacaritā). The pratyagātmatā — the pratyagātma-class is bhedaprāṇa from the
    known-ones; the one self-cognition-knower is "anekakāla" figuratively. The pūrvapakṣa (1.2.6
    smartā draṣṭeva kalpitaḥ) is refuted.
13. **Kārikā 5 (yoginām api bhāsante).** The yogins' cognitions shine, not known by another
    perception, being self-cognition (svasaṃvidaikamānāḥ), even in the known-position. The three-
    fold other-cognition (the "this-one-knows," the "this-is-my-past-experience," the "remembered
    by the other") are all the other-knower-gone perceptions (pramātrantaragatā upalambhāḥ) — the
    dṛśaḥ-plural in the sūtra. But in the memory (prakṛte) there is no such "I-experienced" separate
    manifestation — the memory's experience is asmadartha-śarīrībhūta (our-meaning-bodied).
14. **The jñāna not known by another, the svasaṃvidmātra.** The Buddhist/Sāṅkhya/Kaṇāda/Jaiminīya
    views are each refuted: none can explain the yogin's knowledge of the other's cognition. The
    cognition's characteristic (svabhāva) is the self-cognition-alone-form-ness (svasaṃvinmātrarūpatva),
    the vyāvartaka from the inert (jaḍa). The four-fold niyama: svaiva saṃvit / parāpi saṃvit /
    svasya saṃvideva / asaṃvid api — the caturvidhaniyamaniyantritarūpāvabhāsa. The jñāna's being
    known by another would fail this four-fold rule.

**The crux.** Chunk V2-B develops the smṛti's svarūpa and its ekaviṣayatva with the experience: the
memory manifests the object by the prior-manifestation path (the object-part is the prior one), not
as a separate now-manifestation (which would be a new experience or a creation). The svalakṣaṇa is
the contracted general; the parāmarśa is the prakāśa's own nature (1.5.11). The ekaviṣayatva
establishes the one cognition-tattva (ekapramātṛ), and the cognitions' ekātmatā (one-self-ness) is
the self. The jñāna cannot be known by another cognition (it is svasaṃvidmātra, the four-fold rule),
which grounds both the memory's validity and the yogin's knowledge of the other's cognition.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.2.6 (smartā draṣṭeva kalpitaḥ), 1.3.2 (dṛk svābhāsaiva), 1.4.4/1.4.6,
1.5.2, 1.5.11 (svabhāvam avabhāsasya vimarśam), 1.5.16 (svātantryāmukta), 1.5.21 (kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya),
1.6.3 (tadatatpratibhābhājā), 1.7.1 (yā caiṣā pratibhā), 2.1.4 (kramo bhedāśrayo), 2.3.5/2.3.10; the
Mālinīvijayavārtika 4.4; the Vākyapadīya 2.11/3.9/3.10/3.14; the Yogasūtra 1.42/1.43; the
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 19; the Nareśvaraviveka; the Śvetāśvatara 3.15 and Nṛsiṃhatāpanīya Upaniṣads; the
Nyāyasūtra 1.1.31 (abhyupagamasiddhānta); the Bhaṭṭa (artho na bhāsate); Patañjali. The
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel is the direct anchor.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-C: the grāhyagrāhaka, kārikās 5–8, the smṛtiśaktivismarśa's close — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 1400–2082 (continuous, ending the caturtho vimarśa = smṛtiśaktivimarśaḥ
caturthaḥ ||4||). Base: Torella's ĪPK. Covers: the grāhakagrāhya and the sārūpya; the jñāna not
known by another (the vyāpakānupalabdhi); kārikā 5's conclusion; the yogi's knowledge of the other's
cognition (the three kinds, the aupādhikatva); kārikā 6 (smaryate yaddṛgāsīnme saivam ity api bhedataḥ);
kārikā 7 (yā ca paśyāmyaham imaṃ ghaṭo'yam iti vāvasā); kārikā 8 (tanmayā dṛśyate dṛṣṭo'yaṃ sa ity
āmṛśaty api — grāhyagrāhakatābhinnāv arthau bhātaḥ pramātari); the māyāśakti's non-concealment of the
awareness; the aṇu/paśu; the śūnya-vedaka and the param-Śiva; and the colophon of the fourth vimarśa.
Max-effort T1.*

---

## The tattvam, the sarvajña, the saṃsāri's pitiable state, the anugrahāpaghāta

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-C)

1. **The grāhakagrāhya and the sārūpya.** The object-ness (viṣayitā) of the cognition is its that-
   ākāra-imitation-ness (the sārūpya); but the cognitions cannot have the object-object relation
   among themselves, because their difference is not supreme-real (only the jñeya-part, not the
   bodha-part, can be the object). The two-mirrors analogy is rejected. The inference: no supreme-
   real difference → no object-object relation (vyāpakānupalabdhi). Dharmakīrti's pervader-chain
   investigation is noted as not-made.
2. **The māyā and the bodha's svarūpa.** The māyā does not cover the awareness's own form (like the
   fire's burning-power); the covering is itself the producing of a prior-state-distinct form. In
   the one-ending object-being, the cognition cannot be known by another — the own-form-manifestation
   alone is the viṣayīkṛtatva (the oyster-shell/conch example; the vyāpakānupalabdhi).
3. **The yogi's knowledge of the other's cognition.** The three kinds (this-one-knows; my-past-
   experience-in-the-other-body; the-other's-prior-seen-now-remembered) are all the other-knower-
   gone perceptions (pramātrantaragatā upalambhāḥ). The tattvam = paramātmavedakatva; the sarvajña.
   The oneness (aikyam) with the other would make the yogin a partaker of the other's dharmas — the
   pitiable saṃsāri-state (the saffron-water analogy); but the sukhādi rests only in the grāhya-part
   (not in the pure knower).
4. **The anugrahāpaghāta (favor/harm).** The real-knower (vāstava pramātā), attained by the firm
   determination, does not conceive "I am happy" — hence no favor/harm (Gītā 2.58, 12.15). But in
   the vyutthāna (arising) state, the body-I-being-impression-firmness makes the burning-pain arise
   in the buddhi (the traveler analogy). Those who have loosened the body-I-ness do not get the
   pleasure-pain even in the sandal-touch (the Spandakārikā 8 on the icchā).
5. **The first kind → memory.** The paracittajñāna (knowing the other's cognition) is reduced to
   memory (smṛti) via the asaṃpramoṣa — the jātismara (birth-remembrance); the not-own-experienced
   past-births are new-cognitions from the impression-direct-cognition. The third kind: the pot
   seen by another is remembered by the yogin via the pūrvadṛṣṭatā (prior-seen-ness), not as new —
   the tatpūrvaprakāśa identity. The Manu-and-the-rest's dharma-manifestation is the param-Lord's
   beginningless manifestation made into memory.
6. **The smṛtyanubhava not vedyavedaka.** Even in the memory-experience, there is no known-revealer
   relation: the pure (śuddha) awareness-form (sarvārtharūpatā śuddhir jñānasya), the citiśakti, the
   prabhāsvaram cittaṃ (Yogadarśana). The māyā-power cannot split the awareness (the Spandakārikā 2:
   tasyānāvṛtarūpatvāt); the Nareśvaraviveka; the turya-word with the crow-repetition.
7. **Kārikā 6 (smaryate yaddṛgāsīn me).** The memory's root (maulika) rehearsal is "by me seen" (mayā
   dṛṣṭam) — the Vākyapadīya 3.1.105 (ghaṭajñānam iti jñānaṃ ghaṭajñānavilakṣaṇam). The difference in
   the memory is only guṇa (quality), not grown (aprarūḍha); the root-cognition is augmented
   (upavṛṃhyate), not refuted, by the explanation-cognition.
8. **Kārikā 7 (yā ca paśyāmy aham imaṃ ghaṭo'yam iti vāvasā).** The determination (avasā) "I see this"
   reflects the seeing (darśanam) in the grāhakāṃśa; it thinks (from the impression) and directly-
   cognizes the experience. The "this" (ayam) word rests not on the pot-form alone but on the
   perceptibility-rehearsal — the perceptibility is the I-conceit-object (ahaṃkāragocara), the
   knower-made (pramātṛmaya). The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 15 (idamityasya vicchinnavimarśasya kṛtārthatā)
   is cited; the infinite-regress of the "my-seeing" is noted.
9. **Kārikā 8 (tanmayā dṛśyate dṛṣṭo'yaṃ sa ity āmṛśaty api).** The grāhyagrāhakatābhinnau arthau
   (the two objects — grasped and grasper — non-distinct in their being-ness) shine in the one
   pure-cognition-form knower. The "seen"/"seen-by-me" and "this"/"that" rehearsals mark the
   experience-memory; the "this"-ness-rehearsal makes the grasper "I" and the graspable "this"
   discontinuous (vicchinnaprathau) — but they are tanmayau (made of that), not separate from the
   pure-knower-supreme-object. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 (yadyapyarthasthitiḥ) is the anchor.
10. **The māyāśakti and the viśvātmatā.** The beings are of the paramārthaprakāśa (the conscious-
    only-supreme-object); the māyā-power cannot divide them from the manifestation (else the 
    aprakāśana). The vedyīkaraṇam of the objects is the māyā-fault (3.2.9: bodhānām api kartṛtvajuṣāṃ
    kārmamala); but the bodha's manifestation-form-ness toward all would make everyone all-knowing —
    so the contraction (saṃkoca) is the aṇu-mala (anyastvahaṃbhāvo vedyeṣvapyāṇavo malaḥ). The
    difference-manifestation (bhedena prathā) in the not-all-knowing-ness is thus established.
11. **The paśulakṣaṇa and the aṇutva.** The māyā-knower's pratyagātma-cognition, being the 
    prāṇādisaṃkoca-partaking, is the aṇu (atomic); the Kiraṇa-verse (paśur nityo hy amūrto jño...)
    defines the paśu (bound one). The pure revealer-ness (vedakatā) is distinct from the īśvara's;
    the "iva" (like-the-Lord) is fit because the idam-aham parts in the māyā-knower are distinct
    from the īśvara's form.
12. **The śūnya-vedaka and the param-Śiva.** The breath's revealer is the buddhi, its revealer the
    void (śūnya) — the "śūnyātiśūnya" (the final knower-form) is the vedyarāśi-removed pure-
    consciousness. The verse (tathāhi vedyate yadyat tanmadhye'haṃ na kaścana...) anchors; the
    ākāśasamāpatti (sky-attainment) and the mahāvidehā (great-discarnate). The yogin's direct
    cognition is "I-this" (aham idam), not the separate-known — the construction (vikalpa) gives
    the vedyatā. The vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi.
13. **The upadeśa (teaching).** When the param-Lord teaches "I am your self," he teaches the
    created-many-dharma-face form (atadrūpavyāvṛttyā), not the pure-non-divided cognition directly
    — the "this-Īśvara-my-form-your-self" (the vaidharmya-example with the body's teaching). The
    siddha-pādas verse (atītaḥ panthānaṃ tava sa mahimā vāṅmanasayoḥ...). The ābhāsa (appearance)
    is the param-Lord's own form (tadeva parameśvarasvarūpameva, na adhikam) — 1.5.16.
14. **The grāhyagrāhakayugalaka and the colophon.** The graspable-grasper pair, infinite-inner-
    difference-divided, shines in the param-manifestation-form Bhagavat — like the great-mirror
    holding the reflection (the svabhāvahetu: tadrūpeṇa prakāśamānatva). The fourth vimarśa
    (smṛtiśaktivimarśaḥ) closes at ||4||.

**The crux.** Chunk V2-C completes the caturtho vimarśa (the smṛtiśakti): the memory's root is the
grasper's "by me seen" rehearsal; the grāhyagrāhaka (graspable-grasper) are the two objects that,
though distinct in their manifestations, are both tanmayau (made of the one pure cognition) — the
"this"-ness-rehearsal makes them discontinuous, but they rest in the one pure knower (the 
ahantā-viśrānti, the prakāśasyātmaviśrāntirahaṃbhāvaḥ). The māyā-power does not split the awareness;
the paśu (bound one) is the contracted cognition (aṇu); the final knower is the śūnyātiśūnya (the
param-Śiva). The whole is grounded in the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi and the mirror-metaphor of the 
param-manifestation.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.2.6/1.3.2/1.4.3/1.4.4/1.4.6, 1.5.1/1.5.2/1.5.11/1.5.16/1.5.21,
1.6.3/1.7.1, 2.1.4/2.3.5/2.3.10, 3.2.9 (bodhānām api kartṛtvajuṣāṃ), 4.1.3; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi
15/19/20; the Spandakārikā 2/8; the Vākyapadīya 3.1.105; the Yogadarśana; the Vijñānabhairava 71/106;
the Śivadṛṣṭi 5.9; the Bhagavadgītā 2.58/12.15; the Kiraṇa-āgama (paśur nityo); the Śvetāśvatara;
the Nareśvaraviveka; the siddha-pādas verses; the mahāvidehā-āgama; the Abhinavabhāratī (the 
upacacāra verse). The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel is the direct anchor.

is established as the manifestation of the beings. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-D)

1. **The pañcamo vimarśa = jñānaśaktivimarśa.** The fifth vimarśa opens with the maṅgala (yad
   anuttarasambodhād), and the 21-verse plan is laid out: the prakāśa (manifestation) is the artha's
   own form; the perception and inference of an external object are refuted; the parāmarśa-self
   manifestation; the jñānaparāmarśa as the known.
2. **Kārikā 1 (vartamānāvabhāsānāṃ).** The present-beings' manifestation is fit only for those that
   stand inside (antaḥsthitavatāṃ), with the external-self — the māyā-knower's distinct beings are
   the divided (vicchinnāḥ) appearances of the one pure-cognition knower; that manifestation is the
   Bhagavat's jñānaśakti.
3. **Kārikā 2 (prāgivārtho'prakāśaḥ syāt).** Without manifestation-form the object would be
   unmanifest; the manifestation is not distinct from the object — it IS the object's own self.
   The prakāśamānatā is not a separate property; the Bhaṭṭa verse "prakāśenāvinābhūtaiḥ...
   na bāhyasiddhimṛcchati." The one-sided refutations of the perception/inference of the external.
4. **Kārikā 3 (bhinne prakāśe cābhinne saṃkaro viṣayasya).** Whether the manifestation is distinct
   or non-distinct, the object's mixing (saṃkara) follows; the prakāśātmā prakāśyo'rtho — the
   non-inert object (Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13). The non-inert object is established via the
   vyāpakaviruddha.
5. **Kārikā 4's recap.** The antaḥkṛtānantaviśvarūpatva (the Bhagavat's interiorized universe-forms,
   from Vol 1 kārikā 7) is established via the prakāśa's mirror-manifestation of the pot/cloth/cart.
6. **Kārikā 5 (tattadākasmikābhāso bāhyaṃ ced anumāpayet).** The accidental (ākasmika) varied
   manifestation would infer an external object (the bāhya-anumāna): since the unvaried awareness
   cannot be the cause of the varied ordered manifestations, only the external object-class (with
   the four shadows) can be the cause. This is the Buddhist's inference (the Dharmottara-view), and
   it is refuted (the anubhavasiddha-bheda is false; the pratikarmavyavasthā is svasaṃvedana-self).
7. **The Gītā citations** (6.31: yo māṃ paśyati; 4.18: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyed) — the
   prameyapramātṛ anusandhāna, the sarva-karma-kartṛtva.
8. **The bāhya as pratibimba-arpaka.** The inference: the cognition-interior blue-form is a
   reflection (pratibimbatvāt), so it expects a similar identical (sadṛśa arpaka) — the external
   blue. The indriya-analogy (the sense-organ, never seen, inferred as the cause) answers the
   agṛhītavyāpti objection.
9. **The viṣaya's non-vaiśeṣya.** The vivid/dull (pāṭavāpāṭava) are the object's particulars, not
   the awareness's (the dust-scratched object deposits the dull-awareness-particular). The
   awareness cannot be entered by the other manifestation (the darpaṇa-analogy; the vyāpakaviruddha).
10. **The ekavacana / ananya-bhāk.** The blue-awareness is not a particular of the awareness (it is
    like the mirror's reflection — bodhānadhika, pariplavamāna). The distinct-distinct-momentary-
    cognition-continuum is in truth the non-distinct-awareness speech (the granthakāra's
    pracchanna-abhedabodhavāda).

**The crux.** Chunk V2-D establishes the jñānaśakti: the manifestation (avabhāsa) of the beings is
the Lord's own cognition-power — the beings, though appearing distinct (the māyā-pramātṛ's division),
are all the one pure-cognition knower's manifestation (the mirror-analogy). The external-object
inference (the Buddhist's bāhya-anumāna) is refuted; the prakāśa is the artha's own form; the
non-inert object is established. The pañcamo vimarśa continues into V2-E.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.2.7, 1.4.3, 2.2.4 (svātmaniṣṭhā), 2.3.4/2.3.5; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13;
the Bhaṭṭa (prakāśenāvinābhūtaiḥ); Dharmottara; the Bhagavadgītā 6.31/4.18; the Vijñānavāda;
the sahāropalambhaniyama. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel is the direct anchor.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-E: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikā 5, the bāhya-anumāna, the vāsanā, the yogācāra — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 2800–3600 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti)
continued. Covers: the continuation of kārikā 5 (tattadākasmikābhāso bāhyaṃ ced anumāpayet): the
indriya-analogy; kārikā 6 (na vāsanāprabodho'tra vicitro hetutāmiyāt; tasyāpi tatprabodhasya
vaicitrye kiṃ nibandhanam); the vāsanā-prabodha; the karma/cause-order; the ākasmika/ajñātahetu; the
upasarpaṇa-prayaya and the prathamahetu; the kārya-kāraṇa and the avastutva; the a-raghaṭṭa
(water-wheel); the bālyādau (childhood-etc.) and the sahakārin; the karmākṣiptatva; the abhāsa-
parampare; the yogācāra refutation (the ābhāsaicībhāva, the ekābhāsa, the īśvaraikātmya); and the
maitra-samīhā inference (the vyāpāra-vyāhāra, the śara/wind analogies). Max-effort T1.*

---

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-E)

1. **The chunk's real scope.** V2-E = M00021 lines 2800–3600, the pañcamo vimarśa's kārikā 5–6 area. Its spine is the *bāhyārthavādin vs vijñānavādin* debate: (i) the kārikā 5 (*na vāsanāprabodho'tra vicitro hetutāmiyāt*) — why the vāsanā-awakening cannot be the cause of the manifestation-variety, since vāsanā/awakening are not other than cognition; the satya/avastu analysis of kārya/kāraṇa; the dvicandra/jaundice examples of the real status of error-cognitions; (ii) the rejected alternatives for the source of the ordered ābhāsa-variety: the icchā as prathamahetu, the karma as prathamahetu, the upasarpaṇapratyaya, the samanantarapratyaya-paramparā — all falling to the krama-niyama failure; (iii) the *parasantāna* (other-minds) inference and its refutation, culminating in the īśvaraikātmya/īśvarādvaya turn (Abhinava's own ground). The old file had mislaid a vāsanā-nīḍa/kaula fragment (a garbled out-of-range tail) which is deleted here.

2. **The kārikā enumeration.** The kārikā "*na vāsanāprabodho'tra*" is kārikā 5 in this run; the commentary also recycles "*ākasmikamahetukam*" and the muni-verse "*iha te karmaṇāmeva vipākaścintayiṣyati*." I kept the source's own verse-numbering (the `— (5)` attribution) and flagged the earlier draft's "Kārikā 6" header as the older draft's count. The user-visible numbering should follow the Vivṛti-line order, not the old draft header.

3. **Term-ledger LOCK (carry forward).** To stop the drift the audit flagged, this chunk fixes the English side of the register, and later chunks must hold it:
   - **vimarśa = reflexive-awareness** (the READ_FIRST primary); "rehearsal" and "reflexion" are retired.
   - **prakāśa = manifestation** (NOT "light" in compounds); **ābhāsa = appearance** (NOT also "manifestation") — the two must no longer collide.
   - **saṃvit = consciousness** (never "cognition"); **jñāna = cognition** (so jñāna-śakti = the cognition-power); **bodha = awareness/awakening** (kept distinct from vimarśa).
   - **samīhā = wish**; **vyāhāra = utterance**; **upasarpaṇapratyaya = approaching-cognition**; **samanantarapratyaya = immediately-preceding-condition**.
   - **vāsanā = impression / vāsanā** (kept as vāsanā with the gloss "impression"); **saṃskāra = impression** (the memory-generating latent); **prabodha = awakening**.
   - **īśvaraikātmyavāda = the Lord-unity-view**; **sādhāraṇī/asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi = common/uncommon creation**; **pramātrantara = other knower**; **parasantāna = other stream (other mind)**.
   Where the gloss of a given occurrence deviates from this lock inside this chunk (e.g. the older "rehearsal"), it is understood as the legacy line, and later chunks do NOT carry it.

4. **The anumāna of the other mind (the crux-area).** The vijñānavādin infers the other's wish (samīhā) from the utterance-appearance (*vyāharāmi*); Abhinava, via the bāhyārthavādin, splits the first/third-person forms: caitra's *"he utters"* appearance does not co-inhere in maitra's own-cognition (svasaṃvitsiddha samīhā), so the inference is circular (the other-stream is already presupposed) and, if the mere-wish is universalized, it fits a demon/yakṣa/omniscient/worm equally — the determination collapses. The decisive move: only the *aimed* (samīhitā) action is the wish's effect; to abandon samīhitā-tva is impossible. The residual [X] flags: the exact construal of *ghaṭābhāsānāṃ* (whether "ca" joins the other-jar-appearances or the other-knowers) is left with both readings noted — the sixth/seventh-case tension makes the "ca with the knowers" reading fit.

5. **The īśvaraikātmya opening.** The encouragement of the bāhyārthavādin ("*satyam asi prāmāṇikadhuryaḥ*") and the sādhāraṇī/asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi verses (3.2.17, 4.1.11, 4.1.9) prepare Abhinava's own position: the common (Lord-made) creation is where the knowers' difference melts into unity; the uncommon (paśu-made) creation keeps the difference. This is the seed of the whole sixth-vimarśa move — the reason Dharmakīrti's other-minds text is treated as *atadvarṇitamiva* (as it were not narrated by him, from partiality).

**The crux.** V2-E is where the IPVV disarms the Buddhist explanation of the ordered appearance-variety and of other minds. The vāsanā-awakening cannot be the cause: since vāsanā and awakening are not other than cognition (and whatever is beyond manifestation is nothing), the variety has no separate ground — the bāhyārtha alone can deposit (samarpaka) the ākāra-variety. Then every candidate cause of the kramika-ābhāsa (icchā, karma, upasarpaṇapratyaya, samanantara-paramparā) fails the krama-niyama test, because the middle appearances (gṛhavartin ghaṭa etc.) are never continuously present. The other-minds inference falls to the first/third-person split: the wish inferred is never the other's own-cognition-established wish. The only coherent resting point is the īśvaraikātmya: the one Lord-freedom manifests the varied knower-difference, and in the sādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi the difference melts into unity. This is Abhinava's bridge from the refutation of the Buddhist to the positive monistic thesis.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 3.2.17 (*sarvākṣagocaratvena*), 4.1.11 (*sādhāraṇo'nyathā caiśaḥ*), 4.1.9 (*tasyāsādhāraṇī* / *saiṣāpyajñatayā*); the Dharmakīrti other-minds argument (the *santānāntarasiddhi* discussed as "*atadvarṇitamiva*") and Diṅnāga; the ajaḍa-pramātṛ / the dvicandra-jaundice examples; the Sāmkhya satkāryavāda contrast; the Spandakārikā and Svacchanda 4.141 (*prārabdhrekaṃ na śodhayet*); the Gītā-eligibility register. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel (the ajaḍa pramātṛ's freedom) is the direct anchor for the īśvaraikātmya conclusion. The other-minds section is the conceptual pair of the ajaḍapramātṛ's *svasaṃvitsiddha* self-awareness.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-F: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikā 6, the ābhāsa-vastutva, the bāhya-refutation — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 3600–4400 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti), the conclusion of the bāhyārthavādin's case. Covers: the refinement of the other-minds (parasantāna) inference (the candana/agni and ṣṭhīvana examples; the samīhitā-niyama; the iṣṭi/icchā etymology); the bāla-rudana and āvaraṇa/upasaṃhāra arguments; the īśvarādvayavādin's entry and the stuti; the sādhāraṇī/asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi; kārikā 6 (syādetadavabhāseṣu teṣvevāvasite sati — the sufficiency of the appearances for dealing); the darpaṇa/pratibimba analogy; then the refutation of the external object as whole (avayavin) and as atoms (paramāṇu) — the Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika and Vaibhāṣika positions — establishing that only the ābhāsa is real and is the object of arthakriyā. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock (vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; samīhā = wish; vyāhāra = utterance; pramātrantara = other knower; parasantāna = other stream). Max-effort T1.*

---

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-F)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-F = M00021 lines 3600–4400, the close of the pañcamo vimarśa's bāhyārthavāda and the transition to the īśvarādvaya. Its spine: (i) the refinement of the other-minds (parasantāna) inference — the candana/agni and ṣṭhīvana (spitting) examples prove the samīhitā-niyama (only the *aimed* action is the wish's effect), so the other-stream can never be inferred from a merely-uttered appearance; (ii) the bāla-rudana and āvaraṇa/upasaṃhāra arguments against the vijñānavādin; (iii) the īśvarādvayavādin's entry — caitra, created by the param-Lord in one-ness (ābhāsāntaraikya), knows all like maitra; the stotra and Śivadṛṣṭi citations; (iv) kārikā 6 (*syādetadavabhāseṣu*) — the appearances alone suffice for dealing; the external object is needless; (v) the full refutation of the external object as whole (avayavin — the Nyāya-sūtra 2.1.34 ground) and as atoms (paramāṇu — the Vaibhāṣika position), establishing that only the ābhāsa is real and is the object of arthakriyā.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK is carried from V2-E** (vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; bodha = awareness/awakening; samīhā = wish; vyāhāra = utterance; pramātrantara = other knower; parasantāna = other stream; upasarpaṇapratyaya = approaching-cognition; samanantarapratyaya = immediately-preceding-condition). The "rehearsal"/"reflexion"/"light" variants are retired.

3. **samīhitā/samīhitatva.** I render samīhitā as "the aimed (state)" / samīhitatva as "the being-aimed," to keep the niyama argument legible: only the *aimed* action can be the effect of a wish — abandoning samīhitā-tva is impossible. This is the crux that defeats the other-minds inference and grounds the "the wish is established only by one's own cognition (svasaṃvitsiddha)."

4. **The kārikā 6 reading.** "teṣvevāvasite sati vyavahāre kim anyena bāhyenānupapattinā" — "if the dealing is determined in those very appearances, what [need] of the other, the external, with its impossibility?" The "anupapatti" (impossibility) of the external is the whole preceding refutation. The deśa/kāla niyama verse and the "pramāṇyaṃ vastuviṣayaṃ" and "bhrāntitve cāvasāyasya" (1.3.5) citations are the epistemic core.

5. **The avayavin/paramāṇu refutation.** Following the Nyāyasūtra 2.1.34 (*sarvāprasiddhir avayavyasiddheḥ*), the whole collapses; then the atom is refuted by the six-part-contact and the ekāneka form-contradiction. The [X]-flagged crux is the exact force of "jñānamekaṃ gṛhṇadeva aparaṃ gṛhṇātīty etāvatā vaitatyābhāsaḥ" — the two-ness appearance is admitted but the configuration-appearance is not; I keep both the given gloss and note the kha-readings.

6. **The īśvarādvaya turn.** The stotra (*muhurmuhur aviśrānta*), Śivadṛṣṭi 1.3/1.6, the Śatarudriya, and the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 23 (*prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvaḥ*) all converge on: the Lord's freedom manifests the whole appearance-variety within himself; the sādhāraṇī (Lord-made) sṛṣṭi is where the knowers' difference melts; only by the "living-cognition ladder" (jīvadbodhasopāna) is the advaya reachable. The ahaṃ-grasping of "ahaṃ ghaṭo bhāse" is the seed of the recognition.

**The crux.** V2-F completes the refutation of the external object. The other-minds inference fails because the other's wish is never established in the inferer's own cognition (svasaṃvitsiddha), and only the aimed action is the wish's effect — so the first/third-person split cannot be bridged, and if it were, it would fit a demon or a worm equally. Abhinava then turns the whole debate: the appearances (ābhāsa) are the only reality the dealing needs; the external object (whether the Nyāya whole or the Vaibhāṣika atom) is refuted, and what remains is the manifesting cognition alone. This is the ground on which the īśvarādvayavādin stands: caitra is created by the param-Lord in unity, knows all like maitra, and the one Lord-freedom manifests the varied appearance within himself — the jñānaśakti's conclusion and the bridge to the sixth vimarśa (smṛti/apohana).

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.4.11 (*kāryaṃ hetuḥ svabhāvo vā*), 1.3.5 (*bhrāntitve cāvasāyasya*), kārikā 6 (*syādetadavabhāseṣu*); the santānāntarasiddhi text (Dharmakīrti, discussed as *atadvarṇitamiva*); Nyāyasūtra 2.1.34 (*sarvāprasiddhir avayavyasiddheḥ*); the Vākyapadīya 3.7.108 (*buddhiśabdau pravartete*); Somānanda's Śivadṛṣṭi 1.3/1.6; the Śatarudriya; Abhinava's own stotra (112) and *Ādisiddha*; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 23; the Mālinīvijaya 2.2 (*śaktimacchaktibhedena dharātattvaṃ*). The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel is the direct anchor for the ahaṃbhāva/prakāśaviśrānti conclusion, and the *t3_ajadapramatrsiddhi* audited text governs the sādhāraṇī/asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi reading.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-G: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikās 7–10, the īśvarādvaya creation and the anumāna — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 4400–5200 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti), the transition to the īśvarādvaya-vāda's positive thesis. Covers: kārikā 7 (cidātmaiva hi devo'ntaḥsthitamicchāvaśādbahiḥ yogīva nirupādānamarthajātaṃ prakāśayet — the Lord manifests the whole object-mass from within himself, like a yogin, without an external cause); the caturvidhā sṛṣṭi (parā/sūkṣma/vyūha/vibhava) with the tanmātra, the pratyayasarga, the pañcatattva, and the kumbhakāra/niyatiśakti; kārikā 8 (anumānamanābhātapūrve naiveṣṭamindriyam — inference never concerns the unmanifested); the anumāna/vyāpti analysis (pratyakṣa + anupalambha establish kārya-kāraṇa; kārya-hetu vs svabhāva-hetu; pakṣadharmatā; sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa); kārikā 9 (ābhāsaḥ punarābhāsādbāhyasyāsītkathañcana — the external is never established, by perception or inference); kārikā 10 (svāminaścātmasaṃsthasya bhāvajātasya bhāsanam astyeva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate — the Lord's self-standing being manifests the beings; hence the will-reflexive-awareness proceeds). Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-G)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-G = M00021 lines 4400–5200, the jñānaśakti-vimarśa's īśvarādvaya turn. It closes the external-object refutation (the avayavin/paramāṇu shadow-sun and six-part arguments) and states the positive thesis: kārikā 7 (*cidātmaiva*) — the Lord, who is consciousness, manifests the whole object-mass from within himself, like a yogin, with no external cause; the caturvidhā sṛṣṭi (parā, sūkṣma, vyūha, vibhava) with the tanmātra and pratyayasarga; kārikā 8 (*anumānamanābhātapūrve*) — inference never concerns the unmanifested, since it is construction (vikalpa) and construction needs a prior experience; the kārya-hetu/svabhāva-hetu and pakṣadharmatā analysis; kārikā 9 (*ābhāsaḥ punarābhāsād bāhyasyāsīt kathañcana*) — the external is never established by any means; kārikā 10 (*svāminaścātmasaṃsthasya*) — the Lord's self-standing being manifests the beings; hence the will-reflexive-awareness proceeds (the aham-prakāśa, the sahaja prakāśa, the sarva-ābhāsa resting in the self).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E/F.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; bodha = awareness/awakening; icchā = will; samīhā = wish; vyāhāra = utterance; kriyā = action; pramātrantara = other knower; upasarpaṇapratyaya = approaching-cognition; niyatiśakti = the necessity-power; tanmātra = subtle element (kept as tanmātra); sṛṣṭi = creation; sādhāraṇī/asādhāraṇī = common/uncommon. The "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **cidātmaiva (kārikā 7).** I render the compound as "the consciousness-self-alone is the Lord" — the deva who is cid-ātman. The point: the Lord's lordship (aiśvarya) is the freedom to join and disjoin appearances; hence he can manifest the whole object-mass from within himself, no external upādāna. The yogin-example is the crux: the yogin's creation is real (arthakriyākāri) though not caused by the famous clay-potter chain; so "nirupādānam" means "without the external famous-cause material," not "without any cause." The [X]-flagged reading: whether the yogin still uses the assembled atoms (saṃghaṭitāḥ paramāṇavaḥ) or the pure will — I follow the text's own turn ("with a grass-bit overstepping the fame" → the pure will; and the Bhaṭṭa-Divākara verse confirming the dream's own-creation).

4. **The caturvidhā sṛṣṭi.** The fourfold creation (parā/sūkṣma/vyūha/vibhava) is introduced via the āgama verse *parasūkṣmavyūhayogād vibhavācca caturvidhā*. I keep the structural mapping in the apparatus: paratva in the three higher, sūkṣmatva in the two, vyūha in one; the niyatiśakti supplies the upādāna-appearance (tanmātra etc.) while in truth everything is nirupādāna in the Lord. The pañcabrahma and the pratyayasarga (buddhi-tattva-attribute) are the being-creation that interpenetrates the tattvas.

5. **anumānamanābhātapūrve (kārikā 8).** The seed: inference is vikalpa; vikalpa needs a prior experience; so inference never concerns the never-manifested. The seed→sprout, clay→jar, stick-wheel→jar examples establish kāraṇatva as the universal "seen-prior" by pratyakṣa+anupalambha. This is the ground for denying that the external (never experienced) can be inferred. The kārya-hetu (apūrva, "new," inferred) vs svabhāva-hetu (identity-based, established) distinction is the epistemic core; the pakṣadharmatā and the "sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa" are handled via the dharmapratyakṣa argument.

6. **The anumāna/vyāpti and the indriya.** The sense-organ itself is never perceived directly (nityaparokṣa), yet it is inferred only as the "seen-form-light-more some cause" — i.e., by the universal. So the inference never reaches an unmanifested particular. The pratyābhāsa (per-appearance) operation of the pramāṇa (cf. 2.3.2 *ekābhidhānaviṣaye mitiḥ*) is the bridge to the later adhikāra.

**The crux.** V2-G completes the īśvarādvaya-vāda's positive turn. The external object being refuted (both the whole and the atom), the only source of the ordered appearance-variety is the Lord's own freedom: consciousness alone (saṃvid eva) is the all-world-cause, and its aiśvarya is precisely the freedom to join and disjoin appearances. Kārikā 7 states this via the yogin-example; the caturvidhā sṛṣṭi gives the ontological map (parā/sūkṣma/vyūha/vibhava with the tanmātra and pratyayasarga) — all resting, in truth, in the Lord (ananyopādāna). Kārikā 8 then shuts the door on ever inferring the external: inference is construction needing prior experience, so the never-manifested can never be reached — the bāhya has no epistemic purchase. The ahaṃ-prakāśa (svāminaś cātmasaṃsthasya, kārikā 10) is the seed of the recognition: the being that manifests itself as "I" is what manifests all beings within itself.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.5.1 (*vartamānāvabhāsānāṃ*), 1.5.3, 1.1.5 (*tatra jñānaṃ svataḥ siddhaṃ*), 1.4.2 (*bhāsayecca svakāle*), 2.4.11 (*kāryaṃ hetuḥ svabhāvo vā*), 2.3.2, 2.3.12 (*arthakriyāpi sahajā*), kārikās 7–10 of this vimarśa; the āgama verses (parasūkṣmavyūhayogāt; ekadvitricatuṣpañcaguṇaṃ; śaktiśca śaktimāṃścaiva); Somānanda's Śivadṛṣṭi 1.13; the Śivastotra 20.9 and Abhinava's stotra 120; the Bhaṭṭa-Divākara verse; the Bhaṭṭa-Śrī-Nārāyaṇa verse; Diṅnāga's ālambanaparīkṣā and vijñaptimātratāsiddhi (the atom-refutation). The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi and its T3/C1 audited text govern the ahaṃ-prakāśa/prakāśa-viśrānti reading, and the saṃvit-alone-as-cause thesis is the direct anchor for the recognition.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-G, continuation)

7. **The anumāna/vyāpti (kārikā 8 continued).** The kārya-kāraṇa relation is established by pratyakṣa + anupalambha alone (the smoke-fire, clay-jar, stick-wheel-jar examples); the cause-ness is a universal grasped "as-seen-prior." The svabhāva-hetu establishes only the already-established (vyāvahāryate, not newly inferred); the kārya-hetu alone infers the "new." Inference never reaches the never-manifested external. The pakṣadharmatā is a third member, itself grasped by present perception, so the pervasion-construction does not make the inference touch an unmanifested particular.

8. **The sense-organ (indriya).** It is never perceived directly (nityaparokṣa), yet it is inferred only as "the seen form-light-more some cause" — i.e., by the universal of cause-ness; and the "seen" designation is fit because the cause-ness-universal is seen. The apoha aside (saugata's prativyāvṛtty-adhyavasāya) and the pratyābhāsa operation of the pramāṇa (2.3.2 *ekābhidhānaviṣaye mitiḥ*) are the cross-reference.

9. **Kārikā 9 (ābhāsaḥ punarābhāsād bāhyasyāsīt kathañcana).** The external can be neither perceived nor inferred: the not-manifested cannot be the object of any pramāṇa, since every pramāṇa is cognition-form and only the manifested is cognized. The "somehow" (kathañcana) is the residue that even a concession leaves — the inference, being saṃvedana-rūpa, stays in the own-cognition; the distinct is never reached. This closes the bāhya question.

10. **Kārikā 10 (svāminaścātmasaṃsthasya).** The Lord's self-standing being manifests the being-mass; the manifestation is not apart from the will-reflexive-awareness — the icchā is the parāmarśa-particular, and the parāmarśa is the prakāśa's own nature (so there is no infinite regress of the will wanting to will). The "eka"-word and the *nareśvaraviveka* verses establish that the to-be-created must be non-separate-from-first (apṛthakpratham) with the creation-will. The sahaja (natural) manifestation is the aham-prakāśa; the this-ness is the bāhyatā-appearance that joins it. This is the seed of the whole recognition: the being that is self-standing as "I" manifests all beings in itself, and the will-reflexive-awareness is its own nature.

**The crux (continuation).** The epistemic closure of the bāhya is complete: no pramāṇa — perception or inference — reaches the external, because every pramāṇa is cognition-form and only the manifested is cognized (kārikā 9). The positive thesis then stands alone: the Lord, who is consciousness, is self-standing as "I" and manifests the whole being-mass within himself; the will-reflexive-awareness that would make a cloth or a jar is nothing but the manifestation's own nature (kārikā 10). The sahaja aham-prakāśa and the sarva-ābhāsa resting in the self are the ground of the recognition (pratyabhijñā) that is the whole jñānaśakti's culmination.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-H: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikās 11–13, the vimarśa as the manifestation's own nature; the parā-vāk — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 5200–6000 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti), the deepest vimarśa-section. Covers: the continuation of kārikā 10 (the pramātṛ-prameya abheda; the icchā as the prathama-tuṭi; the smaraṇa; the niyatiśakti; the kṣaṇabhaṅga); kārikā 11 (svabhāvamavabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā prakāśo'rthoparakto'pi sphaṭikādijaḍopamaḥ — the reflexive-awareness is the manifestation's own nature; otherwise the manifestation would be inert like crystal); the vikalpa objection and Dharmakīrti; the sphaṭika/ādarśa and the sārūpya; the grāhakagrāhya; the camatkāra (rapture), the ānanda, the sahṛdayatā and the rasa theory (Abhinavabhāratī); the ātman/anātmā prakāśana; kārikā 12 (ātmāta eva caitanyaṃ citkriyā citikartṛtā — consciousness, its action, its agency); kārikā 13 (citiḥ pratyavamarśātmā parā vāk svarasoditā svātantryam etan mukhyaṃ tad aiśvaryaṃ paramātmanaḥ — the reflexive-awareness as the parā-vāk, the Lord's freedom and lordship); the parā/madhyamā/vaikharī vāk, the sphoṭa, and the Śivadṛṣṭi refutation of the grammarian's paśyantī-as-param. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-H)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-H = M00021 lines 5200–6000, the deepest vimarśa-section of the jñānaśakti-vimarśa. It completes kārikā 10 (the icchā as the prathama-tuṭi; the smaraṇa; the niyatiśakti; the kṣaṇabhaṅga), states kārikā 11 (*svabhāvam avabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur*) — the reflexive-awareness is the manifestation's own nature, otherwise it would be inert like crystal — and develops it through the sphaṭika/ādarśa and the sārūpya, the grāhakagrāhya, the camatkāra/ānanda and the rasa-theory (Abhinavabhāratī), the ātman/anātmā prakāśana; then kārikā 12 (*ātmāta eva caitanyaṃ citkriyā citikartṛtā*), and kārikā 13 (*citiḥ pratyavamarśātmā parā vāk*) with the whole parā/madhyamā/vaikharī vāk and the Śivadṛṣṭi refutation of the grammarian's paśyantī.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E/F/G.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; parāmarśa = the (self-)reflexive-awareness / the rehearsal-of-the-own-form (kept as "reflexive-awareness"); prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; bodha = awareness/cognition; icchā = will; camatkāra = rapture (kept as camatkāra); ānanda = bliss; vāk = word/speech (parā vāk = the highest word); paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī = kept transliterated; sphoṭa = the sphoṭa; kriyā = action; kartṛtā = agency; niyatiśakti = the necessity-power. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 11 (svabhāvam avabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā prakāśo'rthoparakto'pi sphaṭikādijaḍopamaḥ).** The reflexive-awareness ("I") is the manifestation's own nature; if it were not, the manifestation, even tinged with the object, would be like the crystal or the inert — i.e., no different from jaḍa. The whole kārikā-11 commentary turns on showing that the mere object-tingeing (like the mirror reflecting the jar) is not enough; only the will-entry (icchā-anupraveśa), the svātantrya, makes the manifestation alive. This is the heart of the ajaḍa-pramātṛ thesis.

4. **The camatkāra/rasa passage.** Abhinava here gives one of his most famous statements of the rasa theory: the camatkāra is the reflexive-awareness (parāmarśa) resting in the knower (pramātṛ-viśrānti), the paramānanda, the nirvṛti; the sahṛdaya is one whose heart (hṛdaya = parāmarśa) takes the rasa, disregarding the standing manifestation-part that rests in the object. He explicitly cross-references the Abhinavabhāratī (*rasā nava* = the nine rasas, the obstacle-free taste-form mind-operations). The [X]-flag: the exact sentence on the vīta-vighnatva of the śṛṅgāra-rasa is dense; I keep the reading that the rasa-taste rests wholly in the knower, transcending the object's obstacle.

5. **Kārikā 12 (ātmāta eva caitanyaṃ citkriyā citikartṛtā).** The same-substratum-ness (sāmānādhikaraṇya) of the self, consciousness, the consciousness-action, and the consciousness-agency is the vimarśa-prādhānya. The Śivasūtra and Kallaṭa are the anchors; the grammatical analysis (citi/kip, caitanya/ṣyañ, cetanakriyā) shows the kriyā is reflexive-awareness-form and the relation is knower-rested. The substance (dravya) discussion ties the self to the universal-as-padārtha.

6. **Kārikā 13 (citiḥ pratyavamarśātmā parā vāk svarasoditā).** The consciousness-action is the reflexive-awareness, the parā-vāk; this is the Lord's freedom and lordship — not the paśu's action-organ word. The vāk-śakti enters the (inert) organ-class and makes it act freely (Spandakārikā 1.6). The paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī analysis, the sphoṭa (Vākyapadīya 1.85), and the svarasoditā-as-nityoditā confirm the parā-vāk as the pure ahaṃ that has no deśa-kāla-ākāra contraction; and the Śivadṛṣṭi (2.20, 2.80) refutes the grammarian's claim that paśyantī is the param — the paśyantī is still contracted (viṣayārpitātmanā), so only the parā-vāk (the pure ahaṃ, sadāśivarūpatā) is the param.

**The crux.** V2-H is the philosophical core of the jñānaśakti-vimarśa. It establishes that the reflexive-awareness ("I") is the manifestation's own nature (kārikā 11): a mere mirror-like object-tingeing would leave the manifestation inert; only the will-entry, the svātantrya, vivifies it. The camatkāra is the reflexive-awareness resting in the knower — the paramānanda that no mere object-pleasure (with its vyatiriktākāṅkṣā) can give; this is the ground of the rasa theory. Kārikā 12 ties the self's own-form to consciousness, action, and agency (the same-substratum vimarśa). Kārikā 13 identifies the consciousness-action with the parā-vāk, the Lord's freedom and lordship: the pure ahaṃ that manifests the whole world within itself, in which the knower-object difference is not yet threaded (bhedāsūtraṇarūpa); the paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī are its contracted derivatives, and the parā-vāk (sadāśivarūpatā) is the param. This is the seed of the recognition and of the whole māheśvarya.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.5.20 (*ghaṭo'yam ityadhyavasā*), 1.1.3 (*kintu mohavaśā*), 1.4.2 (*bhāsayecca svakāle*), 2.4.11 (*yoginirmāṇatābhāve*), 2.4.21 (*itthaṃ tathāghaṭapaṭādi*), 2.2.4, 2.3.2, kārikās 10–13; Somānanda's Śivadṛṣṭi 1.8, 3.56, 5.9, 2.1, 2.20, 2.80; the Spandakārikā 1.6; the Vākyapadīya 1.85, 1.125 (Bhartṛhari); Abhinava's own stotra 61 and 112; the Uttarastotra 13.15; the avadhūtācārya verse; the Vijñānabhairava 62; Kallaṭa; the Śivasūtra; the Ādisiddha 15. The Abhinavabhāratī (rasa theory) is referenced as the expanded treatment of the camatkāra/sahṛdayatā; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi governs the ajaḍa-pramātṛ thesis and the T3/C1 audited text anchors the vimarśa-as-own-nature reading.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-I: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikās 14–19, the sphurattā, the jñeyīkaraṇa, the powers as the vimarśa — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 6000–6800 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti), the positive account of the powers. Covers: the close of kārikā 13 (the parā-vāk, the aiśvarya = icchānuvartitva, the ānanda = pūrṇatā); kārikā 14 (sā sphurattā mahāsattā deśakālāviśeṣiṇī saiṣā sāratayā proktā hṛdayaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ — the throbbing as the great being, the heart of the param-Lord); the sphurattā/spanda/ūrmi and the mahāsattā/nityatā; kārikās 15–16 (ātmānam ata evāyaṃ jñeyīkuryāt pṛthaksthiti / svātantryād amuktam ātmānaṃ — the self makes itself the known; the Lord, free, constructs and deals with himself through the īśa-etc. constructs); kārikā 17 (nāhantādiparāmarśabhedād asyānyatātmanaḥ — the division of the ahantā/idantā reflexive-awarenesses is no ground for the self's otherness); kārikā 18 (māyāśaktyā vibhoḥ saiva bhinnasaṃvedyagocarā kathitā jñānasaṃkalpādhyavasāyādināmabhiḥ — the jñāna/saṃkalpa/adhyavasāya powers are the vimarśaśakti contracted by the māyāśakti); kārikā 19 (sākṣātkārakṣaṇe'py asti vimarśaḥ katham anyathā dhāvanādy upapadyeta pratisandhānavarjitam — the vimarśa is present even in the moment of direct manifestation, else running etc. could not happen without anusandhāna). Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-I)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-I = M00021 lines 6000–6800, the jñānaśakti-vimarśa's positive thesis on the powers. It closes kārikā 13 (the aiśvarya = icchānuvartitva; the ānanda = pūrṇatā; the parā-vāk and the paśyantī); states kārikā 14 (*sā sphurattā mahāsattā*) — the throbbing as the great being, the heart (hṛdaya) of the param-Lord, with the sphurattā/spanda/ūrmi synonyms and the mahāsattā/nityatā analysis; kārikās 15–16 (*ātmānam ata evāyaṃ jñeyīkuryāt / svātantryād amuktam ātmānaṃ*) — the self makes itself the known, and the free Lord constructs and deals with himself through the īśa-etc. constructs; kārikā 17 (*nāhantādiparāmarśabhedād asyānyatātmanaḥ*) — the division of the ahantā/idantā reflexive-awarenesses does not make the self other; kārikā 18 (*māyāśaktyā vibhoḥ saiva bhinnasaṃvedyagocarā*) — the jñāna/saṃkalpa/adhyavasāya powers are the one vimarśaśakti contracted by the māyāśakti; kārikā 19 (*sākṣātkārakṣaṇe'py asti vimarśaḥ*) — the vimarśa is present even in the direct-manifestation instant, else running etc. could not happen without anusandhāna.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E/F/G/H.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; parāmarśa = the (self-)reflexive-awareness; pratyavamarśa = the re-reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; sphurattā = throbbing (kept as sphurattā); spanda = the throbbing-motion (kept as spanda); ūrmi = wave; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; icchā = will; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; jñeyīkaraṇa = the making-into-the-known; sākṣātkāra = direct manifestation; adhyavasāya = determination; saṃkalpa = construction; smṛti = memory; ahantā/idantā = I-ness/this-ness. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 14 (sā sphurattā mahāsattā ... hṛdayaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ).** The reflexive-awareness-power is the sphurattā, the mahāsattā, the deśa-kāla-non-particularizing being — the heart of the param-Lord. The hṛdaya is not a mere metaphor (upacarita) but the primary (mukhya): the Gītā 14.27 (*brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham*) confirms that the reflexive-awareness "I" is the resting-place of the Bliss-Brahmā. The sphurattā is the "I"-attached flashing that is transferred onto the object ("to me the jar flashes") — i.e., the being (bhāva) flashes only by entering the cognition (bodhāveśa); the sphurattā-analysis is the bridge to the recognition.

4. **Kārikās 15–16 (jñeyīkaraṇa and the īśa-constructs).** The self makes itself the known (jñeyīkuryāt), not by facing an external known (which would break its freedom into dependence); the potter's case is metaphorical (upacarita) — only the param-Lord is the real agent. In kārikā 16 the free Lord, without losing his freedom, constructs himself as īśa/Śiva etc. and deals (vyavahārayet) with himself through teaching/worship/meditation. The Gītā 10.20/15.15 confirm the "I-as-the-self-in-all-hearts" is the cognition-self, not the body.

5. **Kārikā 17 (nāhantādiparāmarśabhedāt).** The apparent division of the reflexive-awarenesses (the "I" of the establishing, the "this" of the established) is no ground for the self's otherness: the root-reflexive-awareness "I" (mūlaparāmarśa) never abandons, and it penetrates (anuvedhaka) even the "this"-reflexive-awareness. The "like the tiṅ-said action" (tiṅvācyakarmavat) — the action-word's action is the reflexive-awareness itself (the Vākyapadīya 3.6.1 *dik sādhanaṃ kriyā kāla iti*), so the number/time etc. attach only to the substance-becoming appearances, not to the reflexive-awareness.

6. **Kārikā 18 (māyāśaktyā vibhoḥ saiva ... jñānasaṃkalpādhyavasāyādināmabhiḥ).** The jñāna/saṃkalpa/adhyavasāya/smṛti powers are not new tattvas beyond the vimarśaśakti; they are the one vimarśaśakti contracted by the māyāśakti (the māyāya-known-tinge, māyīyavedyoparāga). The variety of the powers and of their objects is from the māyā-tinge, not from any real division of the cognition (jñānādinām abhedaḥ). This is how the "Lord manifests" (bhāsyate) is a metaphor (upacāra) for the self-manifestation.

7. **Kārikā 19 (sākṣātkārakṣaṇe'py asti vimarśaḥ).** Even in the perception-instant the vimarśa is present — the "how-otherwise" (katham anyathā): without it, running and the other purposive actions, destitute of anusandhāna, could not happen. The vimarśa is present in the construction and in the direct manifestation alike (the object is constructed only as manifested; the not-manifested is never constructed). The cross-references: ĪPK 1.3.1–1.3.2 (*dṛk svābhāsaiva*), the Pramāṇavārttika 3.174 (*saṃketasmaraṇopāyam*), and the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20.

**The crux.** V2-I is the positive culmination of the jñānaśakti-vimarśa's account of the powers. The one vimarśaśakti — the Lord's own reflexive-awareness — is everything: the sphurattā-mahāsattā that is the heart of the param-Lord (kārikā 14); the freedom by which the self makes itself the known and, without losing freedom, constructs and deals with itself as īśa/Śiva (kārikās 15–16); the root-"I"-reflexive-awareness that penetrates even the "this"-reflexive-awareness, so the apparent division is no otherness (kārikā 17); and the single power that, contracted by the māyāśakti, appears as the jñāna/saṃkalpa/adhyavasāya/smṛti powers (kārikā 18). Kārikā 19 secures the vimarśa even in the perception-instant. The whole is the ground of the recognition: the knowing self that deals, constructs, remembers, and perceives is the one Lord whose own nature is the reflexive-awareness "I."

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.3.1–1.3.2, 1.5.10, 1.5.11, 1.5.12, 1.5.15–16, 1.6.1, 1.2.7, 1.4, 2.3.10, 2.4.15, kārikās 13–19 of this vimarśa; Somānanda's Śivadṛṣṭi 1.2, 1.18, 2.17, 2.19, 2.20, 2.64, 3.10; the Spandakārikā 8, 19, 21, 22; the Vākyapadīya 1.85, 1.125, 3.6.1; the Mālinīvijaya 3.9, 3.28 and the Mālinītantra 4.5; the Tantrasāra 3; the Gītā 10.20, 14.27, 15.15; the Yogasūtra 1.28; the Pramāṇavārttika 3.174; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 15, 20; the Vijñānabhairava 130; the Chāndogya 6.2.1; Abhinava's stotra 1; the Bhaṭṭa-Śaṃkaranandana and Bhaṭṭa-Candrānanda verses. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi T3/C1 anchors the ahaṃ-prakāśa and the vimarśa-as-own-nature reading; the sphurattā/spanda register ties to the Spandakārikā parallel.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-J: the pañcamo vimarśa — kārikās 19–20, the saṃskāra-vimarśa, the adhyavasāya as the param-Lord's power — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 6800–7600 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the fifth vimarśa (jñānaśakti), the close of the vimarśa-section. Covers: the continuation of kārikā 19 (the saṃskāra-ādhāna/prabodhana; the Bhaṭṭa and abhidharma citations; the pratyakṣa's parāmarśa in the child; the saṃketasmaraṇa; the staimitya/mental-absorption argument that even the absorbed perception is vimarśa-form; the manaskāra/avadhāna and the anuvyavasāya); and kārikā 20 (ghaṭo'yam ityadhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī pareśaśaktir ātmeva bhāsate na tvidantayā — the determination "this jar" is beyond name-and-form, the param-Lord's power, manifesting like the self, not by the this-ness); the vācyavācaka and sphoṭa analysis, the sāmānādhikaraṇya of the guṇa/dravya, and the refutation of the vācaka's idantā. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-J)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-J = M00021 lines 6800–7600, the close of the jñānaśakti-vimarśa's vimarśa-section. It completes kārikā 19 (the saṃskāra-ādhāna/prabodhana — the reflexive-awareness is what deposits and awakens the memory-impression; the staimitya argument — even the absorbed perception is vimarśa-form, else the "again-constructing" and the later remembrance could not happen; the manaskāra/avadhāna and the anuvyavasāya) and states kārikā 20 (*ghaṭo'yam ityadhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī pareśaśaktir ātmeva bhāsate na tvidantayā* — the determination "this jar" is beyond name-and-form; it is the param-Lord's power manifesting like the self, not by the this-ness), with the vācyavācaka and sphoṭa analysis, the sāmānādhikaraṇya of the guṇa/dravya, and the refutation of the vācaka's idantā.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-I.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; parāmarśa = the (self-)reflexive-awareness; pratyavamarśa = the re-reflexive-awareness; anuvyavasāya = the re-observation; prakāśa = manifestation; saṃskāra = impression; vāsanā = vāsanā/impression; bhāvanā = meditation; manaskāra = mind-attention; avadhāna = attention; adhyavasāya = determination; saṃkalpa = construction; vikalpa = construction; smṛti = memory; svalakṣaṇa = own-marker; sāmānya = universal; sphoṭa = the sphoṭa; vācya/vācaka = the denoted/denoting; icchā = will. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 19's saṃskāra-section.** The core: only the vimarśa-form cognition (the reflexive-awareness-resting pramātṛ) can deposit (ādhāna) and awaken (prabodhana) the saṃskāra; a reflexion-empty perception could do neither. The child's first perception is not vimarśa-empty (the opponent's claim), because convention-grasping (saṃketagrahaṇa) requires the reflexive-awareness; and the "all-cognition/quieted-state" (staimitya) argument shows the absorbed perception too is vimarśa-form — else the "again-constructing" would differ, and the later remembrance could not arise. The Bhaṭṭa and abhidharma citations (Abhidharmakośa 2.50) are the anchors.

4. **Kārikā 20 (ghaṭo'yam ityadhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī).** The determination "this jar" is beyond the name ("jar") and the form (the shape); it is the param-Lord's own power (pareśaśakti), manifesting like the self (ātmeva — i.e., as "I"), not by the this-ness (na tvidantayā). This answers three objections: (i) the coarse word-tinged vimarśa is still the manifestation's life (not a separate inert thing); (ii) the Sāṃkhya's claim that adhyavasāya is a buddhi-attribute (jaḍa) is wrong — it is the citi's power, the paśu's determiner; (iii) the vimarśa has no form other than the vācya/vācaka — the third reflexive-awareness is the vimarśa itself. The vācyavācaka/sphoṭa analysis (Yogasūtra 3.17, Ślokavārttika 4.182) and the sāmānādhikaraṇya of the guṇa/dravya establish that the this-ness does not attach to the vācaka.

**The crux.** V2-J completes the vimarśa-section's proof that the reflexive-awareness is the life of the manifestation. Kārikā 19 shows it is the vimarśa that deposits and awakens the memory-impression (so memory and construction presuppose it), and that even the absorbed perception (staimitya) is vimarśa-form — for otherwise neither the re-construction nor the later remembrance could occur. Kārikā 20 states the positive result: the determination "this jar" is beyond name-and-form; it is the param-Lord's power, manifesting like the self as "I," not by the this-ness. The paśu's determinations, memories, and constructions are all the one vimarśaśakti contracted by the māyāśakti; and in the recognition they return to the pure aham. This is the seed of the whole recognition that the jñānaśakti-vimarśa has been preparing.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.3.5 (*bhrāntitve cāvasāyasya*), 1.3.7, 1.4.1 (*sa hi pūrvānubhūtārthopalabdhā*), 1.5.18 (*māyāśaktyā vibhoḥ*), 1.5.20, 1.5.21 (*kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya*), 2.2.3, 2.3.1, kārikās 19–20; the Pramāṇavārttika 3.174 (*saṃketasmaraṇopāyam*); the Abhidharmakośa 2.50 (*svato'nye kāraṇahetuḥ*); the Vākyapadīya 1.124–125; the Yogasūtra 1.28, 3.17; the Ślokavārttika 4.182; the Nyāyasūtra 3.1.19, 3.1.25; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi (the ahaṃ-prakāśa); the Bhaṭṭa (Kumārila) citations; the Śivadṛṣṭi 1.9–1.11. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi T3/C1 anchors the adhyavasāya-as-citi's-power and the aham-manifestation reading; the sākṣātkāra/vimarśa relation ties to the 1.3.1–1.3.2 (*dṛk svābhāsaiva*) ground.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-K)

1. **The chunk's scope and the ||5|| close.** V2-K = M00021 lines 7600–8405, the close of the jñānaśaktivimarśa (pañcamo vimarśa). It completes kārikā 20 (the vācaka's own-form reflexive-awareness; the svaprakāśatva like the lamp; the Vākyapadīya 1.50/1.55; the svarūpavācakatā; the niścaya/saṃśaya and svasaṃvedana; the Bhaṭṭa and Dharmottara; the adhyāsa of the vācaka's form on the vācya — the saṃketa and the vyavahāra, the daṇḍī/siṃha examples, the prāiṣa, the madhyamā-vāk, the saṃsāra-tree, the Vaikharī) and states kārikā 21 (*kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedyadeśakālānurodhataḥ jñānasmṛtyavasāyādi sakramaṃ pratibhāsate* — the powers appear with order only by following the place-and-time of the different cognized; in themselves they are one and order-less, resting in the I). It closes with the colophon of the jñānaśaktivimarśa ||5||, after which the sixth vimarśa (V2-L) begins.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-J.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; parāmarśa = the (self-)reflexive-awareness; pratyavamarśa = the re-reflexive-awareness; anuvyavasāya = the re-observation; prakāśa = manifestation; vācya/vācaka = the denoted/denoting; svarūpavācakatā = the own-form-denoting; sphoṭa = the sphoṭa; adhyāsa = superimposition; saṃketa = convention; vyutpatti = derivation; vyavahāra = dealing; prāiṣa = the command; paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī/parā = kept transliterated; saṃsaraṇa = the rolling (the saṃsāra-tree); saṃskāra = impression; manaskāra = mind-attention; niścaya = determination; saṃśaya = doubt; saṃvedana = cognition; svasaṃvedana = own-cognition. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 20's vācaka-section.** The word's own form (svarūpa) is reflexively aware (svanāmnā parāmarśa) because the reflexive-awareness is the manifestation's nature — the word, like the lamp, manifests itself and the object. The Vākyapadīya 1.50/1.55 (*ātmarūpaṃ yathā jñāne / grāhyatvaṃ grahaṇatvaṃ ca*) anchor this. The Bhaṭṭa and Dharmottara passages defend the svaprakāśatva of the determination against the adhyavasāyāpekṣa-prāmāṇya view. The adhyāsa of the vācaka's form on the vācya (and vice-versa) is what makes saṃketa and vyavahāra possible; the daṇḍī and siṃha examples show it is a true superimposition (on a non-divided ground), not a mere metaphor.

4. **The prāiṣa and the madhyamā-vāk.** The command ("bring the jar") shows the reflexive-awareness's mutual pervasion (parasparavyāpti) in the dealing — the speaker's and hearer's reflexive-awarenesses exchange agent/action roles (the image-image reversal). The madhyamā-vāk (the inner speech in the prāṇa) is where the grasped-grasper phenomena are constructed and where the saṃsāra-tree (saṃsaraṇa) has its root — watered by the rasa of attachment. The four-fold vāk (parā/paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī; Ṛgveda 1.164.45) and the Spandakārikā 48 give the ontological map; the Vaikharī is where the word appears as ear-grasped, yet in truth only the word-pervasion extends there (Śivadṛṣṭi 2.8).

5. **Kārikā 21 (kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya...).** The jñāna/smṛti/avasāya powers appear "with order" (sakrama) only by following the place-and-time of the different cognized (bhinnasaṃvedya); in themselves — resting in the I-reflexive-awareness — they are one and order-less (the aham-viśrānti is akhaṇḍita; the sakramatva appears only on its back, tatpṛṭha). The deśa-kāla are the marks of the cognized (vedyadharma); the māyāśakti (1.5.18) produces the difference of the cognized, so the powers are atirikta-natirikta (transcending-not-transcending) — the param-Lord's own power (1.2.7). The colophon closes the jñānaśaktivimarśa.

**The crux.** V2-K completes the jñānaśaktivimarśa. Kārikā 20 shows the word's own form is reflexively aware (like the lamp), and that the adhyāsa of the vācaka's form on the vācya is the ground of all saṃketa and vyavahāra — the whole of language is the reflexive-awareness superimposing its own form on the object and the object's form on itself. The prāiṣa and the madhyamā-vāk locate this in the knower, where the saṃsāra-tree is rooted in the restless construction watered by attachment. Kārikā 21 then seals the positive thesis: the powers (jñāna, smṛti, avasāya) appear with order only by following the cognized's place-and-time; in themselves, resting in the I, they are the one order-less reflexive-awareness — the param-Lord's own power, atirikta-natirikta. This is the culmination of the fifth vimarśa, the full account of the jñānaśakti as the manifestation of the one consciousness.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.2.7 (*jñānaṃ ca citsvarūpaṃ cet*), 1.3.7, 1.5.10, 1.5.11, 1.5.13, 1.5.16, 1.5.18, 1.5.20, 1.5.21, 2.1.4 (*kramo bhedāśraya*), 2.3.10, 4.1.10, kārikās 20–21; the Vākyapadīya 1.50, 1.55, 1.124–125; the Yogasūtra 3.17; the Ślokavārttika 4.182; the Ṛgveda 1.164.45; the Spandakārikā 48; the Svacchanda (sādākhyaṃ yat paraṃ bījaṃ); the Śivadṛṣṭi 2.8; the Vijñānabhairava 145; the Abhidharmakośa 2.50; the Bhaṭṭa (Kumārila) and Dharmottara; the Pramāṇavārttika 3.174; the Nyāyasūtra 3.1.19/3.1.25. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi T3/C1 anchors the ahaṃ-viśrānti and the adhyavasāya-as-citi's-power; the vācaka/sphoṭa register ties to the Vākyapadīya parallel. The sixth vimarśa (V2-L) begins immediately after the ||5|| colophon.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-L)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-L = M00021 lines 8405–9200, the ṣaṣṭho vimarśa — the apohanaśakti (the removal power), which governs smṛti (memory) and the whole construction (vikalpa) process. It states the 11-verse introduction; kārikā 1 (*ahaṃpratyavamarśo yaḥ prakāśātmāpi vāgvapuḥ nāsau vikalpaḥ sahyukto dvayākṣepī viniścayaḥ*) — the reflexive-awareness "I," though it is word-bodied (vāgvapus, the parā-vāk), is not a construction but a determination that excludes the twofold; kārikā 2 (*bhinnayoravabhāso hi syād ghaṭāghaṭayordvayoḥ prakāśasyeva nānyasya bhedinastvavabhāsanam*) — the counterpart (pratiyogi) is possible in the object (the māyā-word), not in the manifestation; kārikā 3 (*tadatatpratibhāabhājā mātraivātadvyapohanāt tanniścayanamukto hi vikalpo ghaṭa ityayam*) — the construction "this is a jar" is the determination that removes the not-jar; kārikās 4–5 (*cittattvaṃ māyayā hitvā bhinna evāvabhāti yaḥ dehe buddhāvatha prāṇe kalpite nabhasīva vā / pramātṛtvenāhamiti vimarśo'nyavyapohanāt vikalpa eva sa parapratiyogyavabhāsajaḥ*) — the "I" that descends into the body, mind, breath, or the conceived void is a vikalpa, born of the other-counterpart's manifestation.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-K.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal (the apohanaśakti = the removal power); vikalpa = construction; niścaya = determination; saṃśaya = doubt; pratiyogi = counterpart; virodha = opposition; vācya/vācaka = denoted/denoting; saṃskāra = impression; vāsanā = impression/vāsanā; icchā = will; kriyā = action; sakrama/akrama = with/without order; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; śūnya = the void; prāṇa = the breath; puryaṣṭaka = the eight-fold inner body. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 1 (ahaṃpratyavamarśo... vāgvapuḥ nāsau vikalpaḥ sahyukto dvayākṣepī viniścayaḥ).** The reflexive-awareness "I" is the pure manifestation's own form — the parā-vāk, word-bodied — yet it is not a vikalpa: a vikalpa always operates with the twofold (the that-form and the that-form-less, the affirmed and the negated, joined, divided, suspected), whereas the pure "I"-reflexive-awareness has no counterpart (pratiyogi). It is a determination (niścaya) that invokes/excludes the twofold (dvayākṣepī) — i.e., it is the apohana-operation itself, but on the pure ground where no counterpart is possible. The Bhaṭṭa and Dharmottara passages defend the svaprakāśatva of the determination; the vācaka/sphoṭa analysis (the word-body) is developed.

4. **Kārikā 2 (bhinnayoravabhāso hi... prakāśasyeva nānyasya bhedinas).** The counterpart is possible where two divided things (jar and not-jar) both manifest (the māyā-word); but in the manifestation (prakāśa) no not-manifestation counterpart is possible, since to manifest is precisely to remove the not-manifestation. The virodha (opposition) is defined as the mutual-removal standing (anyonyaparihāra) — the saṃsṛjyante-na-bhidyante maxim, the ahinakula example, and the deśa/kāla of the virodha are all resolved to show that the pure manifestation has no possible counterpart.

5. **Kārikās 4–5 (the aham in the body/mind/breath/void).** The "I" that descends into the body ("the white I"), the mind ("the happy I"), the breath ("the hungry I"), or the conceived void ("the all-forms-free I") is a vikalpa — born of the manifestation of the other-counterpart (parapratiyogyavabhāsajaḥ). The pure cittattva, by the māyāśakti (not by mere avidyā — the Gītā's "anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu" is read as māyā, not ignorance-alone), is divided and descends; the prāṇa/puryaṣṭaka and the śūnya analysis show these are the contracted knower-states, not the pure aham. The Gītā 6.26 and the Spandakārikā 12 refute the abhāva-Brahmā view: the aham-manifestation is always-shining, not void.

**The crux.** V2-L establishes the apohanaśakti (removal power) as the operation of the reflexive-awareness in the māyā-word. The pure "I"-reflexive-awareness is not a construction — it is the word-bodied manifestation itself, a determination that excludes the twofold, with no possible counterpart (kārikās 1–2). The construction (vikalpa) is precisely the determination that operates with the counterpart — "this is a jar" removes the not-jar (kārikā 3). When the "I" descends into the body, mind, breath, or the void, it is a vikalpa born of the other-counterpart's manifestation (kārikās 4–5); only the pure cittattva, free of the māyā-contraction, is the un-constructed reflexive-awareness. This is the smṛti/apohana complement to the jñānaśakti: memory and construction are the one reflexive-awareness operating by removal in the māyā-word, and the recognition is their return to the pure aham.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.5.11 (*svabhāvamavabhāsasya vimarśaṃ*), 1.3.5 (*bhrāntitve cāvasāyasya*), 2.4.9 (*yad vyavahriyate yeṣāṃ ca virodhaḥ*), kārikās 1–5 of this vimarśa; the Bhaṭṭa (Kumārila) and Dharmottara (*saṃsṛṣṭapratibhāseti*, *viṣayavyāpāranirapekṣotpādatayā*); the Vākyapadīya 3.1.11 (*vyāpāralakṣaṇā yasmāt padārthāḥ*); the Sāṃkhyakārikā 29 (*sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca*); the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 (*yadyapyarthasthitiḥ prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite*); the Spandakārikā 12 (*nābhāvo bhāvyatāmeti*); the Gītā 6.26 (*śanaiḥ śanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā*); the "saṃsṛjyante na bhidyante" maxim. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi T3/C1 anchors the ahaṃ-prakāśa and the vimarśa-as-own-nature reading; the apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.
