## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-M)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-M = M00021 lines 9200–10000, the ṣaṣṭho vimarśa (the apohanaśakti,
   continued). It opens at the close of kārikā 5's commentary (the prāṇa/puryaṣṭaka, the
   suṣupta/turya, the māyā/anava/kārma malas; the ahaṃpratyaya as pure and impure, anubhava and
   anusandhāna; the Śivadṛṣṭi/Gītā/Spandakārikā citations; the Sāṃkhyakārikā 29 and Yogasūtra
   1.40); it then gives **kārikā 6** (*kādācitkāvabhāse yā pūrvābhāsādiyojanā saṃskārāt kalpanā
   proktā sāpi bhinnāvabhāsini* — the joining of the "this" from the prior appearance, by the
   impression, is the construction, resting in the different manifestations), with the aikyayojanā/
   pratyabhijñā (the shadow-made recognition) analysis, the cidadvayavāda (Vasugupta), the
   bālyayauvana and the body-states continuity; and **kārikā 7** (*tadevaṃ vyavahāre'pi prabhur
   dehādimāviśan bhāntam evāntararthaugham icchayā bhāsayet bahiḥ* — even in dealing, the Lord,
   entering the body etc., manifests the inner object-mass without, by the will), with the
   kṛtyapañcaka (sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra/tirodhāna/anugraha), the parameśvara as the self-manifesting
   knower, the two pratītis (the "I" and the "I-this"), the pure/mixed/unpure states, the māyāśakti
   as the source of the divided manifestation, and the kalā/vidyā (the action-range and the
   cognition-range of the divided knower). The chunk closes at the objection about the
   mantreśvaras and liberation (10000), which V2-N (10000–10385, the close of the ṣaṣṭho vimarśa
   \|\|6\|\|) answers.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-L.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal (the
   apohanaśakti = the removal power); vikalpa = construction; niścaya = determination; saṃśaya =
   doubt; pratiyogi = counterpart; anusandhāna = continuity; anubhava = experience; kāla = time;
   māyāśakti = the māyā-power; kalā/vidyā = (action-)range/(cognition-)range; suṣupta/turya =
   deep sleep/fourth state; puryaṣṭaka = the eight-fold inner body; icchā = will; kriyā = action;
   sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra/tirodhāna/anugraha = creation/maintenance/destruction/concealment/grace.
   The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 6 (kādācitkāvabhāse...).** The "this" of the construction is not the pure ahaṃ: it is
   the joining (yojanā) of a "this" from a prior appearance (the child-body with the youth-body,
   the name "Caitra" with the present "I", the hungry/thirsty/weak breath-states, the happy/
   unhappy mind-states, the limited/unlimited void-states), done by the impression (saṃskāra). The
   recognition (pratyabhijñā) that "this very is I" across the changing body-states is thus a
   construction resting in the different manifestations (bhinnāvabhāsini) — the counterpart
   (pratiyogi) is possible because the manifestations differ. The cidadvayavāda (Vasugupta) is
   invoked for the identity of consciousness across states; the pūrvānubhava/uddrikta and the
   sākṣātkāra-vs-smṛti distinction keep the pure ahaṃpratyaya free of the vikalpa.

4. **Kārikā 7 (tadevaṃ vyavahāre'pi...).** The Lord, whose param-essence is manifestation
   (prakāśaparamārthaḥ), by his lordship enters (āviśati) the body etc. as knower even in the
   māyā-word, makes them his own, and manifests the inner (antaḥ) object-mass without (bahiḥ), by
   the will (icchayā) alone — the inner-tool/outer-tool known-ground (antaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇavedyatā-
   bhūmi) receiving the idam in order, clear then unclear. The kṛtyapañcaka: the same Lord, always
   free, in the famous creation/maintenance/destruction/concealment/grace times AND in the
   unending dealing-times, enters the distinct knowers, builds the unity, maintains the state,
   destroys the prior knower-unity, shows the dissolution by enclosing his own dense form, and
   manifests the grace-portion (anugrahakalā) by the unity-entry. This is the "five-fold deed" as
   the apohanaśakti's self-unfolding; the "na asaṃbhāvyam etat" and the liṅ in the reason show the
   inconceivability is only apparent.

5. **The pure/mixed/unpure states and the two pratītis.** The pure state is the Śiva-ground
   (śuddhaśivabhūmi) where the ahaṃ (the anubhava-svabhāva) is un-constructed; the Sadāśiva-ground
   is the manobhūmi where "I-this" (aham idam) flashes un-divided; the māyā-ground is where the
   prakāśa-part is closed (nimīlita) and the beings appear as the divided. Abhinava reads the
   Sadāśiva/Īśvara states as the reflexive-awareness-primary and the manifestation-primary daśās;
   the distinction (bheda) between them is not a real object-distinction (the "nīlam asphuṭaṃ pītaṃ
   sphuṭam" example, the cviprayoga) — there is no excess or lack in the Lord. The time-distinction
   is only from the māyā-impression; in the Lord "with-which-form-not-does-it-shine" — the 
   "now-shines/previously-shone/will-shine" is all pure manifestation (śuddhabhāsanamātraparamārtha),
   like the mirror's clarity-unfolding (svacchatāvijṛmbhita). This grounds the viruddhavyāptopalabdhi
   (opposed-pervasion-apprehension) of ĪPK 1.3.2 (dṛk svābhāsaiva): the distinction-dealing is
   pervaded by the un-distinction-dealing.

6. **The kalā/vidyā and the māyāśakti.** The māyāśakti gives the self-ness (ātmatā) in the not-self
   and contracts the knower-ness; but by that much alone the contracted knower does not become the
   knower of the divided (nīlasukha): a pervader-non-apprehension (vyāpakānupalabdhi) shows that
   the mere knower-ness (pramātṛtāmātra) does not entail the divided-object consciousness — else
   the deep-sleep/fourth states would not be conceived. Hence something beyond the māyā is to be
   expected: the kalā (which, by the general operation, moves the divided action — the lame's
   walking-effort — and, specifically, the action-organs complete it) and the vidyā (which, by the
   general operation, grasps the divided object — the blind's tasting the juice — and, specifically,
   the cognition-organs complete it). The sva. 11.98 (kalodbalitacaitanyo vidyādarśitagocaraḥ) is
   the āgama anchor; the rāga/kāla (passion/time) are the upādhis (adjuncts), not the raisers, of
   jñatvakartṛtva (the knowing/acting). The kārikā 7 commentary here completes the transition: the
   "śuddhacidātmana" and "viśvanirmāṇecchoḥ" glosses fold the pure/mixed/unpure creation into the
   one manifesting Lord.

**The crux.** V2-M establishes the apohanaśakti's self-unfolding as the Lord's kṛtyapañcaka — the
same recognition-power by which the "this" is joined to the "I" across the changing body-states
(kārikā 6) is the power by which the free Lord, entering the distinct knowers as their
self-manifesting essence, builds, maintains, destroys, conceals, and graces the world by the will
alone (kārikā 7). The pure "I"-reflexive-awareness is never a construction; the construction is
always the joining of a prior appearance in the divided manifestations. When the Lord's manifestation
enters the māyā-ground the appearance is contracted and divided, and the kalā/vidyā (the action- and
cognition-ranges) are what make the divided dealing possible; but even there the object is only the
consciousness (saṃvideva viśvarūpā, na ghaṭaḥ kaścit svatantraḥ) — no free jar outside the
manifestation. The recognition is the return to the pure ahaṃ, and the whole creation/dealing is
the one prakāśa unfolding its own clarity.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.3.2 (*dṛk svābhāsaiva...*), 1.5.10 (*svāminaśca...*), 2.1.6
(*sarvatrābhāsabhedo'pi...*); the kārikās 5–7 of this ṣaṣṭho vimarśa; the Gītā 15.8
(*śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yaccāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ*); the Spandakārikā 8 (*apitu ātmabalasparśāt
puruṣastatsamo bhavet*); the Śivadṛṣṭi 1.12 (*pañcaprakārakṛtyoktiḥ śivatvān nijakarmaṇe*);
the Svacchandatantra 11.98 (*kalodbalitacaitanyo vidyādarśitagocaraḥ*); the Mālinīvijaya 2.45
(*uditaṃ vipulaṃ śāntaṃ suprasannam*); the "tena māyābhidhā śaktiḥ sahaiva kurute dvayam" verse
(the nareśvaraviveka); the Sāṃkhyakārikā 29; the Yogasūtra 1.40; the Vākyapadīya; the
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi parallel (the ahaṃ-prakāśa and the vimarśa-as-own-nature reading); the
"saṃsṛjyante na bhidyante" maxim. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha
parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-N: the close of the ṣaṣṭho vimarśa (the apohanaśaktividadhi) — kārikās 8–11 + the ||6|| colophon — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 10000–10385 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the sixth vimarśa (the apohanaśakti). Covers: kārikā 8 (evaṃ smṛtau vikalpe vāpyapohanaparāyaṇe jñāne vāpyantarābhāsaḥ sthita eveti niścitam — thus in memory, in construction, or in cognition, bent on removal, the inner appearance stands firm, it is determined); kārikā 9 (kintu naisargiko jñāne bahirābhāsanātmani pūrvānubhavarūpastu sthitaḥ sa smaraṇādiṣu — but in cognition whose form is the external manifestation, the prior-experience-formed [inner appearance] is innate, while it stands in memory etc.); kārikā 10 (sa naisargika evāsti vikalpe svairacāriṇi yathābhimatasaṃsthānābhāsanād buddhigocare — he is innate indeed in the freely-wandering construction, from the manifestation of the place-form as wished, in the mind's range); kārikā 11 (ata eva yathābhīṣṭasamullekhāvabhāsanāt jñānakriye sphuṭe eva siddhe sarvasya jīvataḥ — hence, from the manifestation of the uplifting as wished, knowledge and action are clear, established for every living one); and the ||6|| colophon (iti ... apohanaśaktivimarśaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ), which closes the apohanaśaktividadhi. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-N)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-N = M00021 lines 10000–10385, the CLOSE of the ṣaṣṭho vimarśa (the
   apohanaśaktividadhi). It opens mid-argument (the muktāṇava, mantreśvaras and their liberation
   — answering the objection raised at the end of V2-M), then gives kārikā 8 (*evaṃ smṛtau vikalpe
   vāpyapohanaparāyaṇe jñāne vāpyantarābhāsaḥ sthita eveti niścitam* — thus in memory, construction,
   or cognition, bent on removal, the inner appearance stands firm, it is determined), kārikā 9
   (*kintu naisargiko jñāne bahirābhāsanātmani pūrvānubhavarūpastu sthitaḥ sa smaraṇādiṣu* — but in
   cognition whose form is the external manifestation, the prior-experience-formed is innate, while
   it stands in memory etc.), kārikā 10 (*sa naisargika evāsti vikalpe svairacāriṇi yathābhimata-
   saṃsthānābhāsanād buddhigocare* — he is innate indeed in the freely-wandering construction), and
   kārikā 11 (*ata eva yathābhīṣṭasamullekhāvabhāsanāt jñānakriye sphuṭe eva siddhe sarvasya
   jīvataḥ* — hence from the manifestation of the uplifting as wished, knowledge and action are
   clear, established for every living one). The chunk ends at the ||6|| colophon
   (*iti ... apohanaśaktivimarśaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ*) at source line 10385, which closes the apohanaśakti
   vimarśa.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-M.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal (the
   apohanaśakti = the removal power); vikalpa = construction; niścaya = determination; saṃśaya =
   doubt; pratiyogi = counterpart; antarābhāsa = the inner appearance; bahirābhāsa = the external
   appearance; anusandhāna = continuity; anubhava = experience; saṃskāra/vāsanā = impression;
   kāla = time; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; kalā/vidyā = (action-)range/(cognition-)range;
   kṣetrajña = the field-knower; svaira = freely (own-will); svātantrya = freedom; naimittika/
   naisargika = occasioned/innate; svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya = own-marker/general. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 8 (evaṃ smṛtau...).** The three operations — memory (smṛti), construction (vikalpa),
   cognition (jñāna) — are all "bent on removal" (apohanaparāyaṇa): each operates with the
   counterpart, removing the not-object, and in each the inner appearance (antarābhāsa) stands firm
   (sthita eva). The sūtra confirms that the param-essence-knower (paramārthapramātṛ) alone knows,
   remembers, determines; the jar-appearances are in-truth inner-standing (antaḥsthitā eva). The
   objection that "this"-reflexive-awareness (idamitivimarśa) is the beings' flashing but not the
   "I"-reflexive-awareness is removed by the prāk (1.5.2) and ahaṃpratyavamarśa (1.6.1) sūtras,
   confirmed by the kakṣyāstotra verse (sarve'nubhūtā...). The vivṛti is "spaṣṭaprāya" — quite
   clear.

4. **Kārikā 9 (kintu naisargiko...).** In cognition whose form is the external manifestation
   (bahirābhāsanātma), the inner appearance's clarity (sphuṭatva) is innate (naisargika): the jar-
   appearance comes from the Lord's freedom (svātantryād ananyaśaraṇatayaiva) at the first seeing/
   first creation, and is therefore new (apūrva) and clear (sphuṭa). In memory and the rest it is
   not freedom-come but experience-impression-dependent — hence faded (parimlāna), like a worn
   garland (nirmālyakalpa), asphuṭa (unclear). The "sargadvaye'pi" (in both creations) shows the
   pure (Īśvara) and impure (māyā) creations; the "sahaja" (innate) is the Lord's own freedom-
   unfold. The objection that the param-Lord (avicchinnaprakāśavimarśasvātantryaparamārtha) cannot
   remember is removed: the same one, having adopted the field-knower-being (parigṛhīt kṣetrajñabhāva),
   remembers, determines, conjectures, removes — there is no third state beyond the Śiva-consciousness
   (sarvānuyāyinī saṃvit), so the kalā-power (kalāśaktī) makes the some-agent-ness and the double-moon
   delusions show the Īśvara-activity clear even in dealing.

5. **Kārikā 10 (sa naisargika evāsti...).** In the freely-wandering construction (svairacāriṇi
   vikalpe) — the mind-kingdom (manorājya) constructions that rise and set without other-prompting —
   the external manifestation of the inner appearance is innate (naisargika). The objection that
   even the cow-horse is prior-experience-object is answered by the elephant example (the three-
   hands, tooth-ten elephant): the place-form joining (saṃsthānayojanāṃśa) is experience-following,
   but the to-be-joined part (yojyamāna bhāga) is not — so the newness (navatva) of the innate
   appearance is fit. The construction is not Saugata-free (svatantra) in the object-part: the
   object's own-marker (svalakṣaṇa) is established by the pramāṇa as the pure manifestation, the
   nitya-vyāpaka general (sāmānya) spanning all time/place (this is the Pradyumna line). The
   ābhāsanakriyā (manifestation-action) is innate, unmediated, time-marked-clear — hence even the
   mountain-family (kulagiri) is newly created every moment (pratikṣaṇam aviśrāntaḥ, sta. ci. 112),
   so the always-creation (sadāsṛṣṭi) power belongs to the Lord. The svabhāvahetu: what manifests
   thus, that is param-essence-being, like the manifestation. The embryo objection (the first 'I'
   in the womb) is cut by svabhāvam avabhāsasya (1.5.11): the innate 'this'-reflexive-awareness,
   even without the 'i'-distinction, is possible as made (kṛtaka) — the idam is conventional.

6. **Kārikā 11 (ata eva yathābhīṣṭasamullekhāvabhāsanāt...).** From the manifestation of the
   uplifting (ullekha) as wished, the knowledge and action (jñānakriye) of every living one (from
   Brahmā to the worm) are established as clear — the jñāna is avabhāsanātmaka (manifestation-own)
   and the kriyā is svollekhanirmāṇarūpā (self-uplifting-creation-form), both by freedom. This is
   the adhikaraṇasiddhānta (nyā. sū. 1.1.30, yatsiddhāv anyaprakaraṇasiddhiḥ): the purpose of the
   śāstra is the Īśvara-form-recognition (īśvararūpatāpratyabhijñā) of one's own self, and the
   saṃvidśaktiprasaramātratā of the thirty-six tattvas (the Bhaṭṭa-Pradyumna doctrine) is its
   essence. The "aiśvarya" singular shows the param-essence non-dual alone, even in the māyā dual
   appearance. The "ata eva" carries the prior-sūtra's reason and achieves the additional object —
   the siddhisamuccaya (establishment-aggregation).

**The crux.** V2-N completes the apohanaśaktividadhi: memory, construction, and cognition are the
one reflexive-awareness operating by removal, and in all three the inner appearance stands firm
(kārikā 8). The clarity of the inner appearance in cognition is innate (freedom-born, new, clear);
in memory it is impression-born, faded (kārikā 9). Yet in the free construction too the innate
appearance operates — only the object's own-marker is never new, only the manifestation-action is
innate and ever-new (kārikā 10). From all this the recognition-conclusion: knowledge and action of
every living one are the free manifestation of the one Īśvara-self, which is the very purpose of
the śāstra (kārikā 11). The whole ṣaṣṭho vimarśa — the smṛti/apohana complement to the jñānaśakti —
is thus closed at ||6||, and the jñānādhikāra moves to the saptamo vimarśa (the śaktivargaikāśraya).

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.5.2 (*prāk...*), 1.5.7 (*cidātmaiva hi...*), 1.5.11 (*svabhāvam
avabhāsasya...*), 1.6.1 (*ahaṃpratyavamarśaḥ...*), 2.3.7 (*pṛthagdīpaprakāśānāṃ...*); the kakṣyāstotra
verse (*sarve'nubhūtā yadi nāntararthāḥ...*); the Spandakārikā 8 (*apitu ātmabalasparśāt...*);
the Stanzas on Vibration (sta. ci. 112, *pratikṣaṇam aviśrāntaḥ*); the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.30
(*yatsiddhāv anyaprakaraṇasiddhiḥ*); the pravṛttir jantūnāṃ aiśvarī; the buddhipūrvāṃ kriyāṃ dṛṣṭvā
maxim; the Bhaṭṭa-Pradyumna doctrine of the saṃvidśaktiprasaramātratā of the thirty-six tattvas;
the muktāṇava/mantreśvara/paśu liberation hierarchy. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the
Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-O: the saptamo vimarśa — the śaktivargaikāśraya (the one-support of the powers' group) — kārikās 1–? — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 10385–11200 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the seventh vimarśa (atha saptamo vimarśaḥ), the maṅgala (svaprasarapreṅkhitavilasadūrmisaṃkṣubhitacidrasāpūram...), the support (āśraya) of the powers. Covers: the opening maṅgala; the sūtrārthāvatāra (the 14-verse plan: 1 for the support's own form, 2 for the anvaya-vyatireka, 1 for the vyavahāra, 1 for the smaraṇalakṣaṇa, 8 for the sarvavyavahāra, 1 for the nigamana); kārikā 1 (yā caiṣā pratibhā tattatpadārthakramarūṣitā akramānantacidrūpaḥ pramātā sa maheśvaraḥ — this pratibhā, seasoned with the order of the various word-objects, the order-less-infinite-consciousness-form knower, he is the great Lord); kārikā 2 (tattadvibhinnasaṃvittimukhairekapramātari pratitiṣṭhatsu bhāveṣu jñāteyamupapadyate — with the faces of the various divided consciousnesses, in the objects resting in the one knower, the cognition-aggregation is fit); and the anvaya/vyatireka argument, the jñāteya (cognition-aggregation) as the vyavahāra, the Bhaṭṭa-Candrānanda and the samanvaya. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-O)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-O = M00021 lines 10385–11200, the opening of the saptamo vimarśa
   (atha saptamo vimarśaḥ), the śaktivargaikāśraya (the one-support of the powers' group). It
   contains the maṅgala (svaprasarapreṅkhita...), the sūtrārthāvatāra (the 14-verse plan), and the
   first several kārikās of this vimarśa, together with their commentary: kārikā 1 (yā caiṣā
   pratibhā tattatpadārthakramarūṣitā akramānantacidrūpaḥ pramātā sa maheśvaraḥ — this pratibhā,
   seasoned with the order of the various word-objects, the order-less-infinite-consciousness-form
   knower, he is the great Lord); kārikā 2 (tattadvibhinnasaṃvittimukhairekapramātari pratitiṣṭhatsu
   bhāveṣu jñāteyamupapadyate — with the faces of the various divided consciousnesses, in the
   objects resting in the one knower, the cognition-aggregation is fit); kārikā 3 (deśakālakramajuṣām
   arthānāṃ svasamāpinām sakṛdābhāsasādhyo'sāv anyathā kaḥ samanvayaḥ — of the objects enjoying the
   order of place and time, converging in themselves, that is attainable by the once-manifestation,
   otherwise which conjunction?); kārikā 4 (pratyakṣānupalambhānāṃ tattadbhinnāṃśapātinām
   kāryakāraṇatāsiddhihetur ekapramātṛjā — of the perception and non-apprehension falling in the
   various divided parts, the cause-effect-ness-establishment-reason is the one knower-born); and
   the long commentary on the samanvaya (conjunction) as the vyavahāra, the jñāteya, the kāryakāraṇa
   bhāva, the relation (saṃbandha) as the distinction-un-distinction, the paurvāparya, the will
   (icchā/kāmanā) as the supporter of all dealing, and the pramāṇa/prāmāṇya analysis. The chunk
   ends at the objection about the ahaṃpratyavamarśa (11200), which V2-P answers.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-N.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal;
   vikalpa = construction; niścaya/avasāya = determination; pratiyogi = counterpart; anusandhāna =
   continuity; anubhava = experience; saṃskāra/vāsanā = impression; kāla = time; māyāśakti = the
   māyā-power; kalā/vidyā = (action-)range/(cognition-)range; icchā = will; kriyā = action;
   samanvaya = conjunction; saṃbandha = relation; jñāteya = cognition-aggregation; vyavahāra =
   dealing; kāryakāraṇabhāva = effect-cause-being; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti = valid-means/known/
   result-of-knowing; prāmāṇya = validity; prāpaka = the reacher; svaprakāśa = self-manifesting;
   śaktivargaikāśraya = the one-support of the powers' group. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light"
   variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 1 (yā caiṣā pratibhā...).** The pratibhā (the immediate flash of the object-word-order,
   "shines-the-jar") is the manifestation, and though it seems to cling to the object, it is not the
   object's own light (svajyotiḥ): it is the consciousness (saṃvedana) that flashes "to me" — i.e.,
   it is the knower-resting (pramātṛniṣṭha). The ka. u. 5.15 (tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam) and
   the Bhaṭṭa-Candrānanda verse anchor this. The akrama-anantacidrūpaḥ pramātā (the order-less,
   infinite-consciousness-form knower) is the great Lord (maheśvaraḥ) — the pure
   ahaṃpratyavamarśamaya — whose freedom (svātantrya) raises the deśakālaparipāṭī (the place-time
   order) that "seasons" (rūṣitā) the pratibhā. The inner-turned form (antarmukha vapuṣā) is
   order-less, so the support (āśraya) is established without further effort (ayatnasiddha).

4. **Kārikā 2 (tattadvibhinnasaṃvittimukhaiḥ...).** The consciousness-resident establishments of
   the objects are not just the resting (viśramaṇa) in the divided cognitions — that would not
   establish the dealing (vyavahāra). It is when the various divided consciousnesses, ending in
   determination (niścayāntāḥ), are led as so many stream-faces (mukhāni) by the force (haṭhavāhena)
   into the one great consciousness-ocean as "I" (aham) that the cognition-aggregation (jñāteya) —
   the mutual servant/effect-cause relations, the samanvaya as the vyavahāra — becomes fit. The
   "yāvat"/"tad" and the aikadhyam point to the knower-fit (pramātṛrucita) partial simultaneity; the
   Sāṃkhya objection (the divided puruṣas in liberation) is announced. The saptamī-samāsa vs
   karmadhāraya and the bhāvavācinyā/kriyāvācinyā distinction are resolved.

5. **Kārikās 3–4 (deśakālakramajuṣāṃ...; pratyakṣānupalambhānāṃ...).** Without the one-knower-rest,
   the objects (blue, pleasure, their knowledges, their determinations), divided in place, time and
   order and fixed in their own form, have no conjunction: the samanvaya is only attainable by the
   once-manifestation (sakṛdābhāsa) that joins place-time-own-form in a unity-appearance. The
   effect-cause-being (kāryakāraṇabhāva) that the Buddhist establishes from the fivefold
   perception/non-apprehension is shown to be only their wish (manorathamātra): the prātipadika-
   meaning-only determinations (fire, smoke, fire-absence, smoke-absence) fall in different parts and
   cannot, by the apekṣālakṣaṇa alone, establish the anvaya-vyatireka truth. In our view the
   prameyas, stirred/rested in the one consciousness-ocean, are united and raised by the knower's
   freedom; the kāryatā is the thus-manifested-ness, the kāraṇatā the thus-manifestation.

6. **The saṃbandha (relation) and the pramāṇa/prāmāṇya.** The relation is not a separate real
   feature: it is the distinction-un-distinction (bhedābheda) appearance — the same form is
   distinguished by its counterpart (pratiyogi) and unified in the one manifestation. The connection
   (saṃbandha) spans the mutual-help (upakāryopakāraka), the expectation (apekṣā), and the dependence
   (pāratantrya), all rooted in the one knower. The pramāṇa (valid means) is not a separate agent
   working independently of the knower: it is prāpaka (the reacher) only as the knower's operation
   (pramātṛvyāpāra) — the reaching (prāpti) needs the prior memory (smaraṇād abhilāṣeṇa) and the
   will, which only the free knower's own-consciousness supplies. The Buddhists themselves, by
   accepting svasaṃvedana, are forced to accept the pramātṛtattva (the aśakyasamayo hy ātmā verse).
   The kāryakāraṇabhāva established from the external is refuted: the fire's prior-ness and the
   smoke's posterior-ness are never grasped as a distinct feature by the own-form-grasping cognition.

**The crux.** V2-O opens the saptamo vimarśa — the one-support (āśraya) of the powers' group: the
great Lord (maheśvara) is the order-less, infinite-consciousness-form knower, the pure
ahaṃpratyavamarśamaya, whose freedom raises the entire deśakāla order that seasons the pratibhā
(kārikā 1). The dealing (vyavahāra) and the cognition-aggregation (jñāteya) are fit only when the
divided consciousnesses rest in that one knower (kārikā 2); the conjunction (samanvaya) is only
attainable by the once-manifestation in that one knower (kārikā 3); and even the effect-cause-being,
which the Buddhist claims to establish from the perception/non-apprehension fivefold, is really
only the one-knower-born manifestation (kārikā 4). The relation (saṃbandha) is the distinction-
un-distinction appearance rooted in the free knower, and the pramāṇa is prāpaka only as that
knower's operation. This is the apohanaśakti's own ground: the powers find their support, and the
recognition (pratyabhijñā) of the Lord as the one knower is the śāstra's purpose.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.7.1–1.7.4 (the four kārikās of this chunk: yā caiṣā pratibhā; tattadvibhinna-
saṃvittimukhaiḥ; deśakālakramajuṣāṃ; pratyakṣānupalambhānāṃ), ĪPK 1.3.7 (*na ced antaḥkṛtā...*), 1.2.6 (*tato bhinneṣu dharmeṣu...*), 1.5.21
(*kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya...*), 1.6.9 (*kintu naisargikaḥ...*), 2.1.4 (*kramo bhedāśrayo...*), 2.2.1
(*kriyāsaṃbandha...*), 2.4.3/2.4.4/2.4.19; the Ka. U. 5.15 (*tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam*); the
Bhaṭṭa-Candrānanda verse (*paśyato rūpam ālekhāt...*); the Gītā 17.3 (*śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣaḥ*);
the Spandakārikā 17; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 23 (*uktā ca saiva viśrāntiḥ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ*);
the lelihānā sadā devī āgama verse; the bhūtabhavyāsamuccāraṇa rule; the "bhinnā apy ekatāṃ yānti"
maxim; the "smaraṇād abhilāṣeṇa" and "taddṛṣṭāv eva dṛṣṭeṣu smaraṇāt" Nyāya rules; the
aśakyasamayo hy ātmā Saugata verse; the saṃketakaraṇa/svabhāvaviruddhakāryopalabdhi analysis.
The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's
refutation of the external.

# IPVV Vol 2 — Chunk V2-P: the saptamo vimarśa (the śaktivargaikāśraya) — kārikās 5–10 — T1

*Source: M00021 lines 11200–12000 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the seventh vimarśa. Covers: kārikā 5 (smṛtau yaiva svasaṃvittiḥ pramāṇaṃ svātmasaṃbhave pūrvānubhavasadbhāve sādhanaṃ saiva nāparam — in memory, that very self-consciousness is the valid means in the self's birth; in the prior-experience-being it is the proof, that alone, not another); kārikā 6 (the smṛti/anusandhāna as the pramātraikyasādhana); the jñāteya/samanvaya and the pramāṇa as the pramātṛvyāpāra; the saṃvittis and their one-knower unification; kārikā 7 (the antarābhāsa as the pramāṇa); kārikā 8 (the vyavahāra as the saṃvedana); kārikās 9–10. The Pradyumna line and the ābhāsanakriyā continue. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

   another); kārikā 6 (*bādhyabādhakabhāvo'pi svātmaniṣṭhāvirodhinām jñānānām udiyād
   ekapramātṛpariniṣṭhiteḥ* — the refuted-refuter relation too, of the knower-resting non-opposed
   cognitions, let it rise from the one-knower full-establishment); kārikā 7 (*viviktabhūtalajñānaṃ
   ghaṭābhāvam atir yathā tathā ced ... śuktikājñānaṃ rupyajñānāpramātvavit* — the clear-ground
   cognition, as the jar-non-being, so if the shell-cognition, the silver-cognition's non-validity
   it would be); kārikā 8 (*naivaṃ śuddhasthalajñānāt sidhyet tasyāghaṭātmatā ...*); kārikā 9
   (*viviktaṃ bhūtalaṃ śaśvad ...*); kārikā 10 (*kintvālokacayo'ndhasya sparśo voṣṇādiko mṛduḥ
   tatrāsti sādhayet tasya svajñānam aghaṭātmatām*); and kārikā 11 (*piśācaḥ syādanāloko'py
   ālokābhyantare yathā adṛśyo bhūtalasyāntar niṣedhyaḥ sa sarvathā*). The chunk ends at source
   12000 (the piśāca/āloka atom analysis), which V2-Q (12000–12423, the close of the saptamo
   vimarśa \|\|7\|\|) continues.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-O.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal;
   vikalpa = construction; niścaya/avasāya = determination; pratiyogi = counterpart; anusandhāna =
   continuity; anubhava = experience; saṃskāra/vāsanā = impression; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti =
   valid-means/known/result-of-knowing; prāmāṇya = validity; prāpaka = the reacher; svasaṃvedana =
   self-consciousness; svaprakāśa = self-manifesting; bādhya/bādhaka = the refuted/refuter;
   saṃvāda = agreement; kāryakāraṇabhāva = effect-cause-being; vyatireka/tādātmya =
   absence/identity; jñāteya = cognition-aggregation; vyavahāra = dealing; samanvaya = conjunction;
   saṃbandha = relation; ghaṭābhāva = the jar-non-being; piśāca = the goblin; svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya =
   own-marker/general. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 5 (smṛtau yaiva...).** In memory, the prior experience does not appear separately as a
   known (it is past, its object gone); it appears only as the un-divided self-consciousness that
   announces the memory's own being. Neither the experience's own consciousness nor the memory (by
   itself, or as object) is the valid means of the prior-experience's being: only the one
   self-consciousness (svasaṃvedana), un-broken across time, is — and that is the knower-essence
   (pramātṛtattva). The memory, being past-time-stained (gṛhītagrāhitva), is non-valid; the
   self-consciousness, being time-cut-free (antarmukhe kālāvacchedavirahāt), is valid. The
   "mayā ghaṭo'nubhūtaḥ" cognition is not denied but confirmed; the middle side (that the proof is
   non-distinct from the memory's self-consciousness) is established.

4. **Kārikā 6 (bādhyabādhakabhāvo'pi...).** Even the refuted-refuter relation between cognitions
   rests on the one knower. The Buddhist's opposition (virodha) by co-absence, by destruction, by
   other-room, by other-valid-means — each fails or is only apparent. The shell/silver example: the
   cognition "this is shell, not silver" destroys the prior "this silver is true and object-action-
   capable" cognition's result-continuation, and rests — only because both rest in the one free
   knower (pramātā svatantraḥ). The bādhyatā of the to-be-abandoned and the bādhakatā of the
   abandonee follow by the svabhāvahetu and the viruddhavyāptopalabdhi. The Bhaṭṭa view (that the
   shell-support alone produces the silver-consciousness) is dismissed: without the one knower the
   one-support is unknowable. The pramāṇalakṣaṇa sūtra (2.3.2, so'ntastathāvimarśātmā...) is
   invoked.

5. **Kārikās 7–11 (the bādha as the abhāva; viviktabhūtala; kintvāloka; piśāca).** The main
   argument: the bādha (refutation) of the silver-cognition is not a separate cognition of a
   distinct non-being (vyatiriktābhāva) — it is the same cognition "this is shell" whose conformity
   (yathārthatā) is itself the announcement of the silver-cognition's non-validity. The ground/jar
   example is analogized: the pure-ground cognition is the jar-non-being cognition because the
   jar's non-being is nothing other than the pure ground's own manifestation (tādātmya), not a
   distinct object. Kārikā 9 (viviktaṃ bhūtalaṃ śaśvad) fixes the ground's clarity as its
   own-self-resting (svātmaniṣṭhatā) — it is always the same, so it cannot prove the non-being of a
   distinct (bhinnasya) jar except by identity. Kārikā 10 (kintvālokacayo...) gives the positive
   account: the light-mass / the warm-soft-touch IS the ground's own form, and it is that (not a
   distinct non-being) which the own-cognition proves to be jar-less (aghaṭātmatā) — the
   vyatiriktābhāva is the light/touch itself, dealt by the tādātmya. Kārikā 11 (piśācaḥ...) answers
   the objection that then any absence (the goblin's) would be the light's: the goblin is not a
   part of the light's own form (un-light, extra-sensory), so its non-being cannot be established by
   the light's identity; the sarvathā (in all ways) is the niyama (rule) restricting the absence to
   the known own-form.

**The crux.** V2-P completes the argument that the bādha (refutation/opposition) and the abhāva
(non-being) are not separate realities but the operations of the one free knower's self-consciousness.
Memory is valid only by the un-broken self-consciousness that is the knower-essence (kārikā 5); the
refuted-refuter relation between cognitions rests only in that one knower (kārikā 6); the bādha of
the silver-cognition is not a distinct non-being but the very conformity of the shell-cognition
(kārikā 7); the pure ground never proves a distinct non-being except by identity (kārikā 8–9); the
positive absence is the own-form (light/touch) dealt by identity (kārikā 10); and only what is part
of the own-form can be negated, the goblin being excluded by the niyama (kārikā 11). The whole
ṣaṣṭho/saptamo vimarśa argument converges: the dealing, the relation, the effect-cause-being, the
memory, the bādha, and the abhāva are all the one pramātṛ's freedom — the pramāṇa is prāpaka only
as the knower's operation, and the recognition (pratyabhijñā) of the Lord as that one knower is the
śāstra's purpose.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.7.5–1.7.11 (the seven kārikās of this chunk), 1.7.4 (*pratyakṣā...*),
1.7.12 (*evaṃ rupyavidā...*), 1.7.13 (*dharmyasiddherapi...*), 2.3.2 (*so'ntastathāvimarśātmā...*),
2.3.5 (*tathaiva sat...*); the Śrīmukuṭasaṃhitā verse (*saṃvidvyāpāra evaikā yuktiḥ sarvatra
sādhanī*); the Bhaṭṭa verse (*kāryaucityāt prāksvasaṃvid asaṃvitsmaraṇāntare*); the Abhidharmakośa
1.10 (*rūpaṃ tadā viṃśatidhā*); the "smaraṇād abhilāṣeṇa" and "taddṛṣṭāv eva dṛṣṭeṣu smaraṇāt"
Nyāya rules; the Dharmottara bādha account; the "abhāvo'pi budhyamāno bodhātmabhūta īśvara eva"
maxim; the ātmacakra/piśāca analysis; the kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi and vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi
inference-forms. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the
pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-Q)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-Q = M00021 lines 12000–12423, the CLOSE of the saptamo vimarśa (the
   śaktivargaikāśraya). It opens mid-kārikā-11 (the piśāca/āloka atom analysis, the arvāgdarśana vs
   the sarvajña), then gives kārikā 12 (*evaṃ rupyavidābhāvarūpā śuktimatir bhavet na tv ādyarajatajñapter
   syād aprāmāṇyavedikā* — thus the shell-cognition would be the silver-seer-non-being-form, but it
   would not be the cognizer of the first silver-cognition's non-validity), kārikā 13 (*dharmyasiddher
   api bhaved bādhā naivānumānataḥ svasaṃvedanasiddhā tu yuktā saikapramātṛjā* — from the property's-
   non-establishment too the refutation would not be by inference; but the self-consciousness-
   established, the one-knower-born, is fit), and kārikā 14 (*ittham atyarthabhinnārthāvabhāsakhacite
   vibhau samalo vimalo vāpi vyavahāro'nubhūyate* — thus in the pervader studded with the appearances
   of the utterly distinct objects, the stained or the stainless dealing is experienced). The chunk
   ends at the ||7|| colophon (*iti ... śaktivargaikāśrayavimarśaḥ saptamaḥ*) at source 12423, which
   closes the saptamo vimarśa.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-P.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; apohana = removal;
   vikalpa = construction; niścaya/avasāya = determination; pratiyogi = counterpart; pramāṇa/prameya/
   pramiti = valid-means/known/result; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana = self-consciousness;
   svaprakāśa = self-manifesting; bādhya/bādhaka = the refuted/refuter; saṃvāda = agreement;
   virodha = opposition; kāryakāraṇabhāva = effect-cause-being; vyatireka/tādātmya =
   absence/identity; abhāva = non-being; dharmin/hetu/sādhya = property/reason/object;
   āśrayāsiddhi/vyadhikaraṇāsiddhi = support-non-establishment/distinct-locus-non-establishment;
   arvāgdarśa/sarvajña = the near-seer/the all-knower; piśāca = the goblin; paramāṇu = atom;
   samalo/vimalo vyavahāra = the stained/stainless dealing; māyāndha = the māyā-blind; vidyeśvara/
   mantramaheśvara/mantreśvara = the vidyā-lords/mantra-great-lords/mantra-lords. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 11 continued (the piśāca/āloka atoms).** The goblin (piśāca) is not part of the
   light's own form: it is un-light (anāloka) and extra-sensory, so its non-being cannot be
   established by the light's identity. The light's atoms, being seen, are the ground's own-form and
   can be negated (the jar's non-being is the light's own-form dealt by identity); but the goblin's
   atoms, if any, would be un-seen like the smell/taste/touch atoms (Dharmottara's bāhyārthasiddhi)
   and cannot be excluded by the near-seer's perception. Only the all-knower (sarvajña), by the
   extra-sensory grasp and the rule (niyama), can negate the goblin — and even so the negation is
   the rule-bound absence, not a distinct object. The kārikā's "sarvathā" is the niyama restricting
   the absence to the known own-form.

4. **Kārikā 12 (evaṃ rupyavidābhāvarūpā...).** The shell-cognition (śuktijñāna) is indeed the
   silver-seer-non-being-form (it is the conformity/validity-consciousness of the shell, which is
   the non-validity of the silver-cognition's object-form). But it is NOT the cognizer of the
   validity-less-ness of the *first* (ādyarajata) silver-cognition as a distinct cognition: the
   reflection only concerns the shell-cognition's own form (svarūpacintā), and does not break or
   adorn anything of the distinct prior silver-cognition. The sūtrārtha: in the jar-cognition's
   validity, the prior cloth-cognition's non-validity being known does not do anything to the prior
   cloth-cognition itself.

5. **Kārikā 13 (dharmyasiddherapi...).** The Buddhist's inference-based refutation fails both
   because the reason (hetu) is un-established and because the property (dharmin) is un-established
   (the vyadhikaraṇāsiddhi). The shell-cognition's truth (śuktijñānasatyatva) is own-form-shining
   (svarūpeṇa bhāty eva) but not established in the distinct locus of the current silver-cognition,
   so the siddhasādhya (established-object) flaw follows. The pramāṇavārtika 3.249 (aśakyasamayo hy
   ātmā) is invoked: the self-consciousness is un-constructed (avikalpa), hence cannot be the
   dharmin of an inference. In our view the bādhā is established by the self-consciousness alone
   (svasaṃvedanasiddhā), born of the one free knower (ekapramātṛjā): the shell-cognition's own-
   consciousness, at its limit, is already the silver-cognition's own-consciousness (the māyā-stain
   removed), and this is what destroys the silver-cognition's result-continuation. The
   virodhasaṃvāda (opposition-agreement), the svabhāvahetu, and the vipakṣe ākasmikatva establish
   the pervasion.

6. **Kārikā 14 (ittham atyarthabhinnārthāvabhāsakhacite...).** The closing verse: in the pervader
   (vibhu), the free Lord, whose consciousness-essence is un-cut by place/time, studded with the
   appearances of the utterly distinct objects (the māyā-power-conceived blue/pleasure objects,
   non-distinct reflections), every dealing rests and is determined by the firm experience-valid-
   means. It is twofold: the stained (samala) dealing of the māyā-blind (the buy-sell-quarrel etc.),
   and the stainless (vimala) dealing of the recognized (pratyabhijñāta) selves — the vīreśas, the
   vidyeśvaras, the mantra-maheśvaras, the mantreśvaras, the niṣkalas — whose dealing is the
   purification-awakening (malaśodhanabodhana) and therefore stainless, though while the mala-remainder
   stands it still has the bhedābheda conjunction-form. The Śivavijñānopaniṣad (vi. bhai. 106) and the
   Mālinīvijaya 1.36 anchor this. The Śivabhaṭṭāraka is the rest-word (viśrāntipadam) of all dealings.

**The crux.** V2-Q closes the saptamo vimarśa: the bādha (refutation) and the abhāva (non-being) are
not separate realities and are not established by perception or inference — they are established by
the self-consciousness alone, as the operation of the one free knower (kārikā 13). The positive
absence is the own-form (light/touch, or for the sarvajña the rule-bound exclusion), and only what
is part of the own-form can be negated (kārikā 11). The shell-cognition's non-validity of the silver
is the identity-non-being, not a cognition of a distinct prior silver-cognition's non-validity
(kārikā 12). And finally, every dealing — stained or stainless — rests in the pervader, the free
Lord, the one knower, whose recognition (pratyabhijñā) is the purpose of the śāstra (kārikā 14). The
saptamo vimarśa (the śaktivargaikāśraya) is closed at ||7||, and the jñānādhikāra moves to the
aṣṭamo vimarśa (the māheśvarya).

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.7.10 (*... svajñānam aghaṭātmatām*), 1.7.11–1.7.14 (the four kārikās of
this chunk: piśācaḥ; evaṃ rupyavidā; dharmyasiddherapi; ittham atyarthabhinnārthāvabhāsakhacite),
1.7.2 (*tattadvibhinna...*); the Pramāṇavārtika 3.249 (*aśakyasamayo hy ātmā...*); the
Abhidharmakośa 1.10; the "śabdārthas trividho dharmī bhāvābhāvobhayāśrayaḥ" maxim; the
Vijñānabhairava 106 (*grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām*); the Mālinīvijaya 1.36
(*avasthātritaye'py asmiṃs tirobhāvanaśīlayā*); the Dharmottara bāhyārthasiddhi (the smell/taste/
touch atoms); the "abhāvo'pi budhyamāno bodhātmabhūta īśvara eva" maxim; the āśrayāsiddhi/
vyadhikaraṇāsiddhi and the pakṣadharmatā analysis. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the
Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.

## The aṣṭamo vimarśa opens: the maṅgala, the māheśvarya, the 11-verse plan

**The eighth vimarśa (atha aṣṭamo vimarśaḥ).**

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-R)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-R = M00021 lines 12423–13200, the opening of the aṣṭamo vimarśa (the
   māheśvarya, the great-Lordship), the last vimarśa of the jñānādhikāra. It contains the maṅgala
   (pūrvaṃ yad anuttaram amṛtabhūmim āsādya saptamīṃ kalanāṃ...), the 11-verse plan (of which this
   chunk gives the first nine), and the jñānaviṣayaṃ māheśvaryaṃ: kārikā 1 (tātkālikākṣasāmakṣya-
   sāpekṣāḥ kevalaṃ kvacit ābhāsā anyathānyatra tv andhāndhatamasādiṣu — the appearances, dependent
   on the at-that-time eye co-presence, only somewhere, otherwise elsewhere in the blind/utter-dark);
   kārikā 2 (viśeṣo'rthāvabhāsasya sattāyāṃ na punaḥ kvacit vikalpeṣu bhaved bhāvibhavadbhūtārthagāmiṣu —
   the distinction of the object-manifestation in being-ness, not anywhere again, would be in the
   constructions going to the future/present/past objects); kārikā 3 (sukhādiṣu ca saukhyādihetuṣv
   api ca vastuṣu...); kārikā 4 (gāḍham ullikhyamāne tu vikalpena sukhādike...); kārikā 5
   (bhāvābhāvāvabhāsānāṃ bāhyatopādhiriṣyate nātmā sattā tatasteṣām āntarāṇāṃ satāṃ sadā — for the
   being-non-being manifestations, the external-ness is declared an adjunct, not the self-being-ness,
   hence of them, the inner ones, the being is always); kārikā 6 (āntaratvāt pramātraikye naiṣāṃ
   bhedanibandhanā arthakriyāpi bāhyatve sā bhinnābhāsabhedataḥ); kārikā 7 (cinmayatve'vabhāsānām
   antareva sthitiḥ sadā māyayābhāsamānānāṃ bāhyatvād bahir api asau); kārikā 8 (vikalpe yo'yam
   ullekhaḥ so'pi bāhyaḥ pṛthakprathaḥ pramātraikātmyam āntaryaṃ tato bhedo'pi bāhyatā — in the
   construction, this uplifting, it too is external, the separate-manifestation; the knower-unity-
   inner-ness, hence the distinction too is the external-ness); and kārikā 9 (ullekhasya sukhādeś ca
   prakāśo bahirātmanā icchāto bharturadhyakṣarūpo'kṣyādibhuvāṃ yathā — of the uplifting and the
   pleasure-and-the-rest, the manifestation with the external self, from the will of the Lord, the
   eye-form, as in the eye-and-the-rest grounds). The chunk ends at source 13200 (the kārikā-9
   colophon at 13202), which V2-S (13200–13405, the close of the aṣṭamo vimarśa and the whole
   jñānādhikāra) continues.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-Q.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; vikalpa = construction;
   niścaya/avasāya = determination; pratiyogi = counterpart; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti = valid-means/
   known/result; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana = self-consciousness; svaprakāśa = self-manifesting;
   bāhya/bāhyatā = external/external-ness; āntara/āntaratva = inner/inner-ness; grāhya/grāhyatva =
   grasped/grasped-ness; arthakriyā = object-action; bhāva/abhāva = being/non-being; saṃskāra =
   impression; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; parameśvara/maheśvara = the param-Lord/great-Lord;
   ahaṃvimarśa = the I-reflexive-awareness; idam = this; viśrānti = rest; viccheda = the cut;
   sattā = being-ness; pramātṛ = the knower. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain
   retired.

3. **The māheśvarya (great-Lordship) and the 11-verse plan.** The aṣṭamo vimarśa determines the
   maheśvara: the māheśvarya is twofold — jñānaviṣaya (knowledge-object) and kriyāviṣaya (action-
   object); the former is determined here in the jñānādhikāra. The 11-verse plan (per the
   sūtrārthāvatāra): verse 1 says the appearance sometimes depends on the eye's co-presence,
   sometimes not; verse 2 that it is still one appearance; verses 3–4 the arthakriyā-appearance too
   is appearance-fixed and where; verse 5 the appearance-other-variety (the wall-conception);
   verses 6–7 the external-ness by own-form and by distinction; verse 8 the upasaṃhāra of the
   knowledge-power-support; and the summarizing verse introducing the future action-section. This
   chunk covers kārikās 1–9.

4. **Kārikā 1 (tātkālikākṣa...).** The appearances that depend on the at-that-time eye co-presence
   (the perception and the immediately-following construction) occur only somewhere; elsewhere (in
   the blind, the utter-dark) they do not depend on the present eye but on the long-happened
   impression (ciravṛttasaṃskāra). The "kevalam" (only) marks the sūtrārthāvatāra's addition: the
   dealing in the Lord is all, and only here the to-be-said-other. The atoms (aṇu), the recognized
   selves (pratyabhijñātātman, the mahāmantreśvaras) whose appearances always shine "I", are fixed by
   the niyatiśakti.

5. **Kārikā 2 (viśeṣo'rthāvabhāsasya...).** In being-ness (sattā), the object-manifestation has no
   distinction anywhere: whether the construction goes to the future, present, or past object, the
   manifestation's existing-ness is the one always-shining (sadātana prakāśa), grasped by the
   "I"-reflexive-awareness (ahamity āmarśa). The "nīlaṃ paśyāmi / utprekṣe / smarāmi" are one blue-
   appearance; the variety in the māyā-knowers is only the joining/unjoining of the appearances. The
   saṃskāra-named appearance (the impression-form pratibhāsa) is the beings' "I"-ness teaching, but
   it is not the pure ahaṃpada (it is varaṇamayatā, covering-natured); the bahiṣkārya (external-
   making) is the "this"-manifestation of the I-one-self's covering.

6. **Kārikās 3–4 (sukhādiṣu; gāḍham).** In the pleasure-and-the-rest and their causes, the
   manifestation, though existing, is past (atīta), hence the standing differs. The pleasure-
   appearances are present with the I-ness but not in it as the present; the past-ness alone fits
   them (they always have occurred, even in the prior birth). The present-ness is the external-
   resting. Kārikā 4: when the construction intensely uplifts the (past) pleasure, the standing at
   the end is the utter-pleasure-form — because it is then presented as present (pratyupasthāpita),
   not remembered (the memory is asphuṭa). The meditation (dhyāna) of the nectar-stream, the kanda-
   suṣumṇā entry, the attachment (āsaṅga), the adṛṣṭa, are the "kutaścit" (from-something) reasons.
   The kāryakāri (object-action-doing) of the pleasure is full even if its past object was unreal:
   the pṛthivīkṛtsnā meditation, the bhāvitā, even the asatya, still accomplish the arthakriyā.

7. **Kārikā 5 (bhāvābhāvāvabhāsānāṃ...).** The external-ness is not the self (ātmā/own-form) of the
   being or non-being manifestations — it is an adjunct (upādhi), the other-appearance-nature, the
   stain-qualifier (uparāganimitta viśeṣaṇa). Their being-ness is always-inner (āntarāṇāṃ sadā
   sattā). The non-being (abhāva) is not a nothing: the jar's non-being is the jar-itself-thus
   (ghaṭa eva tathābhūtaḥ), the tucchatā (emptiness) belongs to the jar, and the world's
   distaste at losing wealth shows the abhāva is a real object. Even the yogi-cognition of the
   past/future (the prāgabhāva, pradhvaṃsābhāva) is real. In our view the prakāśanamātrasāratva (the
   manifestation-mere-essence) is the beings' form: the abhāvātmaka form too manifests. The
   śaśaviṣāṇa (hare's-horn) is the atyantābhāva ("the hare's-horn does not become"), not a mere
   conceptual (sāṅkalpika) like jar-cloth. The "te tu" (they however) = the abhāvas shine by the
   re-reflexive-awareness-niścaya (pratyavamarśasāraniścayātmanā).

8. **Kārikās 6–7 (āntaratvāt; cinmayatve).** In the knower-unity (pramātraikya) the inner-ness means
   no bhedanibandhanā arthakriyā (no distinction-grounded object-action): the object-action is
   appearance-fixed (ābhāsaniyata), and in the inner state there is no bheda. Kārikā 7: since the
   manifestations are consciousness-made (cinmaya), their standing is inner-alone always; only by the
   māyā (the freedom-marker māyāśakti) is the external-ness manifested, and then the standing is
   both outside and inside — but the inner-manifestation of the external-manifestation-cognition
   (the wall, bhittikalpa) is not opposed (like the blue-ness vs the momentariness; the kalpitānyonya-
   parihāra is not pāramārthika). The anubhava is the saṃskārātmā withdrawn, inner, boddhṛmayā. The
   ābhāsana, cut (vicchidyate), is the jñāna; the siddhatā-bhāga is the bhedābhāsa. The Saugata
   sārūpya and the Jaiminīya prakaṭatā (object-dharma) are invoked. The tātkālikādi example and the
   sphuṭāvabhāsa establish the distinction even in the mind-objects.

9. **Kārikā 8 (vikalpe yo'yam ullekhaḥ...).** In the construction (free or experience-supporting),
   the uplifting (ullekha) is external too, not only the external-organ-known: it shines distinct
   from the knower-form (pramātṛrūpād vyatirikta eva bhāti, "ayam iti" idantayā). The inner-ness
   (āntarya) is the unity with the knower; the external-ness is its opposite. The body (the "I am
   white, I see the jar") and the mind (the buddhi) are dealt both as inner and external. The
   śaktitraya (jñāna/kriyā/icchā) are not divided from the power-possessor; their limitedness
   (pārimitya) is the viṣayakṛta contraction — the prāṇāpāna, the deśa (wall/mountain) are the
   saṅkocakopadhāna, and disregarding them the recognition-restored knower fills the viśvāvabhāsatā
   (the Vijñānabhairava 60/107: the tree-less, mountain-less place, abandoning the body-expectation,
   becomes pervading in days). The ghaṭābhāsabhitter ekatā (one-ness of the jar-appearance-wall)
   admits the twofold external-ness by the ābhāsāntaravyāmiśraṇa.

10. **Kārikā 9 (ullekhasya sukhādeś ca...).** The manifestation of the uplifting and the pleasure-
    and-the-rest with the external self is from the will (icchā) of the Lord, like the eye-form of
    the eye-and-the-rest grounds: the internal reflection of the blue/pleasure/sthāyi-vyabhicāri
    mind-operations is the Lord's external-making freedom (bahiṣkaraṇasvātantrya), and even the
    potter's clay/stick/wheel appearances are the Īśvara-will (parā eva saṃvit; the kumbhakāro'sau
    2.4.9). Wherever the bound-one's will is connected, even there the Lord's freedom is the
    support (nimittāntarābhāvāt). The lajjā is a cittavṛttiviśeṣa, not sukha/duḥkha. The
    bauddha/mānasa manifestation is resolved (the niścaya ends the prakāśa, so the "bauddha" is
    non-other). The Naiyāyika bhāṣya-ṭīkā distinction (pratyakṣa/mānasa/yogi/prātibha/aindriya) and
    the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.4 (indriyārthasannikarṣotpannam) are noted. The memory: the
    pūrvagṛhītatva — the memory-self-consciousness is the pramāṇa (1.7.5) — is re-joined at the end.

**The crux.** V2-R opens the aṣṭamo vimarśa (the māheśvarya): the great Lord (maheśvara), the one
knower, is the support (āśraya) of the knowledge-power, and the māheśvarya jñānaviṣaya is
determined here. The appearances, though divided and external-seeming, are inner (āntarāḥ), their
being-ness always-shining (kārikās 1–2, 5, 7); the external-ness is an adjunct, not the own-form
(kārikā 5); the object-action is appearance-fixed and absent in the inner knower-unity (kārikā 6);
the uplifting in the free construction is external too, but only because it shines distinct from the
one knower (kārikā 8); and all of this — the pleasure, the uplifting, even the potter's dealing —
is the manifestation of the Lord's will, the external-making freedom (kārikā 9). This completes the
jñānaviṣaya māheśvarya; V2-S (13200–13405) closes the aṣṭamo vimarśa (the aikya, the
bhāvikriyādhikāra introduction) and the whole jñānādhikāra.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.8.1–1.8.9 (the nine kārikās of this chunk), 1.6.11 (*ata eva
yathābhīṣṭasamullekhā...*), 1.7.5 (*smṛtau yaiva...*), 1.5.21 (*kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya...*), 1.5.80
(*svāminaś ca...*), 2.3.1, 2.3.10 (*dūrāntikatayā...*), 2.4.9 (*tathāhi kumbhakāro'sau...*); the
Vijñānabhairava 60 (*nirvṛkṣagiribhittyādideśe dṛṣṭiṃ vinikṣipet*) and 107 (*apekṣāṃ svaśarīrasya
tyaktvā vyāpī dinair bhavet*); the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.4 (*indriyārthasannikarṣotpannam*); the Saugata
sārūpya verse and the ekasaṃvedanatādātmyabalād rule; the Jaiminīya prakaṭatā; the
ekaikatrāpi ṣaṭtriṃśadātmatā maxim; the māyāśaktikṛta avasāya and the abhimānamātra analysis. The
apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's
refutation of the external.

Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V2-S)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V2-S = M00021 lines 13200–13405, the CLOSE of the aṣṭamo vimarśa (the
   māheśvarya) and the WHOLE jñānādhikāra. It contains kārikā 10 (*tadaikyena vinā na syāt saṃvidāṃ
   lokapaddhatiḥ prakāśaikyāt tadekatvaṃ mātaikaḥ sa iti sthitam* — without that unity the world-
   path of the consciousnesses would not be; from the manifestation-unity that one-ness, that one
   alone is the knower, it is established); and kārikā 11 (*sa eva vimṛśattvena niyatena maheśvaraḥ
   vimarśa eva devasya śuddhe jñānakriye yataḥ* — he alone, by the fixed reflexive-awareness-ness,
   is the great Lord; the reflexive-awareness alone, of the God, in the pure knowledge-action,
   since). The chunk ends at the ||8|| colophon (*iti ... māheśvaryavimarśo'ṣṭamaḥ*) and the
   jñānādhikāra colophon (*samāptaś ca ayaṃ jñānādhikāraḥ prathamaḥ*) at source 13401 (the file's
   END OF FILE at 13405). **This completes Vol 2 (M00021) — the entire jñānādhikāra (vimarśas 4–8).**

2. **The term-ledger LOCK carried from V2-E through V2-R.** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa =
   appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; smṛti = memory; vikalpa = construction;
   niścaya/avasāya = determination; pratiyogi = counterpart; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti = valid-means/
   known/result; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana = self-consciousness; svaprakāśa = self-
   manifesting; bāhya/bāhyatā = external/external-ness; āntara/āntaratva = inner/inner-ness;
   grāhya/grāhyatva = grasped/grasped-ness; arthakriyā = object-action; bhāva/abhāva =
   being/non-being; saṃskāra = impression; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; parameśvara/maheśvara = the
   param-Lord/great-Lord; ahaṃvimarśa = the I-reflexive-awareness; idam = this; aikya = unity;
   sattā = being-ness; śuddha/miśra/aśuddha = pure/mixed/unpure; guṇatraya = the three qualities
   (sattva/rajas/tamas); pāramārthika = param-essence; jñānādhikāra = the knowledge-section. The
   older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 10 (tadaikyena vinā...).** The world-path (lokapaddhati) of the consciousnesses — all
   dealing (vyavahāra) — would not be without the unity (aikya) of the cognitions; and since it is,
   the unity is of-necessity. It is not hard to establish: the param-essence of the consciousnesses
   is the manifestation (prakāśa eva hi saṃvidāṃ paramārthaḥ), and it is one, from the non-being of
   distinction; the one is, in-truth, the knower (pramātā). The vṛtti's "paramātman" = the param-
   essence-knower-ness (paramārthapramātṛtā); the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 is invoked. The Sāṃkhya-
   Jaiminīya svaprakāśā-saṃvid, the ancient Vaiśeṣika citsvabhāva-ātmā (1.2.7), and the Buddhist
   grāhikā-buddhi all confirm. The māyāśakti's bheda is not real: the distinction is from the other
   (the body, the known), not from the manifestation; the grāhyagrāhaka (the māyīya body and the
   paramārthapramātṛ) — the tanmayā dṛśyate (1.4.8) — makes the bheda a pratibimbakalpa (reflection-
   like). The bhrānti (the shell-silver) is real only with respect to the māyāpramātṛ: the
   saṃvāda/visaṃvāda are his arthakriyā objects.

4. **Kārikā 11 (sa eva vimṛśattvena...).** The great Lord is he alone whose reflexive-awareness-
   ness (vimṛśattva) is fixed (niyata, un-broken): the manifestation-form never appears un-reflected
   (avimṛṣṭa), like the galvarka-gem. It is the "I"-camatkāra, the bliss-form, the other-facing
   (ananyonmukhatātmanā). The pure knowledge-action of the God is the vimarśa itself. The
   prakṛti/pratyaya analysis (the jñāna/kriyā words): the nature means saṃvedana-jñāna, the
   pratyaya (kvi) denotes the action whose kriyā is the siddhatā-pratyavamarśa-fitness — the
   re-reflexive-awareness (pratyavamarśa) resting in the freedom (svātantrya). The ahaṃvimarśana
   (the I-reflexive-awareness): pure in the śuddha-daśā (the paramātman, the ahaṃ-bhāva eternal),
   un-pure when the māyāśakti's idantā conceals it (the saṃsāra-goers' state). The un-pure ahaṃvimarśa
   arises from the bhinnam idaṃbhāga (the mind/breath body) — its svarūpa is fallen (pracyuta) by the
   guṇatraya (the jñāna = sattva, the kriyā = rajas, the niyāmaka tamaḥ); the puruṣa is not other —
   it is the contracted-consciousness, the non-recognition of the own lordship (the sa
   svarūpāparijñānamayo 'nekaḥ pumān, 4.1.3). The ahaṃvimarśana is echoed as bhittikalpa (wall-like),
   not as the vyāpaka (the "yatra yatra dhūmaḥ" rule). The tri-daśā (śuddha/miśra/aśuddha) and the
   āgamasiddha daśāntaratritaya (paravyāmiśrāpara) are both kept (the etā eva ca; the atrāparatvaṃ
   bhāvānāṃ, 3.1.5).

5. **The jñānādhikāra is COMPLETE.** The aṣṭamo vimarśa closes at the ||8|| colophon (the
   śaktivargaikāśrayagata-māheśvarya-vimarśa), and the whole first adhikāra closes at the colophon
   "samāptaś ca ayaṃ jñānādhikāraḥ prathamaḥ" (source 13401). Vol 2 (M00021) — vimarśas 4–8 of the
   jñānādhikāra — is fully translated. The next target is Vol 3 (M00022), the kriyā-, āgama-, and
   tattva-ādhikāras.

**The crux.** V2-S closes the aṣṭamo vimarśa and the whole jñānādhikāra: the consciousnesses are one
in the manifestation, and that one is the knower — the world-path of all dealing rests on this unity
(kārikā 10); and the great Lord (maheśvara) is he whose reflexive-awareness (vimṛśattva) is fixed
and un-broken — the pure knowledge-action of the God is the vimarśa itself, the "I"-camatkāra, the
freedom (kārikā 11). The un-pure ahaṃvimarśa of the bound one is only the māyā-concealed, guṇatraya-
stained, contracted form of the same pure ahaṃ; the recognition (pratyabhijñā) of the Lord as the
one knower — whose reflexive-awareness, knowledge, and action are the manifestation's own freedom —
is the whole purpose of the jñānādhikāra, now complete.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 1.8.10–1.8.11 (the two kārikās of this chunk), 1.5.11 (*svabhāvam
avabhāsasya...*), 1.2.7 (*jñānaṃ ca citsvarūpaṃ ca...*), 1.4.8 (*tanmayā dṛśyate...*), 3.1.5
(*atrāparatvaṃ bhāvānāṃ...*), 4.1.3 (*sa svarūpāparijñānamayo 'nekaḥ pumān...*); the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi
20 (*yadyapy arthasthitiḥ...*); the Sāṃkhya/Jaiminīya svaprakāśā-saṃvid, the Vaiśeṣika citsvabhāva-
ātmā, and the Buddhist grāhikā-buddhi confirmations; the galvarkamaṇi example; the prakṛti/pratyaya
and ghañ/kvi derivation analysis; the "yatra yatra dhūmaḥ" and the agnimān eva dhūmavān rules; the
guṇatraya (sattva/rajas/tamas) and the bhinnam idaṃbhāga. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the
Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the pañcamo vimarśa's refutation of the external.

*Source: M00022 lines 57–850 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the kriyādhikāra (the action-section). Covers: the opening maṅgala (śivam amṛtavapuṣam amṛtakalācatuṣṭayatṛtīyabhāgajuṣam...); the 8-verse plan; kārikā 1 (ata eva yad apy uktaṃ kriyā naikasya sakramā eketi pratikṣiptaṃ tadekasya samarthanāt — hence, though it was said "the action of the one is not ordered" etc., that is rejected, from the establishing of the one); kārikā 2 (sakramatvaṃ ca laukikyāḥ kriyāyāḥ kālaśaktitaḥ ghaṭate natu śāśvatyāḥ prābhavyāḥ syāt prabhor iva — the ordered-ness of the worldly action, from the time-power, fits; but not of the eternal, the primal, as of the Lord); and the commentary — the kriyāśakti as the vimarśaśakti, the paśupramātṛ krama, the nirbādha-pratyabhijñā, the ābhāsasāra. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock. Max-effort T1.*

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-A)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-A = M00022 lines 57–837, the OPENING of the kriyādhikāra (the action-
   section), the prathamo vimarśaḥ. It contains the maṅgala (śivam amṛtavapuṣam...), the 8-verse
   plan, and kārikās 1–9: kārikā 1 (*ata eva yad apy uktaṃ kriyā naikasya sakramā eketi pratikṣiptaṃ
   tadekasya samarthanāt* — hence, though it was said "the action of the one is not ordered" etc.,
   that is rejected, from the establishing of the one); kārikā 2 (*sakramatvaṃ ca laukikyāḥ
   kriyāyāḥ kālaśaktitaḥ ghaṭate natu śāśvatyāḥ prābhavyāḥ syāt prabhor iva* — the ordered-ness of
   the worldly action, from the time-power, fits; but not of the eternal, the primal, as of the
   Lord); kārikā 3 (*kālaḥ sūryādisañcāras tattatpuṣpādijanma vā śītoṣṇe vā tha tallakṣyaḥ krama eva
   sa tattvataḥ* — time is the sun-and-the-rest movement, or the flower-and-the-rest birth, or the
   cold-heat; the that-marker order alone, he, in-truth); kārikā 4 (*kramo bhedāśrayo bhedo'py
   ābhāsasadasattvataḥ ābhāsasadasattve tu citrābhāsakṛtaḥ prabhoḥ* — the order is the distinction-
   support; the distinction too, from the appearance's being-non-being-ness; in the appearance's
   being-non-being, the varied-appearance-made of the Lord); kārikā 5 (*mūrtivaicitryato
   deśakramam ābhāsayaty asau kriyāvaicitryanirbhāsāt kālakramam api īśvaraḥ* — from the form-
   variety he manifests the place-order; from the action-variety-manifestation, the time-order too,
   the Lord); kārikā 6 (*sarvatrābhāsabhedo'pi bhavet kālakramākaraḥ vicchinnabhāsaḥ śūnyāder mātuḥ
   bhātasya no sakṛt*); kārikā 7 (*deśakramo'pi bhāveṣu bhāti mātur mitātmanaḥ svātmeva svātmanā
   pūrṇā bhāvā bhānty amitasya tu* — even the place-order in the beings shines, of the measured-self
   mother; like the own-self, with the own-self filled, the beings shine, of the un-measured,
   though); kārikā 8 (the upasaṃhāra-śloka *ciddhanam ātmapūrṇaṃ viśvam*); and kārikā 9 (*kintu
   nirmāṇaśaktiḥ sāpyevaṃviduṣa īśituḥ tathā vijñātṛvijñeyabhedo yad avabhāsyate* — but the
   creation-power, she too, of the thus-knowing Lord; thus the knower-known distinction, which is
   manifested). The chunk ends at the ||1|| colophon (kriyāśaktivimarśaḥ prathamaḥ, line 837).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (from the Vol 2 V2-E lock, carried into Vol 3).** vimarśa = reflexive-
   awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition;
   kriyā = action; kriyāśakti = the action-power; jñānaśakti = the knowledge-power; kālaśakti = the
   time-power; sakrama/akrama = with/without order; kāla/krama = time/order; pramātṛ/prameya = the
   knower/the known; paśupramātṛ = the bound knower; santāna = stream; saṃskāra = impression; smṛti =
   memory; viśrānti = rest; svātantrya = freedom; āgama = the teaching; māyāśakti = the māyā-power;
   nirmāṇaśakti = the creation-power; sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra = creation/maintenance/dissolution;
   kṛtyapañcaka = the five-fold deed; avacchedaka = the cutter; mūrti = the form; deśa/kāla-krama =
   place/time-order. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The kriyā as the vimarśaśakti.** The action-section (kriyādhikāra) determines the kriyāśakti
   (the action-power) just as the knowledge-section determined the jñānaśakti. The kriyā is, in
   truth, the vimarśaśakti — the reflexive-awareness-power's freedom of joining/unjoining
   (saṃyojanādisvatantratātmā vimarśaśaktir eva vastutaḥ kriyā). The pūrvapakṣa (that the cognitions
   are stream-operations, the memory from the impression, the cognition inert-or-not) is answered:
   the one un-contracted consciousness, whose known-stain contracts it, is the power/dharma; the
   nirbādha-pratyabhijñā-pratyakṣa establishes the one ābhāsasāra padārtha that accepts the opposed
   forms without opposition (the mirror example), and that is the kriyāśraya (the action-support).

4. **Kārikās 2–5 (the kāla/krama, sakrama/akrama).** The worldly action's ordered-ness comes from
   the time-power (kālaśakti, the Lord's freedom that raises the appearance-cut); but the Lord's own
   action, being time-un-cut, is eternal/order-less. Kārikā 3: time (kāla) is not a substance — it is
   the order (krama) itself, observed in the sun's movement, the flowers' birth, the cold-heat; the
   Vaiśeṣika substance-time, the Kāpila rajas, the grammarian's eternal-operation, the Saugata
   stream — all are, in truth, the order (krama eva nāma bahiḥ kālaḥ). Kārikā 4: the order is the
   distinction-support; the distinction is from the appearance's being-non-being; and in the
   appearance's being-non-being the varied-appearance (citrābhāsa) is the Lord's own doing — the
   spring/summer, the dream, the māyā — the saṃvicchakti itself blazes, the vākyapadīya 2.22
   (ekasyaiva tu sā śaktir yad evam avabhāsate) and the lokayantra verses. Kārikā 5: from the form-
   variety the place-order; from the action-variety the time-order — the one recognition (the
   un-divided hand) admits the varied places/actions without breaking the own-form unity.

5. **Kārikā 6–7 (the kālakrama in the pramātṛ).** The objection that the orders are only in the
   appearances, not in the appearance-less knower, is answered: the cut-manifestation (vicchinnabhāsa)
   bound knower (the śūnya/prāṇa/deha) has the time-order, since its manifestation is not its own
   form but the consciousness-flashing that is intermittent (the fainting); but the param-essence
   knower, the at-once-shone (sakṛd vibhāta), the always-un-broken-manifestation, has no
   time-joining. Kārikā 7: the place-order too is only in the measured-self (mitātmana) mother — the
   bound knower whose own form is the body/place; the beings of the un-measured (amitasya) Lord shine
   filled by the own-self, order-less. The ābhāsapratibhāsatadvirahayoḥ stuti is cited.

6. **Kārikā 8–9 (the upasaṃhāra and the nirmāṇaśakti).** Kārikā 8 (ciddhanam ātmapūrṇaṃ viśvam) is
   the upasaṃhāra-śloka: the world is the consciousness-dense, self-filled. Kārikā 9: the creation-
   power (nirmāṇaśakti) of the thus-knowing Lord manifests the knower-known distinction; that
   manifestation is the Lord's creation-capability (kriyāśaktirūpa). The icchā (will) is the Lord's
   action (icchaiva hetutā kartṛtā kriyā, 2.4.21): like Caitra's "I cook" — the order-less will that
   appears ordered through the cooking-steps — so the Lord's "I flash / I re-reflexively-aware / I
   whirl" appears ordered through the knower-known distinction. The sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra (creation/
   maintenance/dissolution), the mahāsṛṣṭi (great-creation, the pure form), and the Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Rudra
   forms are all the māyāśaktyā-made specifics of the one nirmāṇaśakti; the kṛtyapañcaka
   (five-fold deed) is the Lord's essence. The ||1|| colophon closes the kriyāśaktividadhi's first
   vimarśa.

**The crux.** V3-A opens the kriyādhikāra: the action (kriyā) is, in truth, the reflexive-awareness-
power (vimarśaśakti) — the freedom of the one Lord. The worldly action is ordered through the time-
power, but the Lord's own action is eternal/order-less (kārikā 2). Time is not a substance but the
order (krama) itself, raised by the Lord's freedom from the appearance's being-non-being (kārikās
3–4); the place-order and the time-order are the two forms of the one action-variety in the
appearance-class (kārikā 5). Only the bound (cut-manifestation) knower has the orders; the param-
essence knower is the at-once-shone, un-measured, filled-with-its-own-self (kārikās 6–7). And the
creation-power (nirmāṇaśakti) of the thus-knowing Lord manifests the whole knower-known world — the
will (icchā) is the action, appearing ordered through the distinction it freely raises (kārikā 9).
This completes the first vimarśa of the kriyādhikāra.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.1.1–2.1.9 (the nine kārikās of this chunk), 2.1.4 (*kramo bhedāśrayo...*),
2.1.5 (*mūrtivaicitryato...*), 2.4.19 (*ābhāsabhedād ekatra...*), 2.4.21 (*... icchaiva hetutā kartṛtā
kriyā*), 2.4.3 (*yad asat tad asat...*); the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 15/22; the Vākyapadīya 1.3
(*janmādayo vikārāḥ ṣaḍ...*), 2.19 (*avyaktaḥ kramavāñ śabdo...*), 2.22 (*ekasyaiva tu sā śaktir...*),
3.8.11 (*pūrvottaraistathā kṣaṇaiḥ...*); the 3.3.77 (*mūrtau ghanaḥ*); the Bodhapāñcadaśikā
(*paricchinnaprakāśatvam...*); the tamasya lokayantrasya sūtradhāraṃ and the pratibandhā-
bhyanujñā verses; the kṛtyapañcaka (sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra/tirodhāna/anugraha); the
saṃvitsphuraṇa and the mūrcchā (fainting) example. The apohana/pratiyogi register ties to the
Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the Vol 2 jñānādhikāra's refutation of the external.
