## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-B)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-B = M00022 lines 842–2055, the kriyādhikāra, dvitīyo vimarśaḥ (the
   bhedābhedavimarśa, the distinction-un-distinction reflexive-awareness). It contains the maṅgala
   (saṃjīvanaturyakalākalitavibodhaṃ...), the 7-verse plan, and kārikās 1–7: kārikā 1
   (*kriyāsaṃbandhasāmānyadravyadikkālabuddhayaḥ satyāḥ sthairyopayogābhyām ekānekāśrayā matāḥ* —
   the action, relation, universal, substance, direction, time-cognitions are true, by the stability
   and the use, the one-many-support, the declared); kārikā 2 (*tatraikam āntaraṃ tattvaṃ tad eva
   indriyavedyatāṃ saṃprāpya anekatāṃ yāti deśakālasvabhāvataḥ* — there the one, the inner essence,
   thus attaining the organ-known-ness, the many-ness, it goes, from the place-time-own-nature);
   kārikā 3 (*taddvayālambanā etā mano'nuvyavasāyi sat karoti mātṛvyāpāramayīḥ karmādikalpanāḥ*);
   kārikā 4 (*svātmaniṣṭhā viviktābhā bhāvā ekapramātari anyonyānvayarūpaikyayujaḥ saṃbandhadhīpadam*);
   kārikā 5 (*jātidravyāvabhāsānāṃ bahir api ekarūpatāṃ vyaktyekadeśabhedaṃ cāpy ālambante
   vikalpanāḥ*); kārikā 6 (*kriyāvimarśaviṣayaḥ kārakāṇāṃ samanvayaḥ avadhyavadhimadbhāvānvayālambā
   digādidhīḥ*); and kārikā 7 (*evam evārthasidhiḥ syād mātuḥ arthakriyārthinaḥ
   bhedābhedavatārthena tena na bhrāntir īdṛśī* — thus indeed the object-attainment would be, of the
   object-action-desiring mother; with the distinction-un-distinction-possessing meaning, by that,
   not the delusion, this-form). The chunk ends at the ||2|| colophon (bhedābhedavimarśo dvitīyaḥ,
   line 2050).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa =
   manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; kriyā = action;
   kriyāśakti = the action-power; kālaśakti = the time-power; sakrama/akrama = with/without order;
   kāla/krama = time/order; pramātṛ/prameya = the knower/the known; paśupramātṛ = the bound knower;
   santāna = stream; saṃskāra = impression; smṛti = memory; viśrānti = rest; svātantrya = freedom;
   āgama = the teaching; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; satya/asatya/saṃvṛtisatya = true/untrue/
   conventional-true; sāmānya = the universal; svalakṣaṇa = the own-marker; jāti = the class;
   dravya = the substance; avayava/avayavin = the part/the part-possessor; samavāya = the inherence;
   saṃyoga = the conjunction; sambandha = the relation; kāraka = the adjunct; samanvaya = the
   conjunction; arthakriyā = the object-action; saṃkhya = the number; parimāṇa = the measure;
   pṛthaktva = the separateness; bhedābheda = the distinction-un-distinction; anuvyavasāya =
   the re-determination; vikalpa = the construction; pratibhāsa = the manifestation; apoha = removal.
   The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The satya/asatya/saṃvṛtisatya distinction.** Kārikā 1 establishes the action/relation/
   universal/substance/direction/time cognitions as true (satyāḥ): they are so by the stability
   (sthairyam, the not-uprooted reflexive-awareness) and the use (upayoga, the arthakriyā). The
   satya (e.g. the jar-cognition, whose "this jar" vimarśa is un-uprooted and object-action-
   serving), the asatya (e.g. the double-moon, whose vimarśa is uprooted and whose arthakriyā fails),
   and the saṃvṛtisatya (the conventional-true, the sāmānya: the sarvatrika/sadātanī cognition that
   does not cease) are distinguished. The sāṃvṛta is a bhrāntiviśeṣa (a delusion-specific), not a
   separate truth-class. The arthakriyākāritva (object-action-doing-ness) is not the own-form
   (svarūpa, that would be paryāya) nor the marker (lakṣaṇa, that would over/under-extend) but the
   upalakṣaṇa (the incidental marker) whose upalakṣita is the svātantrya.

4. **Kārikās 2–3 (the ekatva/anekatva; the anuvyavasāya).** The one inner essence (āntaraṃ tattvaṃ,
   the saṃvinmātra) is un-computable (kalanāśūnya); the same one, attaining the external-organ-
   known-ness, goes into the many-ness from the place-time-own-nature — without opposition, since
   the cognition is un-broken (like the cause/non-cause). Kārikā 3: the mind-re-determining
   (mano'nuvyavasāya), being, makes the action-and-the-rest conceptions supporting the two (the
   one-many). The sāmānya and the other universals gain their "life" (jīvita) only in the
   construction (the sāmānyoparañjakatā, the sambandhibhedodreka, the kṣaṇabhedaikya, the
   avayavarāśīkaraṇa). The māyāpramātṛ's anuvyavasāya is the occasion of the kriyādi-vyavahāra; the
   śivatādaśā and the sadāśivādibhūmi are not the locus.

5. **Kārikās 4–6 (the sambandha, the jāti/dravya, the kāraka).** Kārikā 4: the relation is the
   mutual-form-clinging (paraspararūpaśleṣa), the bhedābhedakoṭidvaya-swing (dolāyantra), resting in
   the one knower. Kārikā 5: the class/substance manifestations are one-form outside too — the
   one-cow-ness with the individual-distinction (the "imā gāvaḥ", the abheda-qualifier/bheda-
   qualified); the jar is the niḥsandhibandhana-one with the extended-many-parts (the vaitatya, the
   part-mass). The māyā-fit (māyocita) pramātṛ, the sambandhamukhaprekṣi, confirms. Kārikā 6: the
   kāraka-conjunction (samanvaya) is the kriyāvimarśa-object; the action's distinction (by the
   adjuncts) and its un-distinction (by the one-agent-rest) are the relation-life. The
   dig/kāla (direction/time) cognitions are the limit-limitable, the bhedāvamarśana-middle-
   abheda-ending (melayantī) — the relation-form. The samavāya (inherence) of the Kāṇādas is
   rejected: its one-ness yields the sarvapadārthasaṅkara, its bheda yields the anavasthā, and its
   "tādātmyena iva" is only the sādṛśya/utprekṣā; the samavāya's svātantrya is the parameśvara or
   his śakti — our view.

6. **Kārikā 7 (the arthasiddhi, the bhrānti).** The object-attainment (arthasidhi) of the object-
   action-desiring world is only through the bhedābhedavat artha (the distinction-un-distinction
   meaning) — the relation-general-and-the-rest. Without it no arthakriyā; where it is not cognized
   it still flashes within (antaḥsphurann eva). If this were untrue, nothing would be true; so
   whoever deals with it as delusion (bhrāntivyavahāra) is himself the deluded one (sa eva paraṃ
   bhrāntaḥ). The sthairyopayogau (the stability and the use) of the grasping-sūtra are fit; the
   stability = the bādhakābhāva, the use = the saṃvāda (in one explanation), or the stability =
   the saṃvāda and the use = the arthakriyākāritva (in the other).

**The crux.** V3-B establishes the dvitīyo vimarśa of the kriyādhikāra — the bhedābhedavimarśa. The
action, relation, universal, substance, direction, time cognitions are true (kārikā 1) — their
truth is the un-uprooted manifestation (prakāśamānatā) and the arthakriyā, not a separate real
feature. The one inner essence (saṃvinmātra) enters the many-ness through the place-time (kārikā 2);
the mind-re-determination (anuvyavasāya), by the free knower's operation, makes the kriyādi-
conceptions (kārikā 3). The relation is the mutual-form-clinging in the one knower (kārikā 4); the
class and substance manifestations are one-form outside too, with the individual-part-distinction
(kārikā 5); and the kāraka-conjunction is the action-reflexive-awareness-object, the direction/time
being the limit-limitable relation (kārikā 6). Finally, the object-attainment is only through the
bhedābhedavat artha, and its "delusion" is the delusion of the deluder (kārikā 7). This completes the
second vimarśa of the kriyādhikāra.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.2.1–2.2.7 (the seven kārikās of this chunk), 2.2.1 (*kriyāsaṃbandha...*),
2.2.4 (*svātmaniṣṭhā viviktābhā...*), 2.2.5 (*... ālambante vikalpanāḥ*), 2.1.2 (*sakramatvaṃ ca
laukikyāḥ...*), 2.1.4, 2.1.5, 2.3.2 (*ekābhidhānaviṣaye mitiḥ...* / *so'ntastathāvimarśātmā...*),
2.3.5 (*tathaiva sadghaṭa...*), 2.4.21 (*... icchaiva hetutā kartṛtā kriyā*), 1.3.5 (*bhrāntitve
cāvasāyasya...*), 1.3.7 (*na ced antaḥkṛtā...*); the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 21 (*tadātmanaiva tasya syāt
kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā*); the Vijñānabhairava 106 (*... saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā*); the Vākyapadīya
3.3.9 (*ātmāntarasya yenātmā tadātmevāvabhāsate*); the Kāṇāda sūtras (rūpidravyasamavāyāc cākṣuṣāṇi
sāmānyāni 4.1.11; the parimāṇa/unmāna definitions); the Nyāyasūtras 2.1.34 (*sarvāgrahaṇam avayavya-
siddheḥ*), 2.1.35 (*dhāraṇākarṣaṇopapatteś ca*); the kārakavārtika (*bhinnaṃ paceḥ svarūpaṃ...*);
the Pāṇinisūtra 5.3.94 (*ekāc ca prācām*); the camasenāpaḥ praṇayanti (the Śrauta example); the
na vinā saṃkhyayā kaścit sattvabhūto'rtha ucyate maxim. The apoha/pratiyogi register ties to the
Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the Vol 2 jñānādhikāra's refutation of the external.

## The kriyādhikāra, tṛtīyo vimarśaḥ: the maṅgala, the 17-sūtra plan

**The third vimarśa (atha tṛtīyo vimarśaḥ).**

> "[and]-the-one (ekam), [and]-from-the-un-surpassed-form (anuttararūpāt), [and]-with-the-beginning (prabhṛti), [and]-with-the-trika-power-filled (trikaśaktipūrita), [and]-the-bliss (ānandam);

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-C)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-C = M00022 lines 2055–3000, the kriyādhikāra, tṛtīyo vimarśaḥ (the
   pramāṇavimarśa, the valid-means reflexive-awareness), covering the beginning through the
   extensive commentary on kārikās 1–2 (the pramāṇa and the pramāṇaphala; the mānameya, the
   sākṣātkāra/svasaṃvedana, the kāryakāraṇa, the āgama, the saṃvāda/visaṃvāda, the tarka). Kārikā 1
   (*idam etādṛg ity evaṃ yad vaśād vyavatiṣṭhate vastu pramāṇaṃ tat so'pi svābhāso'bhinavodayaḥ* —
   the object, through whose force "this, of-this-form, thus" it stands, the object is the valid-
   means; that even, the self-manifesting, the new-rise); kārikā 2 (*so'ntas tathāvimarśātmā
   deśakālādy abhedini ekābhidhānaviṣaye mitir vastuny abādhitā* — he, the inner-thus-reflexive-
   awareness-own, in the place-time-and-the-rest-un-divided, the cognition in the one-utterance-
   object, in the object, the un-refuted). The chunk ends at source 3000, mid-vimarśa (the next
   chunk V3-D continues).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa =
   manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; kriyā = action;
   pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti = valid-means/known/result-of-knowing; pramāṇaphala = valid-means-result;
   mānameya = measuring-known; pramātṛ = the knower; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana = self-
   consciousness; svaprakāśa = self-manifesting; sākṣātkāra = direct-manifestation; abādhita = the
   un-refuted; bādhya/bādhaka = the refuted/refuter; saṃvāda/visaṃvāda = agreement/disagreement;
   kāryakāraṇabhāva = effect-cause-being; liṅga = the marker; āgama = the teaching; tarka = the
   reasoning; anumāna = the inference; pratīti = the cognition; abhyāsa = the practice; saṃskāra =
   the impression; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; parameśvara = the param-Lord; māyāśakti = the
   māyā-power; sāmānya/svalakṣaṇa = the general/the own-marker; bhāvanā = the meditation;
   anuvyavasāya = the re-determination. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The pramāṇa and the pramāṇaphala.** Kārikā 1: the object (the external blue or the inner
   pleasure) stands by the force of the manifestation (prakāśa) — "this, of-this-form, thus". The
   object itself is the valid-means (vastu pramāṇaṃ); it is the self-manifesting new-rise
   (svābhāso'bhinavodayaḥ). Kārikā 2: the inner-thus-reflexive-awareness-own (antastathāvimarśātmā)
   — in the place-time-un-divided (the pure consciousness) — is the cognition (mitiḥ), un-refuted,
   in the object, in the one-utterance-object. The pramāṇa and the phala are non-distinct in the
   main sense: the manifestation, external-facing, is the pramāṇa; the same, inner-facing as the
   vimarśa (contracted by the object-stain, word-bodied), is the phala. The reflexion-alone is the
   phala; the bodha is the pramāṇa by its strength. The śūnyādyupādhisaṅkoca is the 
   pramātṛ-pramāṇa-prameyollāsa by the one creation-power; the siddha-pāda verse (udety ekaḥ
   samālokaḥ pramāṇārthapramātṛjaḥ) is cited.

4. **The sākṣātkāra and the svasaṃvedana.** The bādhya/bādhaka and the abādhita are governed by
   the un-uprooted vimarśa: the jar-cognition's vimarśa is un-uprooted and object-action-serving
   (satya); the double-moon's vimarśa is uprooted (asatya). The svasaṃvedana (own-consciousness) is
   always abhrānta even in the deluded awareness (the bhrāntabodhe'pi svasaṃvedanam abhrāntam
   sarvatra) — only the object-part is deluded, not the awareness-part. The saṃvāda (agreement) is
   the arthakriyā-attainment; the viśeṣaṇa (the "idam etādṛk") is what the pramāṇa (the vastu)
   grasps, the sāmānya is the karman (to-be-established). The pramāṇasiddha (that which the
   valid-means establishes) is the un-refuted (abādhita), and the bādhya is the apramāṇasiddha.

5. **The kāryakāraṇa (effect-cause).** The effect-cause-being (kāryakāraṇabhāva) is not a real
   own-form (āsvābhāvika): the fire-smoke rule (paurvāparyalakṣaṇa) is only the consciousness-
   unfolding (saṃvidvijṛmbhā), manifested with the rule by the niyatiśakti. The dhūmasya rūpaṃ is
   the smoke-manifestation's re-reflexive-awareness-firmness (dhūmābhāsataiva pratyavamarśadārḍhyam
   āpannā), not the fire-immediacy, not the throat-eye-distortion-prior-ness; otherwise the
   anavasthā (regress) and the anyonyāśrayatva (mutual-support) follow. The kāryakāraṇa-inference
   (anumāna) is durlabha (hard to get): the one-many determinations, the sāmagrī/sahakāri-variety,
   and the yogi-creation all undermine the fixed inference.

6. **The āgama (the teaching).** The āgama is the firm re-reflexive-awareness (dṛḍhavimarśarūpaṃ
   śabdanaṃ), the word-transfer (śabdanasaṃkrāntiśarīraḥ) of the param-Lord; the mantras, the
   nāmākṣara, and the letter-syllable (lipyakṣara) all act by the param-Lord-will and the firm
   vimarśa. The famous (prasiddhi), rooted (nirūḍhi), is the sole pramāṇa; the Sugata/Kapila
   statements are the param-Lord's āgamas (the sva. 10.680 verse), and their beginning-less-ness is
   in the param-Lord. The Veda's validity: the īśvarājñā (the Lord's command), the
   vedātmikājñā (sta. ci. 69). The nibaddhā/anibaddhā speech, the viparyaya (opposed fame), and the
   mahājana (the Varāhamihira verse on the worship-rules) are all the firm-fame-based. The tarka
   (reasoning) is apratiṣṭha (un-established) — a kāvyasaṃsāra, not a firm ground.

**The crux.** V3-C opens the pramāṇavimarśa of the kriyādhikāra: the object is the valid-means
through the manifestation that stands it as "this, of-this-form, thus" (kārikā 1); the cognition is
the inner-thus-reflexive-awareness-own, un-refuted, in the one-utterance-object (kārikā 2). The
pramāṇa and its phala are non-distinct (the manifestation external-facing = the pramāṇa, inner-
facing = the phala). The svasaṃvedana is always un-deluded; only the object-part is deluded in the
bhrānta. The effect-cause and the inference are not real own-forms but the consciousness-unfolding
by the niyatiśakti; the firm āgama (the param-Lord's word) is the sole reliable pramāṇa, and the
tarka is un-established. This continues the kriyādhikāra's demonstration that all valid cognition
rests in the one free Lord's reflexive-awareness.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-D)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-D = M00022 lines 3000–4000, the kriyādhikāra, tṛtīyo vimarśaḥ (the
   pramāṇavimarśa), covering kārikās 3–8: kārikā 3 (*yathāruci yathārthitvaṃ yathāvyutpatti bhidyate
   ābhāso'py artha ekasminn anusandhānasādhite* — as the taste, as the wish, as the derivation, the
   appearance is divided, even in the one meaning established by the continuity); kārikā 4
   (*dīrghavṛttordhvapuruṣadhūmacāndanatādibhiḥ yathābhāsā vibhidyante deśakālāvibhedinaḥ* — with the
   long-round-upright-person-smoke-sandalwood-and-the-rest, as the appearances are divided, of the
   place-time-un-divided); kārikā 5 (*tathaiva sadghaṭadravyakāñcanojjvalatādayaḥ ābhāsabhedā
   bhinnārthakāriṇas te padaṃ dhvaneḥ* — thus-alone the being-jar-substance-gold-shining-ness-and-
   the-rest, the appearance-distinctions, the different-object-makers, they the word of the sound);
   kārikā 6 (*ābhāsabhedādvastūnāṃ niyatārthakriyā punaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratibhāsād abhedinām*);
   kārikā 7 (*pṛthagdīpaprakāśānāṃ srotasāṃ sāgare yathā aviruddhāvabhāsānām ekakāryā tathaikyadhīḥ*);
   and kārikā 8 (*tatrāviśiṣṭe vahnyādau kāryakāraṇatoṣṇatā- tattacchabdārthatādyātmā pramāṇād ekato
   mataḥ*). The chunk ends at source 4000, mid-vimarśa (the next chunk V3-E continues).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa =
   manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; jñāna = cognition; kriyā = action;
   pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti = valid-means/known/result; pramāṇaphala = valid-means-result; mānameya =
   measuring-known; pramātṛ = the knower; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana = self-consciousness;
   sākṣātkāra = direct-manifestation; abādhita = the un-refuted; saṃvāda = the agreement;
   kāryakāraṇabhāva = effect-cause-being; liṅga = the marker; āgama = the teaching; āpta = the
   trustworthy; dīkṣā = the initiation; prasiddhi/nirūḍhi = the fame/rootedness; sāmānya/svalakṣaṇa =
   the general/the own-marker; anusandhāna = the continuity; parāmarśa/pratyavamarśa = the (re-)
   recollection; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; parameśvara = the param-Lord; bhāvanā = the
   meditation; saṃskāra = the impression; abhyāsa = the practice; ekānekatva = one-many-ness.
   The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 3 (yathāruci...).** The object (e.g. the jar) is one (ekam) but its appearances are
   divided (bhidyante) by the taste (ruci = the freedom), the wish (arthitva = the object-action-
   desire), and the derivation (vyutpatti = the old-dealing/skill). The anusandhāna (continuity)
   established in the one: the reflexion (vimarśa), per-appearance-rested, grounds the
   general-dealing; at other times, by the quality-primary mixing, it is the anusandhāna. The
   svalakṣaṇa (own-marker) is fixed, the sāmānya (general) is relative (the mahāviṣayatva/alpa-
   viṣayatva). The bhittirekhā (wall-line) example: the own-marker like the wall, the general like
   the line-division.

4. **Kārikās 4–5 (dīrghavṛtta...; tathaiva sadghaṭa...).** The famous distinctions (the long, the
   round, the upright-person, the smoke, the sandalwood) exemplify the bheda; the not-famous
   (sattva, ghaṭatva) is the dārṣṭāntika (the exemplified). The dīrgha is seen in the jar's upright
   parts with the attentive eye; the dhūmacāndanatā are the vyutpatti-example. The bhartṛhari 1.35
   (pareṣām asaṃkhyeyam abhyāsād eva jāyate) shows the ābhyāsika-pratyakṣa. The sadābhāsa (the
   being-manifestation) is distinguished from the cloth/jar by the mūrtibheda (form-distinction),
   and the sannityābhāsa is the antaḥkaraṇa-manifested (the mind-re-determining, 2.2.3), not the
   bahiṣkaraṇa; its arthakriyā is the heart-break-removal (hṛdbhaṅgaparihāra).

5. **Kārikā 6 (ābhāsabhedādvastūnāṃ...).** From the appearance-distinction, the fixed object-action
   (niyatārthakriyā), by the same-reference (sāmānādhikaraṇya), of the un-divided (abhedin). The
   mixed appearances: one primary appearance (pradhāna), the others the same-locus (samānam
   adhikaraṇam); the sāmānādhikaraṇya marks the pratibhāsa that, by the sentence-meaning-recollection
   ("this-here-now the jar is"), animates the abhedin (the one-own-marker-attained) — whose
   arthakriyā is the aggregate-form. The pramāṇa (the valid-means) is the one pramāṇa; the
   saṃvādakam eva pramāṇam (only the agreement-maker is the valid-means).

6. **Kārikā 7 (pṛthagdīpaprakāśānāṃ...).** Like the separate-lamp-lights (that do not together
   illuminate) vs. the congealed one-building (ekabhavanasaṃmūrcchitā), and the streams in the ocean,
   so the un-opposed appearances (aviruddhāvabhāsā) — the jar-gold-red-raised — by the one own-
   marker-mingling (svalakṣaṇātmanā melanena) yield the one-effect (ekakārya) and the unity-mind
   (aikyadhī). The virodha (opposition) is by the niyatiśakti. The bhāvābhāvau (the being/non-being
   of the appearance) are the own-form-distinction; the mūrtibhedagarbhatāsaha is the mahāsāmānya
   (the being-ness). The kāryakāraṇabhāva is not an own-form but the consciousness-unfolding by the
   niyatiśakti; the dhūmarūpa is the smoke-manifestation's re-reflexive-awareness-firmness.

7. **Kārikā 8 (tatrāviśiṣṭe vahnyādau...).** In the un-distinguished fire, the heat-ness, the
   effect-cause-ness, the word-declared-ness (tattacchabdārthatā) are the one self (ātmā) from the
   one valid-means (pramāṇād ekato mataḥ). The pramāṇa-grasped (the anapekṣa, the akṛtrima, the
   niyatiśakti-made) is the svalakṣaṇa; the ābhāsa-antaram-iśraṇa (the other-appearance-mixing) is
   the viśeṣa. The auṣṇya (heat-ness) is grasped by the same pramāṇa that grasped the bhāsvara
   rūpa — the one valid-means, by the avyabhicāritā (un-deviation), establishes the
   trailokya-traikālya niścaya. The dṛṣṭānta (the pepper-jaggery-drink, the pānaka) and the
   dārṣṭāntika (the jar) are fitted.

**The crux.** V3-D continues the pramāṇavimarśa: the one object's appearances are divided by the
taste/wish/derivation but rest in the one anusandhāna (kārikā 3); the famous/non-famous distinctions
exemplify the svalakṣaṇa and the sāmānya (kārikās 4–5); the fixed object-action and the same-
reference mark the un-divided appearances in the one knower (kārikā 6); like the lamps and the
streams, the un-opposed appearances yield the one effect and the unity-mind (kārikā 7); and in the
un-distinguished fire, the heat-ness, the effect-cause-ness, the word-declared-ness are all the one
self from the one valid-means (kārikā 8). The āgama, the āpta (trustworthy), the dīkṣā, the
bādhaka, the prasiddhi, and the tarka are all grounded in the one Lord's reflexive-awareness.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.3.3–2.3.8 (the six kārikās of this chunk), 2.3.2 (*ekābhidhānaviṣaye
mitir...*), 2.3.7 (*pṛthagdīpaprakāśānāṃ...*), 2.2.3 (*... mano'nuvyavasāyi sat*), 1.8.1
(*tātkālikākṣa...*), 1.3.2 (*dṛk svābhāsaiva...*), 1.7.4 (*pratyakṣānupalambhānāṃ...*), 1.5.20
(*ghaṭo'yam ity adhyavasā...*), 1.5.21 (*kevalaṃ bhinnasaṃvedya...*); the Pramāṇavārtika 1.223
(*nirupadravabhūtārthasvabhāvasya viparyayaiḥ...*), 1.51 (*yāvanto'rthasamāropās tanniṣedhe'pi
niścayāḥ...*); the Vākyapadīya 1.35 (*pareṣām asaṃkhyeyam abhyāsād eva jāyate*), 1.40, 1.142, 3.5
(*śaktīnām api sā śaktir guṇānām apy asau guṇaḥ*), 3.11 (*tāṃ śaktiṃ samavāyākhyāṃ...*), 3.32
(*satyāsatyau tu yau bhāgau pratibhāvaṃ vyavasthitau...*); the Svacchandatantra 10.680, 11.119
(*nāsti dīkṣāsamo mokṣaḥ...*); the Nyāyasūtra 4.1.6 (*teṣāṃ mohaḥ pāpīyān nāmūḍhasyetarotpatteḥ*);
the Yogasūtras 3.9, 3.12; the Abhidharmakośa 1.9 (*tadvijñānāśrayarūpaprasādāc cakṣurādayaḥ*); the
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 15; the Varāhamihira worship-rules verse; the Bhaṭṭanāyaka verse. The apoha/
pratiyogi register ties to the Dharmakīrti apoha parallel and the Vol 2 jñānādhikāra's refutation
of the external.

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-E)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-E = M00022 lines 4000–5000, the kriyādhikāra tṛtīyo vimarśaḥ (the
   pramāṇavimarśa), covering kārikās 9–17: kārikā 9 (*... tātkālikī pravṛttiḥ syād arthino'py
   anumānataḥ* — the at-that-time activity of the meaning-desiring agent from the inference), the
   kārikā 10 (*dūrāntikatayārthānāṃ parokṣādhyakṣatātmanā bāhyāntaratayā doṣair vyañjakasyānyathāpi
   vā*), kārikā 11 (*bhinnāvabhāsacchāyānām api mukhyāvabhāsataḥ ekapratyavamarśākhyād ekatvam
   anivāritam*), kārikā 12 (*... arthakriyāpi sahajā nārthānām īśvarecchayā*), kārikā 13
   (*rajataikyavimarśe'pi śuktau na rajatasthitiḥ upādhideśāsaṃvādād dvicandre'pi nabho'nyathā*),
   kārikā 14 (*guṇaiḥ śabdādibhirbhedo jātyādibhir abhinnatā bhāvanām ittham ekatra pramātari
   upapadyate*), kārikā 15 (*viśvavaicitryacitrasya samabhittitalopame viruddhābhāvasaṃsparśe
   paramārthasatīśvare*), kārikā 16 (*pramātari purāṇe tu sarvadābhātavigrahe kiṃ pramāṇaṃ navābhāsaḥ
   sarvapramitibhāgini*), and kārikā 17 (*śaktiprakāśenaiśādivyavahāraḥ pravartyate*). The chunk
   ends at source 5000; kārikā 17's commentary (the dīkṣā/yoga/jñāna discussion) continues into the
   next chunk V3-F (5000–5514).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti =
   valid-means/known/result; pramātṛ = the knower; prāmāṇya = validity; svasaṃvedana =
   self-consciousness; svaprakāśa = self-manifesting; svalakṣaṇa = the own-marker; sāmānya = the
   universal/general; viśeṣa = the particular; saṃvāda = the agreement; anumāna = the inference;
   sākṣātkāra = direct-manifestation; parokṣādhyakṣa = the indirect/direct; mithyājñāna = the
   false-cognition; khyāti = manifestation; asatkhyāti/akhyāti/viparītakhyāti = the
   un-real/un-manifestation/opposite-manifestation theories; kṣetrajña = the field-knower;
   pramātrantara = the other-knower; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; īśvara = the Lord; dīkṣā =
   initiation; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; anuvṛtti/vyāvṛtti = the continuity/removal. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 13 and the bhrānti/khyāti analysis.** The silver-in-the-shell: the shell-silver's
   unity (aikya) is re-cognized (vimarśyate), yet in the shell the "silver" of the mental cognition
   has no standing (sthiti) rooted in unity with the true silver — the external-ness, the
   object-ness, the all-common sellable-and-the-rest fitness are absent, because that vimarśa is
   uprooted (unmūlyamāna) by the disagreement (asaṃvāda) in the adjunct-place and the
   satpratipakṣa-vimarśa's stability ("not this form is silver"). The right-speaking
   (samyagvadana) is the manifestation-re-reflection-own consciousness; its opposite is the
   non-agreement. Abhinava resolves the rival khyāti-theories: the un-real-manifestation
   (asatkhyāti), the un-stable-manifestation (asthirakhyāti), the un-common-manifestation
   (asādhāraṇakhyāti), the non-object-action-making-manifestation (anarthakriyākārikhyāti), and the
   opposite-manifestation (viparītakhyāti) are each examined in turn and brought to rest in the
   un-manifestation-param-essence-ness (akhyātiparamārthatā): in the double-moon, the hair, the
   magic-show, the non-being/opposite dealings have no standing because their common pervader is
   the akhyāti itself. This is the chapter's refutation of the external (bāhyārtha) through the
   appearance-essence and the one consciousness.

4. **Kārikā 14 and the bheda/abheda.** The qualities (guṇa: śabda etc.) make the difference
   (bheda); the class and the rest (jāti etc.) make the un-divided-ness (abhinna); and both rest in
   the one knower (pramātṛ). The cow-ness/horse-ness (gotvāśvatva), the configuration (saṃsthāna)
   as a quality, the atom/measure discussion (paramāṇuparimāṇa = pārimāṇḍalya = the round
   configuration; dvyaṇuka = the long; tryaṇuka = the triangular/quadrangular) — all are resolved
   into appearances. The anuvṛtti/vyāvṛtti (continuity/removal) are both projected by the knower's
   freedom (saṃvedanasvātantryāt); the bheda is real in the māyā-plane, and the avikalparūpā bhūmi
   (the Sadāśiva state) is not a dealing-word.

5. **Kārikās 15–17 and the pramātṛ-pradhāna.** The world-variety is pictured on the even wall of
   the ever-manifesting knower (the bhittiprakāśa); in the param-essence-existing Lord there is no
   touch of opposed-absence (viruddhābhāvasaṃsparśa), so the new-appearance (navābhāsa) valid-means
   has no use in the always-manifested (sarvadābhāta) form. Yet for the contracted knower
   (saṃkucitapramātṛ) the new-new appearance is the valid-means; all cognitions rest in the one
   knower. Kārikā 17: by the power-manifestation (śaktiprakāśena) the Īśa-and-the-rest dealing
   (īśādivyavahāraḥ) is operated (pravartyate) — the śāstra operates through the known object and
   the attained object-action, the vimarśa of the valid-means is its life nourished by the word.

**The crux.** V3-E completes the pramāṇavimarśa's central theses: the tātkālikī activity comes from
the aggregate of valid-means grounded in the one free knower (kārikā 9); the far-near /
indirect-direct / external-internal and the distinct-manifestation-shadow ones are unified by the
primary-manifestation's one re-recollection (kārikās 10–11); the object-action is the innate, ruled
by the Lord's will (kārikā 12); the delusions (silver-in-shell, double-moon, hair) are all resolved
to the akhyāti, refuting the external (kārikā 13); the bheda/abheda of qualities and classes rest
in the one knower (kārikā 14); in the param-essence-existing always-manifested Lord the
new-appearance valid-means has no place (kārikās 15–16); and by the power-manifestation the
Īśa-and-the-rest dealing is operated (kārikā 17). All cognition, action, and dealing rest in the one
free Lord's reflexive awareness.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.3.9–2.3.17 (the kārikās of this chunk), 2.2.4 (*... bhāvā ekapramātari
anyonyānvayarūpaikyayujaḥ*), 2.3.2, 2.3.3, 1.6.1, 1.5.20 (*ghaṭo'yam ityadhyavasāyāt*), 1.1.3; the
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13, 20 (a. pra. si.); the Kālottara; the Mālinīvijayottara 2.42, 4.6; the
"svapne svapno gaṇḍe sphoṭa" rule; the "na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge'sti śāṅkare" (the dīkṣā
initiation); and the Dharmakīrtian apoha/other-knower register that ties to Vol 2's refutation of
the external and the many cognitions. (V3-E continues into V3-F at source 5000.)

   pramāṇatatphalaprameyaparamārthavimarśas tṛtīyaḥ || 3 ||*). The caturtho vimarśa begins at source
   5514 (atha caturtho vimarśaḥ) — the start of V3-G. The source is clean, dense Sanskrit
   throughout (contradicting an earlier, erroneous "OCR-corrupt" flag that never persisted to disk).

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness; pramāṇa/prameya/pramiti =
   valid-means/known/result; pramātṛ = the knower; prāmāṇya = validity; svaprakāśa =
   self-manifesting; svasaṃvedana = self-consciousness; vicāra = consideration/deliberation;
   nirṇaya = determination; saṃśaya = doubt; pratyabhijñā = recognition; māyāśakti = the māyā-power;
   māyāpramātṛ = the māyā-knower; paśuloka = the animal-world; jñānādiśakti = the
   knowledge-and-the-rest powers; dīkṣā = initiation; bhāvanā = meditation; saṃskāra = impression;
   moha = delusion; saṃsāra = the world-wandering; mukti = liberation; kāryakāraṇatā =
   effect-causality. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The kārikā-17 close: the śāstraprayojana.** The four-fold action (caturvidha kṛtya) and the
   prayatna (effort); the crossing of the delusion-ocean (mohamahārṇava) through the
   param-Lord's grace; the dīkṣā/yoga/jñāna and the Mālinīvijayottara 4.6 quote
   (*na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge'sti śāṅkare; kriyājñānavibhedena sā ca dvedhā nigadyate*); the
   bhāvanā and the vibhūti. Abhinava grounds the śāstra's abhidheya/prayojana/phala in the
   pratyabhijñā (recognition): the pramāṇa is the recognition, its result the recognition-rise
   (pratyabhijñādayaḥ), and the final result the unfolding of the full-bliss-infinite-power
   param-Lord form.

4. **The vicāra (consideration) analysis.** Abhinava gives an extended dialectic on what
   "consideration" (vicāra) is — rejecting the Naiyāyika "five-footed deliberation" (pañcapado
   vicāra) by dismantling the word/jñāna/vākyārtha options: the vimarśa (reflexive-awareness) as
   the doubt-own (saṃśayātmā) is the consideration's mark, not the establishment (sthāpana). The
   Nyāyasūtra 1.1.40 (*vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ*), the Mahābhāṣya's
   sandhyakṣara-vārtika, and the Yogasūtras 1.47–48 (*savicāra → nirvicāra vaiśāradya;
   ṛtambharā prajñā*) are all adduced. This is the hermeneutic counterpart to the epistemological
   core.

5. **The three koṭis (tips) of the pramāṇa.** The prākkoṭi (before-tip: the knower's desire to
   know, prameyajijñāsā, and the arising doubt that drives the pramāṇa-search), the vartamānatā
   (the present-ness: the pramāṇa blazes but illuminates the knower himself), and the
   phalaparyantatā (the result-end: the dealing). In all three the pramātṛ (knower) is primary; the
   pramāṇa is the knower's operation (vyāpāra), like the axe's raising/lowering. This crowns the
   pramāṇavimarśa's thesis.

6. **The Sārvātmika and the apoha.** The own-form/place/time-difference (svarūpadeśakālabheda)
   grounds the one consciousness-essence (ekam cittattvam); the mutual-absence (anyonyābhāva) is the
   exclusion-form (apoha) which does not obtain in the Lord; the many-cognitions and the
   external-meaning (bāhyārtha) are rejected via the appearance-essence (ābhāsasāratvāt) and the
   pratyabhijñā. The distinction (bheda) in the delusion is moha; the self/other cognition of the
   Lord is established through the powers (jñānādiśakti) and the pervading-ness (vyāpitva).

**The crux.** V3-F completes the pramāṇavimarśa: the one knower (pramātṛ) is the seat of the
valid-means across its three states (before/present/result), the consideration (vicāra) is
determined as the reflexive-awareness of the doubting cognition, the śāstra operates through the
recognition (pratyabhijñā) as its abhidheya/prayojana/phala, and the world is pictured on the wall
of the ever-manifesting Lord; the ||3|| colophon closes the tṛtīyo vimarśa, and the caturtho
vimarśa begins at 5514.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.3.8, 2.3.11, 2.3.17, 1.1.2, 1.1.3, 1.3.5, 1.3.6, 1.6.2, 1.5.20;
the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13, 20; the Spandakārikā 13; the Vijñānabhairava 113; the
Mālinīvijayottara 2.42, 4.6; the Kālottara; the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.40; the Yogasūtras 1.47–48; the
Mahābhāṣya (sandhyakṣara-vārtika); the "pūrṇe tu sarvam asti" and the "karmataś ca śarīriṇaḥ"; the
āgama verses *niṣkampa ātmasaṃvittau jīvanmukto'bhidhīyate* and *tattve vikalpamānas tu piṇḍapātāc
chivaṃ vrajet*; and Abhinava's own verse on the saṃsāra-old-tree. This closes Vol 3's
kriyādhikāra tṛtīyo vimarśa (V3-G continues at source 5514).

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-G)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-G = M00022 lines 5514–6300, the kriyādhikāra caturtho vimarśaḥ (the
   kāryakāraṇatāvimarśa), covering kārikās 1–11: kārikā 1 (*eṣa cānantaśaktitvādevamābhāsayatyamūn /
   bhāvānicchāvaśādeṣā kriyā nirmātṛtāsya sā* — this one, from the infinite power, manifests these;
   by the will-power this is his action and maker-ness); kārikā 2 (*jaḍasya tu na sā śaktiḥ sattā
   yadasataḥ sataḥ / kartṛkarmatvatattvaiva kāryakāraṇatā tataḥ*); kārikā 3 (*yadasattadasadyuktā,
   nāsataḥ satsvarūpatā / sato'pi na punaḥ sattālābhenārtho'thacocyate*); kārikā 4 (*kāryakāraṇatā
   loke sāntarviparivartinaḥ / ubhayendriyavedyatvaṃ tasya kasyāpi śaktitaḥ*); kārikā 5 (*evamekā
   kriyā saiṣā sakramāntarbahiḥsthitiḥ / ekasyaivobhayākārasahiṣṇorupapāditā*); kārikā 6 (*bahis
   tasyaiva tat kāryaṃ yadantaryad apekṣayā / pramātrapekṣayā coktā dvyī bāhyāntarasthitiḥ*); kārikā
   7 (*mātaiva kāraṇaṃ tena sa cābhāsadvayasthitau / kāryasya sthita evaikas tadekasya kriyoditā*);
   kārikā 8 (*ata evāṅkure'pīṣṭo nimittaṃ parameśvaraḥ / tadanyasyāpi bījāderhetutā nopapadyate*);
   kārikā 9 (*tathāhi kumbhakāro'sāvaiśvaryaiva vyavasthayā / tattanmṛdādisaṃskārakrameṇa janayed
   ghaṭam*); kārikā 10 (*yogināmapi mṛdbīje vinaivecchāvaśena tat / ghaṭādi jāyate
   tattatsthirasvārthakriyākaram*); kārikā 11 (*kāryaṃ hetuḥ svabhāvo vāta evotpattimūlajaḥ*). The
   chunk ends at source 6300; the caturtho vimarśa (kārikā 11's commentary on the svabhāvahetu and
   the pratyakṣa-anupalambha) continues into V3-H.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** kriyā = action; kriyāśakti =
   the action-power; kāryakāraṇatā = effect-cause-ness/causality; kāraṇatā = cause-ness; kartṛtā =
   agent-ness; karma = object; śakti = power; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; vimarśa =
   reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; saṃvit = consciousness;
   pramātṛ = the knower; icchā = will; svātantrya = freedom; jaḍa = inert; cetana = conscious;
   īśvara = the Lord; anumāna = inference; hetu = reason; svabhāvahetu/kāryahetu = nature-reason /
   effect-reason; vyāvṛtti = removal/exclusion; apoha = exclusion; pratyakṣa = perception;
   anupalambha = non-perception; arthāpatti = necessary-supposition; nirṇaya = determination;
   saṃśaya = doubt; sanniveśa = configuration; saṃskāra = impression. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The 21-verse plan (ślokaikaviṃśati).** Abhinava maps the whole caturtho vimarśa in advance:
   the agent-object-ness alone is the essence of causality (kartṛkarmataiva tattvaṃ
   kāryakāraṇatāyāḥ); three verses refute the inert's causality (jaḍasya kāraṇatā nirākriyate);
   six establish the conscious alone as the agent-ness (cetanasyaiva sā kartṛtātmeti); three show
   the niyatiśakti is necessary to the inference (anumāne'vaśyaṃ niyatiśaktir upajīvanīyā); three
   that the Śākya causality leans on our view (śākyoktā api kāryakāraṇatā asmannayam eva śaraṇam
   avalambate); three that the Kāpila causality likewise (kāpiloktā api evam eveti); and two that
   even the conscious agent fails in Lord-ness (tasya api anīśvaratāyāṃ tat na nirvahatīti).

4. **Kārikās 1–2 and the jaḍa (inert).** Kārikā 1: this ancient knower (purāṇaḥ pramātā), by the
   un-constructed, un-ordered will (avikalpā akramā icchā), manifests all beings as his own powers
   (anantā viśve bhāvā hi tasyaiva śaktayaḥ). The construction's maker-ness is only in the māyā-ground
   (vikalpasya nirmātṛtvaṃ māyīyapade), not in the Lord's creation. Kārikā 2: the inert has no power
   and no being-ness; the effect-cause-ness is precisely the agent-object-ness. The sprout's being,
   whether real or unreal, does not belong to the seed's power; the action-power manifests the
   object as the effect, and the manifestor is the agent-cause. The asatkārya/satkārya and the
   Sāṃkhya reference are both canvassed.

5. **Kārikās 3–7 and the kriyā's unity.** Kārikās 3–4: the effect-cause-ness in the world, of the
   inner-revolving, is the two-sense-known-ness of the world flashing with the identity and variety
   in the inner self-consciousness. Kārikā 5: the one action, ordered, with the inner-outer
   standing, established in the one support (saṃvidrūpo bhagavān) that bears both forms by its
   freedom-and-purity. The agent-standing vs. object-standing action (the cooking vs. the walking;
   the creation-action as both) and the one-subject (ekaśeṣa) treatment. Kārikā 6: the outer is the
   effect of that which it is inner to; with respect to the knower the inner-outer standing is
   two-fold. The inert has no vaśana/bal/prabhāva — mastery is the will, consciousness-relative;
   the seed's "causality" is only metaphorical (aupacārika). Kārikā 7: the consciousness alone is
   the cause, standing in the two-appearance; the effect's one standing is that one's action-risen.

6. **Kārikās 8–11, the anumāna (inference), and the apoha.** Kārikā 8: the param-Lord is the cause
   in the sprout too; no other (seed) causality. Kārikā 9: the potter, by the Lord-ness arrangement,
   produces the jar through the clay-and-the-rest impression-order — the pervasive rule that the
   inert produces nothing without the conscious, and the conscious agent culminates in the Lord.
   Kārikā 10: the yogins, without clay/seed, by the will-power produce the jar — the free
   consciousness, its object-action stable. Kārikā 11: the effect-reason or nature-reason, both
   root-born in the origin. Abhinava gives the full svabhāvahetu/kāryahetu dialectic: the
   śiṃśapā-tree-ness binding (tanmātrānubandha), the apoha/vyāvṛtti (removal) as neither thing nor
   non-thing, the inherence-unity (samavāyaikatā), the Dharmottara/Dharmakīrtian marker
   (lakṣaṇa), and the pratyakṣa-anupalambha fivefold; the niyatiśakti alone rules the pervasion
   (vyāpti). The Naiyāyika "six-disputation" (ṣaṭtarkyā) and the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.5/1.1.41 close the
   argument.

**The crux.** V3-G establishes the kāryakāraṇatā (causality) as the agent-object-ness grounded in the
one free Lord: the inert has no causality (kārikās 2–4), the one ordered action rests in the
consciousness-support (kārikā 5), the inner-outer standing is with respect to the knower (kārikā 6),
the consciousness alone is the cause (kārikā 7), the Lord is the cause in the sprout and the potter
(kārikās 8–9), the yogin's will manifests without materials (kārikā 10), and the inference's
svabhāvahetu/kāryahetu are both rooted in the origin and ruled by the niyatiśakti (kārikā 11). All
causality, all inference, and all knowing rest in the one free Lord.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.4.1–2.4.11 (the kārikās of this chunk), 2.3.7, 2.3.8, 2.3.11, 1.5.10,
1.5.20, 1.8.5, 1.8.8, 1.3.5, 1.6.2; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13, 20; the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.5, 1.1.40,
1.1.41; the Yogasūtras 1.47–48; the Vijñānabhairava 113; the Pāṇini-vārttika 1.51; the Kālottara;
the Śvetāśvatara (svabhāvahetu); the Dharmottara/Dharmakīrti marker-theory; the asatkāryavāda /
satkāryavāda (the Sāṃkhya) debate; the "ekasāmagryadhīnasya" and the "nahi naurnāvi baddhā" rules;
and the "pratibhuva iva adhamarṇabhāva" simile. This is the first part of the kriyādhikāra caturtho
vimarśa (V3-H continues at source 6300).

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-H)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-H = M00022 lines 6300–7200, the kriyādhikāra caturtho vimarśaḥ (the
   kāryakāraṇatāvimarśa), covering the close of kārikā 11's commentary and kārikās 12–19:
   kārikā 12 (*bhūyastattatpramātrekavahnyābhāsādito bhavet / parokṣādapyadhipaterdhūmābhāsādi
   nūtanam*); kārikā 13 (*kāryamavyabhicāryasya liṅgamanyapramātṛgāt / tadābhāsastadābhāsādeva
   tvadhipateḥ paraḥ*); kārikā 14 (*asmin satīdamastīti kāryakāraṇatāpi yā / sāpyapekṣāvihīnānāṃ
   jaḍānāṃ nopapadyate*); kārikā 15 (*nahi svātmaikaniṣṭhānāmanusandhānavarjinām / sadasattāpade'pyeṣa
   saptamyarthaḥ prakalpyate*); kārikā 16 (*ata eva vibhaktyarthaḥ pramātrekasamāśrayaḥ /
   kriyākārakabhāvākhyo yukto bhāvasamanvayaḥ*); kārikā 17 (*parasparasvabhāvatve kāryakāraṇayor api /
   ekatvameva bhede hi naivānyonyasvarūpatā*); kārikā 18 (*ekātmano vibhedaśca kriyā kālakramānugā /
   tathā syātkartṛtā vai na tathāpariṇamattayā*); kārikā 19 (*naca yuktaṃ jaḍasyaivaṃ
   bhedābhedavirodhataḥ / ābhāsabhedādekkatra cidātmani tu yujyate*). The chunk ends at source 7200;
   the caturtho vimarśa (kārikā 19's commentary on the pratibimba and the bāhyārthavāda) continues
   into V3-I.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** kriyā = action; kāryakāraṇatā =
   effect-cause-ness/causality; kāraṇatā = cause-ness; kartṛtā = agent-ness; apekṣā = dependence;
   anusandhāna = joining; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; niyama = fixation; anvaya/vyatireka =
   presence/absence; anumāna = inference; hetu = reason; svabhāvahetu = nature-reason;
   gamya/gamaka = the known/known-maker; liṅga = marker; vyāpti = pervasion; pratyakṣa =
   perception; anupalambha = non-perception; pramātṛ = the knower; ābhāsa = appearance; vimarśa =
   reflexive-awareness; cit = consciousness; cidātmaka = consciousness-own; pratibimba =
   reflection; nirmeya = measure; pariṇāma = transformation; vivarta = the (illusory) manifesting;
   pradhāna = the primary (Sāṃkhya); puruṣa = the person; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; avidyā =
   ignorance. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikās 12–13 and the inference across knowers.** The Saugata/Vijñānavādin holds the
   appearance-streams per-knower distinct (pratipramātṛsantānaṃ bhinnam ābhāsam), so the
   smoke-fire effect-cause is only within one stream. Abhinava rejects this: in our view the Lord
   creates the one appearance for the knowers together (pramātṝṇām aikyena sṛṣṭiḥ), so the
   pervasion (vyāpti) is grasped once across the knowers, and the fire-appearance, though indirect
   (parokṣa), is the non-wandering cause of the smoke-appearance — the marker (liṅga) and the
   "lord-cognition" (adhipatipratyaya). The potter/cowherd examples and the vṛtti-joining are
   worked out.

4. **Kārikās 14–16 and the apekṣā (dependence).** Kārikā 14: "in this existing, this is" — the
   causality too is impossible for the dependence-less inert ones; the inert has no apekṣā, hence
   no niyama, hence no prior-posterior effect-cause-being. The anvaya/vyatireka (presence/absence),
   the perception-non-perception, the niyatā dhūme agnyādisāmagrī, and the equal-pervasion of
   gamyagamaka are analyzed; the Dharmottara/Bhaṭṭa svabhāvapratibandha. Kārikā 15: the
   saptamī (seventh case) for the self-resting, joining-lacking ones is only constructed
   (prakalpyate) — not real. Kārikā 16: the case-ending-meaning (vibhaktyartha), supported on the
   one knower, is the fit action-actor-being connection (kriyākārakabhāvākhyo bhāvasamanvayaḥ).

5. **Kārikās 17–19 and the Sāṃkhya.** Kārikā 17: in the mutual-nature-ness of the effect-cause
   two, the one-ness alone — in the distinction there is no mutual own-form-ness; this refutes the
   Sāṃkhya satkāryavāda (the "one, order-varied" pradhāna). Kārikā 18: of the one-self the
   distinction and the action follow the time-order; the agent-ness would be thus, not by the
   non-transforming-ness — Abhinava turns the Sāṃkhya pariṇāma into a kriyā (action), grounding the
   kartṛtva in the consciousness's freedom. Kārikā 19: the inert's thus (many-form) is unfit from
   the difference-non-difference contradiction; in the one consciousness-own (cidātmani), the
   appearance-distinction fits (the pratibimba-method, ābhāsabhedāt). The mirror (ādarśa) analogy,
   the Sāṃkhya pradhāna/puruṣa, the Vedānta vivarta (and its failure for the inert Brahman), and
   the bāhyārthavāda (Dharmottara) are all adjudicated.

**The crux.** V3-H completes the caturtho vimarśa's central refutations and the positive thesis: the
inference (anumāna) works because the one Lord creates the shared appearance for all knowers
(kārikās 12–13); the inert's causality is impossible (kārikā 14); the case-ending connections rest
on the one knower (kārikās 15–16); the Sāṃkhya's mutual-nature and transformation are refuted in
favor of the consciousness's freedom and the reflection-method (kārikās 17–19). All causation and
all inference rest in the one free consciousness.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.4.12–2.4.19 (the kārikās of this chunk), 2.4.8, 2.3.7, 2.3.12, 2.2.1,
1.5.10, 1.5.20, 1.8.5, 1.8.8, 1.6.2; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 13, 20; the Pāṇini-sūtra 3.2.37
(*yasya ca bhāvena bhāvalakṣaṇam*); the Nyāyasūtra 1.1.5, 1.1.41; the Dharmakīrti/Dharmottara
svabhāvapratibandha and the marker (lakṣaṇa) theory; the Bhaṭṭa (Kumārila); the Sāṃkhya
satkāryavāda/pariṇāmavāda; the Vedānta vivartavāda; the Vijñānavāda; the "daṇḍī viṣāṇī", "ekopalambhānubhavād iti", "nahi svātmaikaniṣṭhā", "na rāvyaṃ kāraṇāni kāryavanti", and the
"svapne'pi anagnijatvaṃ na sahyate" rules; the Śrīśivadṛṣṭi (on the vivartavāda); and the "pūrṇe tu
sarvam asti" (V3-H continues into V3-I at source 7200).

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-I)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-I = M00022 lines 7200–7662, the close of the kriyādhikāra caturtho
   vimarśaḥ (the kāryakāraṇabhāvavimarśa). It completes kārikā 19's commentary (the pratibimba /
   ādarśa, the nīla-citsattva, the bāhyārthavāda/Dharmottara refutation), translates kārikā 20
   (*vāstave'pi cidekatve na syādābhāsabhinnayoḥ / cikīrṣālakṣaṇaikatvaparāmarśaṃ vinā kriyā*) and
   kārikā 21 (*itthaṃ tathā ghaṭapaṭādyābhāsajagadātmanā / tiṣṭhāsor evamicchaiva hetutā kartṛtā
   kriyā*), and closes with the ||4|| colophon (source 7661: kriyādhikāre kāryakāraṇabhāvavimarśaś
   caturthaḥ || 4 ||). The āgamādhikāraḥ (teaching-section) heading follows at source 7662 — the
   start of V3-J. The source is clean, dense Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** kriyā = action; kriyāśakti = the
   action-power; jñānaśakti = the knowledge-power; icchā = will; vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   parāmarśa = re-recollection; prakāśa = manifestation; saṃvit = consciousness; pramātṛ = the
   knower; ābhāsa = appearance; pratibimba = reflection; ādarśa = mirror; nirmeya = measure;
   nirmātṛ = the measurer; hetutā = causality; kartṛtā = agent-ness; avidyā = ignorance; māyāśakti =
   the māyā-power; māyāpramātṛ = the māyā-knower; satyapramātṛ = the true-knower; kāryakāraṇabhāva =
   effect-cause-being; śaktivibhāga = the power-distinction; camatkāra = wonder; rāga/kāma =
   attachment/desire; kāraka = actor; upacāra = metaphor. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light"
   variants remain retired.

3. **The pratibimba (reflection) and the citsattva.** The mirror (ādarśa) shows the distinct form
   without the form's miXing into it (the elephant in the mirror is not the elephant itself, nor
   another elephant, nor unreal — it is the mirror's own clear manifestation of that distinct form).
   The blue (nīla) is not separate from the consciousness-form: the cognition alone, manifesting
   with the self and with the non-self, is the blue's manifestation; the un-deniable
   meaning-manifestation (arthāvabhāsana) and the beginningless nature of the cognition-grounding
   (jñānalakṣaṇa) establish that "the cognition-manifestation alone is the blue-manifestation." The
   bāhyārthavāda (externalist, Dharmottara/Dharmakīrti) is refuted: no form of the jar can enter the
   dense mirror; the yellow-conch (pītaśaṅkha) delusion differs from the mirror-mountain because in
   the latter both appear fully (ubhayapūrṇaprakhyā), so there is no akhyāti (non-manifestation) in
   the mirror case.

4. **The kriyāśakti in the Lord.** Abhinava resolves the apparent āgama-distinction of the powers
   (icchā in the Lord, jñānaśakti in Sadāśiva, kriyāśakti in Īśvara): the action-power is the
   will, and the will is the reflexive-awareness (vimarśa/parāmarśa) — the camatkāra (wonder) that
   rests in the self. The icchā/rāga/kāma spectrum and the sautsukya (eagerness) follow from the
   degrees of self-resting (svātmaviśrānti). The free consciousness alone is the agent (kartṛ);
   the inert has no svātantrya, hence no action — the "Himālaya" and the "logs burn" are mere
   upacāra (metaphor), as the Grammarians' kāraka and the pāka example show.

5. **Kārikā 20 and the cidekatva.** Even accepting the real consciousness-unity with the
   distinction as avidyā, the action is impossible without the one wish-marker re-recollection
   (cikīrṣālakṣaṇaikatvaparāmarśa) joining the appearance-distinct jar and consciousness. The
   Vedānta anirvācyā avidyā is dismantled (of what? for whom?), the pratītinirūḍhi (cognition-
   firmness) favors the distinction's truth, and the kriyā/karaṇa requires the joining knower.
   Kārikā 21 crowns it: the desiring-to-stand (tiṣṭhāsor) Lord, with the jar-cloth-and-the-rest
   appearance-world-self, has the will alone as causality, agent-ness, and action.

**The crux.** V3-I closes the kriyādhikāra caturtho vimarśa: the reflection-manifestation grounds
the citsattva (all appearances are the one consciousness's manifestation, kārikā 19 close); the
action requires the one knower's wish-re-recollection joining the appearances (kārikā 20); and the
will alone is the causality, agent-ness, and action of the desiring-to-stand Lord (kārikā 21). The
||4|| colophon closes the caturtho vimarśa and the whole kriyādhikāra; the āgamādhikāra begins at
source 7662.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 2.4.19–2.4.21 (the kārikās of this chunk), 2.4.8, 2.1.2, 2.3.12, 1.5.20,
1.7.11, 1.3.5, 3.1.4, 3.1.6, 3.2.9; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20; the piśācaṭīkā (on 1.7.11); the
Śivadṛṣṭi 1.4 (susūkṣmaśaktitritayaṃ sāmarasyena vartate); the "bhāvasthitāni jananāntarasauhṛdāni";
the Grammarians' kāraka/kartṛ (the "kṛtī bhavati" and "kāṣṭhaiḥ pacati" / "kāṣṭhāni jvalanti"
examples); the "kena nāma na rūpeṇa bhāsate parameśvaraḥ"; and the "na tiṅantena upamānam asti"
(Nyāya rule on the third sage). This closes the kriyādhikāra of Vol 3 (V3-J begins the
āgamādhikāra at source 7662).

## End of V3-J (source 8500) — the āgamādhikāra prathamo vimarśa continues at source 8500 (next chunk V3-K)
---

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-J)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-J = M00022 lines 7662–8500, the āgamādhikāra prathamo vimarśaḥ,
   covering kārikās 1–7: kārikā 1 (*evamantarbahirvṛttiḥ kriyā kālakramānugā / mātur eva
   tadanyonyāviyukte jñānakarmaṇī*); kārikā 2 (*kintvāntaradaśodrekāt sādākhyaṃ tattvam āditaḥ /
   bahirbhāvaparatve tu parataḥ pārameśvaram*); kārikā 3 (*sā sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca sadvidyā
   hamidaṃdhiyoḥ*); kārikā 4 (*idambhāvopapannānāṃ vedyabhūmimupeyuṣām / bhāvānāṃ bodhasāratvād
   yathāvastvavalokanāt*); kārikā 5 (*atrāparatvaṃ bhāvānāmanātmatvena bhāsanāt / paratāhantayācchādāt
   parāparadaśā hi sā*); kārikā 6 (*bhedadhīreva bhāveṣu karturbodhātmano'pi yā / māyāśaktyeva sā
   vidyetyanye vidyeśvarā yathā*); kārikā 7 (*tasyaiśvaryasvabhāvasya paśubhāve prakāśikā /
   vidyāśaktistirodhānakarmāyābhidhā punaḥ*). The chunk ends at source 8500; the prathamo vimarśa
   (the vidyā/kriyā tattvas) continues into V3-K. The source is clean, dense Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** āgama = the teaching; tattva =
   category; padārthavarga = the word-object class; śivatattva = the Śiva-category; jñānaśakti =
   the knowledge-power; kriyāśakti = the action-power; icchāśakti = the will-power; vimarśa /
   parāmarśa = reflexive-awareness / re-recollection; spanda = the quiver; unmeṣa/nimeṣa =
   flashing/closing; sadāśiva = the Sadāśiva (category); īśvara = the Lord; vidyā = knowledge;
   śuddhavidyā/aśuddhavidyā = pure/un-pure knowledge; vidyeśvara = the knowledge-Lord; paśu = the
   animal/bound one; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; tirodhāna = obscuring; kṛtya = action; sṛṣṭi/
   sthiti/saṃhāra/tirodhāna/anugraha = creation/standing/dissolution/obscuring/grace; nandīśvara;
   śaktipāta = power-descent; anugraha = grace; tattvādhvā = the category-path. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The āgama's role.** The pārameśvarāgama (param-Lord teaching) alone can measure the whole
   world (viśvaṃ pramātuṃ samarthaḥ), because it is the un-contracted-manifestation reflexive-
   awareness-own of the param-Lord; the yukti (reason) only supports it (tadupabṛṃhaṇāya). The
   Spandakārikā 43 (*didṛkṣayeva sarvārthānyadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate*) and the śrutis establish the
   all-power self-manifesting consciousness.

4. **Kārikās 1–2 and the śivatattva.** Kārikā 1: the inner-outer action following the time-order,
   of the one knower alone, with the knowledge and the action mutually un-separated (jñānakriye
   anyonyāviyukte) — the action-power's form is the manifestation of all word-objects (the
   kārikā 2.3.15). Kārikā 2: the Sadākhya (Sadāśiva) category is first from the inner-state surge;
   the param-Lord (Īśvara) after, in the external-being-primary-ness. The Śivadṛṣṭi (icchāśakti /
   tuṭi), the Mataṅga-tantra, the jñāna/kriyā distinction, and the aṇu/paśu are worked out.

5. **Kārikās 3–4 and the śuddhavidyā.** Kārikā 3: the co-reference (sāmānādhikaraṇya) of the
   "I-this" cognition is the pure knowledge (sadvidyā) — the aham/idam co-reference in the
   consciousness. The Sadāśiva/Īśvara tattvas as the inner/outer states, the spanda, and the
   vidyākhya operation. Kārikā 4: the pure knowledge is the observation (avalokana) of the beings
   as-the-thing (yathāvastu), their awareness-essence (bodhasāratvāt); the aśuddhavidyā (un-pure
   knowledge) is shown by contrast. The Mataṅga-tantra (1.10.22–23) and the paśu's self-only
   manifestation.

6. **Kārikās 5–7 and the vidyā/māyā.** Kārikā 5: in the beings the un-param-ness from the
   non-self-ness manifestation, the param-ness from the I-ness-covering — the parāpara (param-un-
   param) state. Kārikā 6: the distinction-cognition in the beings is the māyā-power; but in the
   pure-consciousness-bound knowers (vidyeśvara) it is the pure knowledge — the other view. Kārikā
   7: the manifesting (prakāśikā) of the lordship-nature in the animal-being is the knowledge-
   power; the māyā-named is again the obscuring-maker (tirodhānakarī). The five kṛtyas (sṛṣṭi,
   sthiti, saṃhāra, tirodhāna, anugraha), the hell-fall and the boon-giving (varadāna), the
   Nandīśvara, and the śaktipāta (the nine-fold power-descent, the Gītā 7.16–18) close the first
   vimarśa's doctrinal core.

**The crux.** V3-J establishes the āgamādhikāra's foundation: the param-Lord teaching alone
establishes the śivatattva as the body of all padārthas, with the yukti as its support (the
maṅgala); the one knower's action and knowledge are mutually un-separated (kārikā 1); the
Sadāśiva/Īśvara categories are the inner/outer surges of the one consciousness (kārikā 2); the
co-reference of I-this is the pure knowledge (kārikā 3); the pure knowledge observes the beings
as-the-thing in their awareness-essence (kārikā 4); the param-un-param state is the I-this
covering and manifestation (kārikā 5); the distinction-cognition is the māyā-power in the animals
but pure knowledge in the knowledge-Lords (kārikā 6); and the knowledge-power manifests the
lordship-nature in the animal-being while the māyā obscures (kārikā 7). All the categories and all
the powers rest in the one free Lord.

# IPVV Vol 3 — Chunk V3-K: the āgamādhikāra prathamo vimarśaḥ, close — the māyāśakti, the kañcukas, the tattvakrama, kārikās 8–11; the ||1|| colophon — T1

*Source: M00022 lines 8500–9267 (continuous). Base: Torella's ĪPK — the āgamādhikāra, the first vimarśa (the tattvavimarśa). Covers: the close of kārikā 7's commentary (the vidyā/māyā); kārikā 8 (*bhede tvekarase bhāte'hantayānātmanīkṣite / śūnye buddhau śarīre vā māyāśaktirvijṛmbhate*); kārikā 9 (*yaśca pramātā śūnyādiḥ prameye vyatirekiṇi / mātā sa meyaḥ san kālādikapañcakaveṣṭitaḥ*); kārikā 10 (*trayoviṃśatidhā meyaṃ yatkāryakaraṇātmakam / tasyāvibhāgarūpyekaṃ pradhānaṃ mūlakāraṇam*); kārikā 11 (*trayodaśavidhā cātra bāhyāntaḥkaraṇāvalī / kāryavargaśca daśadhā sthūlasūkṣmatvabhedataḥ*); and the commentary — the māyāśakti as the first viparyāsa (the aham-I in the anātmā), the second viparyāsa, the puryaṣṭaka, the āṇava-mala, the vācaka-śabdaśarīra, the kañcukas (kāla, niyati, rāga, vidyā, kalā), the pradhāna/puruṣa of the Sāṃkhya, the buddhīndriya/karmendriya, the anumāna and the niyatiśakti; and the ||1|| colophon (source 9267: āgamādhikāre tattvavimarśaḥ prathamaḥ || 1 ||), closing the prathamo vimarśa. The dvitīyo vimarśa follows. Register per the V2-E term-ledger lock (carried into Vol 3). Max-effort T1.*

   bhedataḥ*); and closes with the ||1|| colophon (source 9267: āgamādhikāre tattvavimarśaḥ
   prathamaḥ || 1 ||). The dvitīyo vimarśa follows at source 9272. The source is clean, dense
   Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** māyāśakti = the māyā-power; viparyāsa
   = opposite/error; anātmā = the non-self; ahantā = the I-ness; idantā = the this-ness; puryaṣṭaka
   = the city-of-eight; mala = stain; āṇava = the atomic (stain); vācaka = the word-maker;
   śabdaśarīra = the word-body; kañcuka = corset; kāla = time; niyati = fixation; rāga =
   attachment; vidyā = knowledge; kalā = caliber; tattva = category; pradhāna/puruṣa = the
   primary/person (Sāṃkhya); kāryakaraṇa = effect-instrument; buddhīndriya/karmendriya =
   intellect-sense/action-sense; mahābhūta/tanmātra = great-element/own-marker-element;
   sanniveśa = configuration; adhyavasāya = determination; ālocana = observation; ākāśa/vāyu =
   space/wind; parameśvara = the param-Lord; niyatiśakti = the fixed-power; anumāna = inference.
   The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 8 and the two viparyāsas.** The māyā-power unfolds (vijṛmbhate) in the emptiness,
   the intellect, or the body, when the distinction is one-flavor and the I-ness is seen in the
   non-self. The first viparyāsa is the māyā-made "I" in the non-self's known-ness manifestation
   (the puryaṣṭaka — the body/intellect/breath/emptiness as ātmā); the second viparyāsa is the
   "this-I" (idam aham) in the non-self's mere inert being. Abhinava establishes the stain-ness
   (malatva) of both and the pure object of the āṇava-mala (where there is no āṇava: the
   vācaka-śabdaśarīra, the mantra-Lords). The viśuddhaiśvarya (pure-lordship) of the knowledge-
   made ones is contrasted.

4. **Kārikā 9 and the kañcukas.** The knower who is the emptiness-and-the-rest (śūnyādiḥ), being
   the known in the distinct known, is wrapped in the time-and-the-rest five (kālādikapañcaka) —
   the five kañcukas (kāla, niyati, rāga, vidyā, kalā) are not separate things or common known-
   dharmas but powers of the knower (pramātṛdharmāḥ) that limit (avacchedana) and measure
   (kalana) the consciousness. The time, the fixation, the attachment, the caliber, and the
   knowledge are all re-recollections (vimarśāḥ) resting in the consciousness, not in the known;
   the pāratantrya/aprabhutva of the aṇu follows. The Sāṃkhya-like descriptions and the
   modakarasavat (mutual-grace) of the corsets are worked out.

5. **Kārikās 10–11 and the tattvakrama.** The known (prameyam) is the twenty-three-fold
   effect-instrument-own; its one un-distinction-form root-cause is the primary (pradhāna); the
   thirteen-fold external-inner-instrument-series and the ten-fold effect-class (coarse/subtle)
   complete the enumeration. Abhinava adjudicates the Sāṃkhya pradhāna/puruṣa, the buddhīndriya/
   karmendriya (the adhyavasāya-determination and the ālocana-observation), the mahābhūta/tanmātra
   (the sanniveśa-configuration, the ākāśa/vāyu as the space/wind), the kāryakāraṇa, and the
   dhāraṇā/dīkṣā (holding/initiation) yogas; and he grounds the whole tattvakrama in the
   param-Lord's niyatiśakti via the pārameśvarāgama (its un-broken validity), not in a weak
   anumāna. The Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 concludes: all appearances rest, through the māyā-knower, in
   the true-knower alone.

**The crux.** V3-K completes the āgamādhikāra prathamo vimarśa: the māyā-power unfolds in the
emptiness/intellect/body (kārikā 8); the emptiness-and-the-rest knower, wrapped in the time-and-
the-rest five corsets, is measured and limited in the distinct known (kārikā 9); the twenty-three-
fold effect-instrument known with its primary root-cause (kārikā 10) and the thirteen-fold
instrument-series with the ten-fold effect-class (kārikā 11) are all established in the one
param-Lord's niyatiśakti and teaching. All the categories, all the instruments, and all the
knowing rest in the one free Lord. The ||1|| colophon closes the prathamo vimarśa.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 3.1.8–3.1.11 (the kārikās of this chunk), 3.1.3, 3.1.9, 2.3.10, 2.4.11,
1.5.17, 1.5.20, 2.1.4, 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 3.2.9, 3.2.11, 3.2.15, 4.1.4, 4.1.5, 4.1.8; the
Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20; the Spandakārikā 8, 12, 13; the Mālinīvijayottara 2.2, 2.50, 3.28; the
Mataṅga-tantra 18.83; the Pūrvāgama; the Svacchanda; the Kiraṇa; the Rudrayāmala-sāra; the
Kālapāda; the Sāṃkhyakārikā 28, 35; the Yogasūtra 2.6 and the Vyāsa-bhāṣya; the Nyāyasūtra 3.1.25;
the Bhagavadgītā 9.6; the Tantrāloka (on the śaktipāta, ch. 13); the "māyāntarvartinaḥ proktāḥ
paśavaḥ" and the "dīkṣāyojanaṃ sarvānugrāhi"; the Vindhyavāsin; and the "kadalīgarbhadalavan
modakādirasādivat" simile. (V3-L begins the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa at source 9272.)

## End of V3-L (source 10000) — the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa continues at source 10000 (next chunk V3-M)

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-L)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-L = M00022 lines 9272–10000, the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśaḥ (the
   pramātṛvimarśa / the māyā-vimarśa), covering kārikās 1–11: kārikā 1 (*tatraitanmātṛtāmātrasthitau
   rudro'dhidaivatam / bhinnaprameyaprasare brahmaviṣṇū vyavasthitau*); kārikā 2 (*eṣa pramātā
   māyāndhaḥ saṃsārī karmabandhanaḥ / vidyābhijñāpitaiśvaryaścidghano mukta ucyate*); kārikā 3
   (*svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu pramātā kathyate patiḥ / māyāto bhediṣu kleśakarmādikaluṣaḥ paśuḥ*);
   kārikā 4 (*svātantryahānirbodhasya svātantryasyāpyabodhatā / dvidhāṇavaṃ malamidaṃ
   svasvarūpāpahānitaḥ*); kārikā 5 (*bhinnavedyaprathātraiva māyākhyaṃ janmabhogadam / kartaryabodhe
   kārmaṃ tu māyāśaktyaiva tattrayam*); kārikā 6 (*śuddhabodhātmakatve'pi yeṣāṃ nottamakartṛtā /
   nirmitāḥ svātmano bhinnā bhartrā te kartṛtātyayāt*); kārikā 7 (*bodhādilakṣaṇaikye'pi
   teṣāmanyonyabhinnatā / tatheśvarecchābhedena te ca vijñānakevalāḥ*); kārikā 8 (*śūnyādyabodharūpāstu
   kartāraḥ pralayākalāḥ / teṣāṃ kārmo malo'pyasti māyīyastu vikalpitaḥ*); kārikā 9 (*bodhānāmapi
   kartṛtvajuṣāṃ kārmamalakṣatau / bhinnavedyajuṣāṃ māyāmalo vidyeśvarāśca te*); kārikā 10
   (*devādīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ bhavināṃ trividhaṃ malam / tatrāpi kārmamevaikaṃ mukhyaṃ
   saṃsārakāraṇam*); kārikā 11 (*kalodbalitametacca cittattvaṃ kartṛtāmayam / acidrūpasya
   śūnyāder mitam guṇatayā sthitam*). The chunk ends at source 10000; the dvitīyo vimarśa continues
   into V3-M. The source is clean, dense Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** pramātṛtattva = the knower-category;
   māyā = the māyā; māyāndha = the māyā-blind; saṃsārī = the world-wanderer; karmabandhana =
   action-bound; cidghana = the consciousness-dense; mukta = the liberated; pati/paśu = the
   Lord/animal; rudra/brahmā/viṣṇu = the presiding deities; āṇava/kārma/māyā mala = the
   atomic/action/māyā stains; vijñānākala/pralayākala/sakala = the knowledge-un-caliber /
   dissolution-un-caliber / complete; vidyeśvara = the knowledge-Lord; mantreśvara = the
   mantra-Lord; suṣupta/turya = the sleep/fourth; kañcuka = corset; kāla = time; niyati =
   fixation; rāga = attachment; vidyā = knowledge; kalā = caliber; dīkṣā = initiation; āveśa =
   absorption; sṛṣṭi/sthiti/saṃhāra = creation/standing/dissolution. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikās 1–3 and the pramātṛtattva.** The maṅgala (the trident-handed destroyer of the
   three bonds) opens the dvitīyo vimarśa, which determines the pramātṛtattva (knower-category).
   Kārikā 1: in the this-knower-mere-ness standing, Rudra presides; in the distinct-known spread,
   Brahmā and Viṣṇu stand. Kārikā 2: this knower is the māyā-blind, world-wanderer, action-bound;
   the consciousness-dense with the knowledge-indicated lordship is the liberated. Kārikā 3: in the
   own-member-form beings the knower is called the Lord (pati); in the māyā-distinct ones, the
   afflicted-stained is the animal (paśu).

4. **Kārikās 4–7 and the three malas.** Kārikā 4: the two-fold atomic stain (āṇava) is the
   freedom-loss of the awareness and the un-awareness-ness of the freedom itself. Kārikā 5: the
   distinct-known-manifestation is the māyā-named (birth-enjoyment-giving); in the un-awareness
   agent, the action-stain (kārma); with the māyā-power, the three. Kārikā 6: in the pure-
   awareness-own-ness even, of whom there is no highest agent-ness — they are created distinct
   from the self by the Lord, from the agent-ness-loss. Kārikā 7: in the awareness-and-the-rest
   marker-unity, their mutual distinct-ness is by the Lord-will-distinction; they are the
   knowledge-alone ones (vijñānakevalāḥ).

5. **Kārikās 8–11 and the kalas (stages).** Kārikā 8: the emptiness-and-the-rest un-awareness-form
   agents are the dissolution-un-caliber ones (pralayākalāḥ), with the action-stain and the
   constructed māyā-stain. Kārikā 9: of the awareness-ones even with agent-ness, the action-stain;
   of the distinct-known-possessing ones, the māyā-stain — they are the knowledge-Lords
   (vidyeśvarāḥ). Kārikā 10: of all the becoming-ones the three-fold stain; there the action-stain
   alone is the primary saṃsāra-cause (the dīkṣā/initiation and the śaktipāta). Kārikā 11: the
   time-raised consciousness-essence, agent-ness-made, is measured with the quality-ness in the
   emptiness-and-the-rest un-conscious-form — the saṃsāra-state (waking/dream/sleep).

**The crux.** V3-L establishes the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa's foundation: the pramātṛtattva
(knower-category) is determined with the Rudra/Brahmā/Viṣṇu presiding (kārikā 1), the māyā-blind
world-wanderer versus the consciousness-dense liberated (kārikā 2), the pati/paśu (kārikā 3), the
two-fold āṇava stain (kārikā 4), the māyā/kārma stains and the three (kārikā 5), the created
distinctness of the no-highest-agent ones (kārikā 6), the mutual distinctness of the knowledge-alone
ones by the Lord-will (kārikā 7), the pralayākala ones (kārikā 8), the vidyeśvara ones (kārikā 9),
the three-fold stain with the kārma as the primary saṃsāra-cause (kārikā 10), and the time-raised
agent-ness-made consciousness-essence measured in the un-conscious (kārikā 11). All the knower-
categories and all the stains rest in the one free Lord.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 3.2.1–3.2.11 (the kārikās of this chunk), 3.1.9, 3.2.4, 3.2.5, 3.2.9,
3.2.10, 3.2.15, 2.3.10, 1.5.10, 1.5.17, 1.6.1, 1.8.11, 4.1.5; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20; the
Spandakārikā 8, 15, 25, 33, 34; the Sāṃkhyakārikā 28, 35; the Netra-tantra 8.4; the Mataṅga-tantra;
the Lalitā; the Sarvavīra-mata; the Kiraṇa; the Śivadṛṣṭi; the Yogasūtra 2.6; the Bhagavadgītā; the
"śaktiśivātmatāyā upādeyatvāt" and the "puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam" and the "dīkṣāsamam kiṃcit" rules; the
"kṛtam api phalāya na syād dīkṣoparyūṣaroptabījam iva" (the guru-statement). (V3-M continues the
āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa at source 10000.)

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** turya/turyātīta = the
   fourth/fourth-transcended; suṣupta/svapna/jāgrat = sleep/dream/waking; prāṇa/apāna/samāna/
   udāna/vyāna = the five winds (breath); jīva/jīvana = the life; puryaṣṭaka = the city-of-eight;
   viṣuvat = the equinox; āveśa = absorption; jñānī/yogin = the wise/yogin; vijñānākala/pralayākala/
   sakala = the knowledge-un-caliber/dissolution-un-caliber/complete; mantreśa = the mantra-Lord;
   vidyeśvara = the knowledge-Lord; saṃskāra = impression; māyā = the māyā; śaktipāta = the
   power-descent; dīkṣā = initiation; camatkāra = wonder; spanda = the quiver. The older
   "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikās 12–14 and the turya/āveśa.** Kārikā 12: the primary-ness of the agent-ness and of
   the awareness of the consciousness-self; in the emptiness-and-the-rest quality, the knowledge
   is the absorption-marker (samāveśa). The Gītā (12.2, 12.9–10) and the turyātītatā are adduced.
   Kārikā 13: in the emptiness (the intellect-and-the-rest-absence), the I-ness-agent-ness-word
   — the un-manifest-form-impression-mere is the known-emptiness-ness; the first suṣupta's
   seat-binding (pīṭhabandha). Kārikā 14: the senses' inner operation, the breath-and-the-rest
   stimulating — the life-named; or in the breath, the I-ness is the city-of-eight-own
   (puryaṣṭakātmikā); the jīvanakriyā and the āhaṅkārika sense-ness.

4. **Kārikās 15–17 and the three states.** Kārikā 15: the sleep-like (sauṣupta), dissolution-equal,
   with the known/un-known and the māyā-stain-joined/un-joined. Kārikā 16: in the mind-mere-path,
   the dream is the manifest-manifestation creation of the beings from the delusion. Kārikā 17:
   the waking is the common creation of all the knowers, with the all-sense-object-ness and the
   external-ness-firm. The prāṇādis (breath-and-the-rest) and the state-distinctions are worked
   out with the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 and the Spandakārikā.

5. **Kārikās 18–20 and the prāṇādis.** Kārikā 18: the three are removable from the breath-and-the-
   rest's primary-ness in the agent-ness-quality, with the loss-increase-like pleasure-pain union.
   Kārikā 19: the breath-out-breath-made breath, individually in the sleep-waking; the cut-own
   equal-named (samāna) in the sleep-like, as in the equinoxes. The viṣuvat (equinox), the
   prāṇāpāna-samāna, and the suṣupta are analyzed (the Vijñānabhairava 61–62, the Spandakārikā
   41). Kārikā 20: the middle-upper-going udāna-named, the fourth-going, the fire-made; the
   knowledge-un-caliber-Mantreśa is the vyāna, the world-self param. The udāna/vyāna, the
   vijñānākala/mantreśa/īśa/sadāśiva, the kāla/kalā śaktis, and the prāṇaśakti close the dvitīyo
   vimarśa; the Mālinīvijayottara 2.42 crowns it. The ||2|| and ||3|| colophons close the
   āgamādhikāra.

**The crux.** V3-M completes the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa: the absorption-knowledge in the
primary agent-awareness (kārikā 12); the first suṣupta as the I-ness-agent-ness-word in the
emptiness (kārikā 13); the senses' inner operation as the life-named with the city-of-eight I-ness
(kārikā 14); the sleep-like with the known/un-known and the māyā-stain (kārikā 15); the dream as
the delusion-creation (kārikā 16); the waking as the common creation (kārikā 17); the removable
three from the breath-primary (kārikā 18); the equal-named (samāna) in the sleep-like as the
equinox (kārikā 19); and the udāna/vyāna as the fourth-going fire-made and the world-self param
(kārikā 20). All the knower-states, all the winds, and all the categories rest in the one free
Lord. The ||2|| and ||3|| colophons close the āgamādhikāra.

1.6, 2.2, 4.8, 4.19, 8, 13, 32, 41 and the Śivasūtra-vimarśinī (Kallaṭa); the Vijñānabhairava

61; the "jīvanmuktastu" and the "dīkṣāsamam kiṃcit" and the "aśūnyaḥ śūnya ityuktaḥ" and the
"śucirnāmāgnirudbhūtaḥ saṅgharṣāt somasūryayoḥ" and the "daśa pūrvāndaśāparān" rules; the
"rasaviddhatāmrakanakanyāya" and the "kadalīgarbhadalavan modakādirasādivat" similes; the

   te eva paśoḥ sattvaṃ rajastamaḥ*); kārikā 5 (*bhedashiteḥ śaktimataḥ śaktitvaṃ nāpadiśyate /
   eṣāṃ guṇānāṃ karaṇakāryatvapariṇāminām*); kārikā 6 (*sattānandaḥ kriyā patyustadabhāvo'pi sā
   paśoḥ / dvayātmā tadrajo duḥkhaṃ śleṣisattvatamomayam*); kārikā 7 (*ye'pyasāmayikedantāparāmarśa-
   bhuvaḥ prabhoḥ / te vimiśrā vibhinnāśca tathā citrāvabhāsinaḥ*); kārikā 8 (*te tu
   bhinnāvabhāsārthāḥ prakalpyāḥ pratyagātmanaḥ / tattadvibhinnasaṃjñābhiḥ smṛtyutprekṣādigocare*).
   The chunk ends at source 11600; the prathamo vimarśa continues into V3-O. The source is clean,
   dense Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** tattvasaṅgraha = the category-
   collection; tattvārtha = the essence-meaning; pāramārthika = the param-essence; svarūpa = the
   own-form; svarūpāparijñāna = the own-form-un-cognition; pumān = the person; bandha/mokṣa =
   bond/liberation; pratyabhijñā = recognition; ābhāsa = appearance; svalakṣaṇa/sāmānyalakṣaṇa =
   own-marker/common-marker; parāmarśa = re-recollection; grāhaka/grāhya = the grasper/grasped;
   idantā/ahantā = this-ness/I-ness; sattva/rajas/tamas = the three qualities; kriyā/jñāna/icchā =
   action/knowledge/will; māyāśakti = the māyā-power; puruṣa = the person; paśu/pati = the
   animal/Lord; śūnya = the emptiness; viśva = the world; saṃvid = consciousness; akhaṇḍa = the
   un-broken; viśrānti = rest. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikās 1–3 and the pāramārthika svarūpa.** The maṅgala (the drop-made nectar-juice-known,
   the full-making nectar-Lord) opens the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra; the 15-verse plan (one for the
   pāramārthika svarūpa, nine for the bandhatattva in the pramātṛ/prameya direction, five for the
   pratyabhijñātmaka mokṣatattva). Kārikā 1: the own-self alone of all beings is the one
   mahā-īśvara, the world-form, un-broken-re-recollection-augmented. Kārikā 2: there, in the
   own-created this-part, with the intellect-and-the-rest grasper-own, the I-construction-
   re-recollection-word is brought — the bound grasper. Kārikā 3: he, the own-form-un-cognition-
   made, the many person is the thought; there in the creation the action-bliss two, the enjoyment
   is the suffering-pleasure-own. The āṇava, the boundness, and the aṇutva.

4. **Kārikās 4–6 and the guṇas.** Kārikā 4: in the own-member-form beings, of the Lord the
   knowledge and the action; with the māyā-third, they alone are of the animal the sattva-rajas-
   tamas. Kārikā 5: from the distinction-standing, of the power-possessor the power-ness is not
   declared — of these qualities (the instrument-effect-transforming). Kārikā 6: the being-bliss-
   action of the Lord; the that-absence-even-she of the animal — the two-own rajas is the
   suffering, attached, sattva-tamas-made. The prakāśa/aprakāśa, the sukha/duḥkha/moha, the
   tṛtīyaguṇa, the māyīya prakāra, the Rudra/Īśvara/Sadāśiva, and the jñāna/kriyā are worked out.

5. **Kārikās 7–8 and the prameya.** Kārikā 7: who-even, of the non-conventional-this-ness-
   re-recollection-ground Lord, they are the mixed and the distinct, the varied-manifesting. The
   svalakṣaṇa/sāmānyalakṣaṇa appearances, the īśvara's non-conventional this-ness, the śūnya and
   the Rudra. Kārikā 8: they-though, the distinct-manifestation-meanings, the constructed of the
   inner-self — with the that-that-distinct-designations, in the memory-conjecture-and-the-rest
   range. The vikalpa (construction), the pratyagātman, the śūnyapramātṛ, the infinite-regress
   (anavasthā) and its non-fault, the īśvara's nañartha (negation-meaning), the
   saṃskāra-seed-capacity (bījabhūmi), and the sāmya close the first vimarśa's doctrinal core.

**The crux.** V3-N establishes the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra's foundation: the own-self alone of all
beings is the one mahā-īśvara (kārikā 1); the bound grasper in the own-created this-part (kārikā
2); the own-form-un-cognition-made many person with the enjoyment (kārikā 3); the knowledge-action
of the Lord become the sattva-rajas-tamas of the animal (kārikā 4); the power-ness not declared
from the distinction (kārikā 5); the being-bliss-action of the Lord and the that-absence of the
animal (kārikā 6); the mixed-and-distinct varied-manifesting appearances of the non-conventional
Lord (kārikā 7); and the distinct-manifestation-meanings constructed of the inner-self in the
memory-conjecture range (kārikā 8). All the categories and all the knowers rest in the one free
Lord.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 4.1.1–4.1.8 (the kārikās of this chunk), 1.1.4, 1.3.6, 1.4.8, 1.5.14,
1.5.16, 2.3.7, 3.2.1, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.1.6, 4.1.9; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20; the Spandakārikā 1.7,
1.13; the Śivadṛṣṭi; the Pāṇini-sūtra 1.2.67; the Mālinīvijayottara; the Maṅgalā-śāstra; the
"puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam" and the "pramāṇamekaṃ tadvākyaṃ" and the "na tv evaṃ smaryamāṇatvaṃ
tattattvaṃ pratipadyate" (spa. kā. 1.13) rules; the "sarvabhāvāḥ śivaḥ, sarvabhāvānāmātmā śivaḥ"
(Śivadṛṣṭi). (V3-O continues the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra prathamo vimarśa at source 11600.)
