## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-O)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-O = M00022 lines 11600–12263, the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra tṛtīyo
   vimarśaḥ (the mātṛmeyabandhamokṣatattvavimarśa, the third vimarśa of the category-collection
   section), covering kārikās 9–15: kārikā 9 (*ayamiti hi tasyāsādhāraṇī sṛṣṭirīśasṛṣṭyujīvinī /
   saiṣāpyajñatayā satyaiveśaśaktyā tadātmanaḥ*); kārikā 10 (*svaviśrāntyuparodhāya calayā
   prāṇarūpayā / vikalpakriyayā tattadvarṇavaicitryarūpayā*); kārikā 11 (*sādhāraṇo'nyathā caiśaḥ
   sargaḥ spaṣṭāvabhāsanāt / vikalpahānenaikāgryāt krameṇeśvaratāpadam*); kārikā 12 (*sarvo
   mamāyaṃ vibhava ityevaṃ parijānataḥ / viśvātmano vikalpānāṃ prasare'pi maheśatā*); kārikā 13
   (*meyaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ muktaḥ svātmābhedena manyate / maheśvaro yathā baddhaḥ punaratyantabhedavat*);
   kārikā 14 (*sarvathā tvantarālīnānantatattvaughanirbharaḥ / śivāścidānandaghanaḥ
   paramākṣaravigrahaḥ*); kārikā 15 (*evamātmānametasya samyag jñānakriye tathā / jānan yathepsitān
   paśyañjānāti ca karoti ca*). The chunk ends at the ||3|| colophon (source 12263: the
   tattvārthasaṅgrahādhikāre mātṛmeyabandhamokṣatattvavimarśas tṛtīyaḥ || 3 ||); the caturtho
   vimarśa follows at source 12263. The source is clean, dense Sanskrit throughout.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** vimarśa = reflexive-awareness;
   prakāśa = manifestation; ābhāsa = appearance; kriyāśakti = action-power; māyāśakti = māyā-power;
   pramātṛ/prameya/pramāṇa/pramiti = knower/known/valid-means/cognition; vikalpa = construction;
   avikalpa/nirvikalpa = the un-constructed/non-construction; ekāgratā = the one-pointedness;
   sādhāraṇa/asādhāraṇa = the common/un-common; paśu/pati/īśa = animal/Lord/Īśa; īśvaratā =
   Lord-ness; maheśatā = the mahā-Lord-ness; svātmābheda = the own-self-non-distinction;
   antarālīna = the inner-dissolved; jīvanmukta = the while-living-liberated; svarūpa = the own-form;
   parāmarśa = re-recollection; svaprakāśa = self-manifest; pratyabhijñā = recognition; bandha/mokṣa
   = bond/liberation. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **Kārikā 9 and the paśu's asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi.** The paśu's un-common creation is the
   īśasṛṣṭyupajīvinī (Lord-creation-dependent) vikalpakriyā; it is asādhāraṇī (per-knower, per-time,
   other-knower-state-devoid), sustained on the īśvarasṛṣṭi; the baddhamuktatā hangs on the
   aparijñāna alone. The māyāśakti as the īśvara's viśvaparāmarśavigraha, the vargāṣṭaka, the
   varṇadevatās, and the aṣṭāṣṭakabheda (the Bhartṛhari-āgama concordance) are worked out; the
   svabhāvahetu and the pratyakṣa are validated against the saṃskāradarśana.

4. **Kārikā 10 and the prāṇarūpā vikalpakriyā.** The svaviśrāntyuparodhāya calayā prāṇarūpayā
   vikalpakriyayā: the prāṇāpāna swing that forbids firmness; the "mitram idaṃ śatrur ayam" the
   sūtra-meaning; the kenā prabodhyata (with the īśatva alone); the smṛtiviṣaya vikalpa (own-raised
   vs. established deśakāla); the "cittavṛttibhedamayā svopalabdhā" and the pratikṣaṇa movement; the
   Spa. 3.16, the māyāśakti's tryaṃśā (tucchatābhāsa, vaiparītyābhāsa, nañartha), the nañartha, the
   kārmamala, the parāmaśa-pīḍana, and the varṇānāṃ anantatā (Spa. 1.1, Māyāvaibhava, Sarvavīra).
   The "bandharūpa" and the "sabhittika" svātantrya of the kṣetrajña are reconciled: even in the
   manorājya the sṛṣṭi is parādhīnā.

5. **Kārikā 11 and the sādhāraṇā aiśvarī sṛṣṭi.** The aiśvara sarga (spaṣṭāvabhāsana, avikalpya)
   is sādhāraṇa or asādhāraṇa (the dvicandra), both anyathābhūta from the pāśavī sṛṣṭi; the
   vikalpahāna-krama and the ekāgratā bring the paśu to the īśvaratāpadam (the Vīrāvalī-Bhairava
   113); the parijñātayā īśaśaktyā even the pāśava sarga becomes sādhāraṇa (the nyastamantra
   comparison; the "aiśvara eva sadā sarga" reading over the other vyākhyāntara). The svapna
   (saṅkalpana vs. sparśarasa, the sarvapramātṛsādhāraṇya), the māyīyakṣetrajña's pratiyogin, the
   vikalpalakṣaṇa (1.6.1), the pratyayasṛṣṭi as kārmamalāpyāyikā and the parāmṛtarasa, the
   kṣetrajñatāmasvātantrya (Spa. 3.14), the Bhaṭṭadivākavatsa (dehapratyayadvīpabhaṅga), the
   vikalpanirhrāsa (pā. vā. 3.207, saṃhṛtya sarvataś cintām), the ekāgratā-practice-ladder, the
   tattvārthasaṅgraha's non-repetition, the Vidyākalāśaktis, the ādisiddha-sūtra, the ghaṭādhyavasāya
   (1.5.20), the malatraya and the mokṣa (sattānandasūtra 4.1.6, kaivalya, the bhakta-jana), the
   svaprakāśa, the nirvikalpaka, the nīlādirūpatā and the cittattva, the svabhāvahetu and the
   pratyakṣa (Spa. 1.7, the agnīndhana example, the kāryakāraṇa, the sāhitya, the
   niyatapaurvāparya), the īśvaratā/śivatā gradation and the malasaṃskāra, the aparā/parāparā siddhi,
   the kriyāśakti (bhedaparāmarśa), the pramātrekavapuṣaḥ, the jñānamālā/ātmaśabda Śākya
   comparison, the bha. gī. 13.15 (antikaṃ ca tat), and the "tadevam" nigamana.

6. **Kārikā 12 and the viśvātma.** With the vikalpanirhrāsa and the nirvikalpakasātmībhāva, the
   svapratyaya svaprakāśa is the mokṣa; without it, even in the vikalpānāṃ prasara the viśvātman's
   maheśatā. The "na pratyagātmā kaścid anyo'haṃ" (the grāhyagrāhakaprakāśaghana param-eśvara is
   the aham), the vikalpā api mahāvimarśa-patitā avikalpībhavanti, the Pāradarśana (śaṅkāpi na
   viśaṅkyeta), the Śivadṛṣṭi 1.38 (the sārvabhauma king, pādātadharmāṃs), the prakṛtitvam-prāptān
   vikārān ākaroti, the ṛtudhāmā Āditya (the Bhartṛhari-āgama saṃvāda, the sūṣumnā-nāḍī), the
   pratyāpatti as the māyāpramātuḥ-utthāpita-bhedāvabhāsabhaṅga, and the "maheśvarataiva" (the vṛtti,
   the pratyabhijñā).

7. **Kārikās 13–15 and the meya/mokṣa/śiva.** Kārikā 13: the meya is sādhāraṇa; the mukta thinks
   it with svātmābhedena (like the maheśvara), the baddha with the atyantabhedavat; the
   sādākhyād-ākrimi mātṛvarga as the ahamitirūpa, the ekarasābhedaviśrānti, the Śivadṛṣṭi 5.106/
   7.91/7.93, the grāhyagata-bheda atiśaya, and the tathātvayojana (yathāyogaṃ, not yathākramam).
   Kārikā 14: in the parama-śiva there is no kaścid prameya (the sarvathā, the antarālīna
   anantatattvaugha-nirbhara, the cidānandaghana, the paramākṣaravigraha); the ahaṃpratītir eva
   pūryate, the dūrāpetā bhinnaprameyākāṅkṣā, the dainyayoginī pramātṛtā. Kārikā 15: the
   jñānakriye, the yathepsitān paśyan jānāti karoti; the jīvanmukta, the dehapāte parameśvara; the
   māyāpade'pi citprakāśa (deśakālāspṛṣṭa), the sadāśiveśarūpatā, the "nā khaṇḍayati" (the kācit
   = neti), the manāgapi nīlādyābhāsatva, the Buddhists (kṣaṇika, the virodhacintā, the
   paramāṇusaṅkoca, the "saṃvidastu na yuktaḥ"), the niravabhāsā saṃvid (a. pra. si. 20), the
   ābhāsa-vimarśa stability (śukti-rajata), the bādhaka, the "ātmā aśakyasamayaḥ" (pā. vā. 3.249),
   the ekānekarūpatā, the idantāparāmarśa, the aikādhikaraṇya īśvaratā/śivatā, and the
   paramaśivarūpāntarlīna īśvaratā (Spa. 1.2). The ||3|| colophon closes the third vimarśa.

**The crux.** V3-O completes the mātṛmeyabandhamokṣatattvavimarśa: the paśu's asādhāraṇī
īśasṛṣṭyupajīvinī vikalpakriyā (kārikā 9); the prāṇarūpā, varṇadevatā-beset construction-action
(kārikā 10); the sādhāraṇā aiśvarī sarga and the vikalpahāna-ekāgratā path to īśvaratā (kārikā 11);
the viśvātman's maheśatā even in the vikalpa-prasara (kārikā 12); the meya as sādhāraṇa, known by
the mukta with svātmābhedena (kārikā 13); the antarālīna, cidānandaghana, paramākṣaravigraha śiva
(kārikā 14); and the samyag jñānakriye as the fruit of the whole four-section teaching, with the
jīvanmukta (kārikā 15). The third vimarśa closes with the ||3|| colophon.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 4.1.9–4.1.15 (the kārikās of this chunk), 1.5.20, 1.6.1, 4.1.6; the
Spandakārikā 1.1, 1.2, 1.7, 3.14, 3.15, 3.16; the Vīrāvalī-Bhairava 113; the Pāradarśana; the
Śivadṛṣṭi 1.38, 5.106, 7.91, 7.93; the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20; the Bhagavad-gītā 13.15; the
Pāṇini-vārttika 3.207, 3.249; the Māyāvaibhava-āgama; the Sarvavīra-āgama; the Kālottara; the
Bhartṛhari-āgama concordance; the Bhaṭṭadivākavatsa verse; the ādisiddha-sūtra. (V3-P continues
the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra caturtho vimarśa at source 12263.)

## T1 apparatus — the key decisions (Chunk V3-P)

1. **The chunk's scope.** V3-P = M00022 lines 12263–12539 (to END OF FILE), the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra
   caturtho vimarśaḥ (the samastanigamana, the closing sum), the **final vimarśa of the whole IPVV**.
   Covers: the maṅgala (*prasṛtamanuttararūpādānandādikrameṇa viśvamadaḥ / sarvāmṛtadharamantarbahiśca
   visṛjantamabhivande*); the guruparamparā opening (the gurutaḥ-śāstrataḥ-svataḥ triad, the Kiraṇa,
   the pustakādhītavidyā verse, the kīrtanīyo gurorvargaḥ verse); kārikā 1 (*iti prakaṭito mayā sughaṭa
   eṣa mārgo navo / mahāgurubhirucyate sma śivadṛṣṭiśāstre yathā / tadatra nidadhatpadam
   bhuvanakartṛtāmātmano / vibhāvya śivatāmayīmaniśamāviśansidhyati*); kārikā 2 (*taistairapyupayācitair
   upanatastanvyāḥ sthito'pyantike / kānto lokasamāna evamaparijñāto na rantuṃ yathā / lokasyaiṣa
   tathānavekṣitaguṇaḥ svātmāpi viśveśvaro / naivālaṃ nijavaibhavāya tadiyaṃ tatpratyabhijñoditā*);
   kārikā 3 (*janasyāyatnasiddhyarthamudayākarasūnunā / īśvarapratyabhijñeyamutpalenopapāditā*); the
   vivṛtikāra's 17 ślokas (the author-lineage praise — Bhūtirāja, Lakṣmaṇagupta, the Tryambaka, the
   navatitama-vatsara colophon); the final stuti (16–17); and the two colophons: *samastanigamanaṃ
   caturtho vimarśaḥ || 4 ||* and *samāptā ca iyam īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī* — **the END of the
   whole IPVV**. The source is clean through the end.

2. **The term-ledger LOCK (carried into Vol 3, unchanged).** pratyabhijñā = recognition;
   vimarśa = reflexive-awareness; prakāśa = manifestation; svātantrya = freedom; jñāna/kriyā =
   knowledge/action; guruparamparā = the guru-lineage-order; svataḥ/śāstrataḥ/gurutaḥ = by-itself/from-
   the-śāstra/from-the-guru; mokṣa = liberation; jīvanmukta = the while-living-liberated;
   ahaṃ/idam = I/this; śivatā/īśvaratā = the Śiva-ness/Lord-ness; pramātṛ = the knower; ābhāsa =
   appearance. The older "rehearsal/reflexion/light" variants remain retired.

3. **The guruparamparā (teacher-lineage) frame.** The caturtho vimarśa opens by completing the
   threefold transmission of the teaching (gurutaḥ, śāstrataḥ, svataḥ — from the guru, the śāstra,
   the self), quoting the Kiraṇa and the "pustakādhītavidyā" warning against book-learning without the
   guru-order. The ślokatraya (kīrtanīyo gurorvargaḥ) and the lineage from ādi-Śrīkaṇṭhanātha →
   Durvāsa → Tryambakāditya (the Traiyambaka) are worked out; the samūḍha/ghanasāra glosses, the
   aṣṭādaśabhujā bhrānti, and the citrakarma-upayoga are resolved.

4. **Kārikā 1 and the recognition-path.** The "new, well-fitted path" (navo mārgaḥ) is confirmed by the
   mahāgurus in the Śivadṛṣṭi; the pratyabhijñāmātra-mokṣa, the yama/niyama (kleśayoga) as anupayoga, the
   "sphuṭopāya-anāyāsa" (Spa.-like) verses, the prāṇāyāmādi kṛtrima-yoga with the ṣoḍaśī-kalā, the
   pratyabhijñā/ātmavimarśa-udyo and the jīvanmukta (the dehapātād ekabhaviko mokṣa, "jīvanneva mukta")
   are established; the vikalpahānenaikāgryāt (4.1.11) and sarvo mama (4.1.12) are re-linked; the
   Śivadṛṣṭi-lineage and the śrīkaṇṭhanāthād-guruparvakrama are narrated.

5. **Kārikā 2 and the kāntā/loka analogy.** The lover sought by the slender woman, though standing
   near, is not enjoyed when un-recognized; so the world-Lord own-self, un-observed of quality, is not
   for the own-splendor until the recognition arises. The upayācitāni (deity-prayer/messenger/state-
   declaration), the pratyabhijñānamātra-ānandalābha vs. pariśīlana-saṃbhogasahasra, the
   tattvedantayoḥ ekīkaraṇa = the īśvaratāhantayoḥ, and the āśrayaucitya (dṛṣṭānta/dārṣṭāntika
   ornament vs. aikyam) are worked out.

6. **Kārikā 3 and the utpala-colophon.** The recognition, established by the sun-rise-son (udayākarasūnu
   = Utpala) for the people's effort-less establishment; the jananadharmā-siddhi (not caste/conduct),
   the sarvānugrāhakatva, and the kṛtakṛtyatva (the father's fame-fruit). Then the vivṛtikāra's
   explanation: the susaṃvitti of the īśvaratā; the lāṭa / dvijatva / vāgīśvarī-garbha; the
   antaḥprakṛti (minister-friend); the Karka-śāstra; the Tryambaka (tisro devyaḥ) and the
   dāsya-lakṣmī; the kheṭapālācārya (dvaita-prādhānya); the avidyā (anirvācya); the brahmavāda
   (not ekāntavāda); the "cittamātram idaṃ" (the Buddhist) and the vivaraṇakāra vipratāraṇa; the
   prathāto'khilagrahaṇa (all that is prathamāna = the paramaśiva's prathā), and the
   paryantopāsanīya paramaśiva.

7. **The 17 ślokas and the close.** The vivṛtikāra's vaṃśa (1–15) praises the lineage — Varāha-gupta
   (Cukhulaka, Bhūtirāja's father), Bhūtirāja, Haṭitalakṣmaṇagupta (the śāstra-maker, Abhinava's guru),
   the Tryambaka-śaktitraya, the māṇikyācala/Candrakīrti, the vimarśa-method of the Lord-recognition
   (9), the varṇanikā (10), the vāsanācakravāla (11), the arkameka (12), the ātmāvaraṇa/ātmaprakaṭana
   (14), and the navatitama-vatsara (year 90, Mārgaśīrṣa) colophon (15). The final stuti (16–17: the
   paramaśiva-stuti, "īśvarapratyabhijñā ... vimarśād īśvareṇa ... tmavimarśodyoginīṃ kriyāt") closes the
   work. The ||4|| colophon (samastanigamanaṃ caturtho vimarśaḥ) and the samāptā (the whole IPVV, the
   kṛtiḥ of Abhinavagupta) mark the absolute end of the text.

**The crux.** V3-P is the closing sum of the IPVV: the transmission of the teaching from the guru, the
śāstra and the self (the guruparamparā); the recognition-path as the effort-less, clear means to
jīvanmukti (kārikā 1); the un-recognized world-Lord not enjoyed until recognition (kārikā 2); the
recognition established by Utpala for all (kārikā 3); the vivṛtikāra's lineage-praise (17 ślokas); and
the final stuti and colophons — ending the whole Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī.

**Cross-references:** ĪPK 4.1.9–4.1.11, 4.1.12; the Kiraṇa; the Śivadṛṣṭi (the lineage; the
śivadṛṣṭiśāstra); the Spandakārikā (the sphuṭopāya-anāyāsa verses); the pātañjala-yoga (the yama/niyama,
prāṇāyāma, ṣoḍaśī-kalā); the Vṛtti; the "cittamātram idaṃ traidhātukam" (the Buddhist); the
parātriṃśikā/śaktitraya; the Tryambaka; the Karka-śāstra. **(V3-P is the final chunk — the whole IPVV is
now COMPLETE.)**
